namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions.Atomic{/// <summary> Grants a skill to the player by skill ID. Delegates to <see cref="ICharacterService.AddSkill"/>, which routes through the skills subsystem (SkillsBridge into the skills_base engine mod): the skill is added to the owned set and any action card named by its GrantsAction field lands in the action pool, ready to be assigned to a character. Already owned skills are ignored, making the action safe to replay after loading a save. </summary>
public class CharacterAddSkillAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary> Registered as "character.add_skill" — grants the skill named by the "skill_id" dialog variable. The variable matches the skill's Id in its JSON definition (e.g. "slave_master"). Unknown IDs are rejected downstream with a log warning. </summary>
public string Name=>"character.add_skill";/// <summary> Reads "skill_id" and grants the skill. Returns early with a log message when the variable is missing or empty, so a malformed scenario line cannot half-apply the acquisition. </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var skillId=ctx.GetParam("skill_id");if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(skillId)){ctx.Log("EVENT","CharacterAddSkillAction: missing 'skill_id' variable");return;}ctx.Character.AddSkill(skillId);ctx.Log("EVENT",$"CharacterAddSkillAction: granted skill '{skillId}'");}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions.Atomic{/// <summary> Shows a "character joined" UI notification without actually adding them to the party. Used when the recruitment happens via a different mechanism but the player still needs to see the visual confirmation. </summary>
public class CharacterSendNotificationAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary> Registered as "character.send_notification" — shows a "character joined" UI popup without modifying the party roster. Used when recruitment happens through external means but the player needs visual confirmation, or when re-triggering a notification at a specific story beat. </summary>
public string Name=>"character.send_notification";/// <summary> Reads the "type" variable and triggers the join notification via CharacterData.SendAddNotification. The notification system tracks which characters have already been notified to avoid duplicate popups for the same character. </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var typeRaw=ctx.GetParam("type");if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(typeRaw)){ctx.Log("EVENT","CharacterSendNotificationAction: missing 'type' variable");return;}ctx.Character.SendNotification(typeRaw);ctx.Log("EVENT",$"CharacterSendNotificationAction: sent notification for '{typeRaw}'");}}}

===== FILE Core/Actions/Atomic/SceneInstantiateAction.cs =====
namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions.Atomic;/// <summary> Instantiates a PackedScene into the current scene tree at runtime. The "path" is a Godot resource path (e.g. "res://scenes/SomeObject.tscn"), "name" sets the node's Name property. The instantiated node becomes a child of SceneContextNode.Instance (the current scene root), making it visible immediately. </summary>
public class SceneInstantiateAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary> Registered as "scene.instantiate" — loads a PackedScene from a Godot resource path and inserts it into the current scene tree at runtime. The "path" variable is a Godot resource path (e.g. "res://scenes/SomeObject.tscn"), "name" sets the node's Name property. The node becomes a child of SceneContextNode.Instance and is visible immediately. Both variables are required. </summary>
public string Name=>"scene.instantiate";/// <summary> Reads "path" and "name" from dialog variables and delegates to ctx.Scene.Instantiate. Uses GD.Load&lt;PackedScene&gt; internally — if the resource fails to load (wrong path), an error is logged but the dialog continues. Returns early with a warning if either variable is missing. </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var path=ctx.GetParam("path");var name=ctx.GetParam("name");if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(path)||string.IsNullOrEmpty(name)){ctx.Log("EVENT","SceneInstantiateAction: missing 'path' or 'name' variable");return;}ctx.Scene.Instantiate(path,name);ctx.Log("SCENE",$"SceneInstantiateAction: instantiated '{path}' as '{name}'");}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions.Atomic;/// <summary> Removes a named child from the scene tree. Before RemoveChild+QueueFree, it calls SceneContextNode.RemoveEventObject to notify the event system that the object is being destroyed — this prevents stale references in the event chain. The "name" must match the node's Name property exactly. </summary>
public class SceneRemoveObjectAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary> Registered as "scene.remove_object" — removes a named child node from the scene tree. Before freeing the node, it notifies the event system via SceneContextNode.RemoveEventObject to clean up subscriptions. The "name" variable must match the node's Name property exactly — partial matches won't work. </summary>
public string Name=>"scene.remove_object";/// <summary> Reads the "name" variable and delegates to ctx.Scene.Remove. Safe to call on non-existent nodes — the implementation silently returns if the named child is not found. Returns early with a warning if "name" is missing. </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var name=ctx.GetParam("name");if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(name)){ctx.Log("EVENT","SceneRemoveObjectAction: missing 'name' variable");return;}ctx.Scene.Remove(name);ctx.Log("SCENE",$"SceneRemoveObjectAction: removed '{name}'");}}

===== FILE Core/Actions/Atomic/TogglePanelAction.cs =====
using Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap;using Cthangover.Core.UI;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions.Atomic;/// <summary> Toggles the visibility of any Control node in the scene by name. Uses ctx.Scene.Find for recursive tree search — panels can be nested arbitrarily deep. When the name is not found in the scene, the action falls back to <see cref="UiRegistry.Toggle"/> so host-built panels (e.g. the world map, live under UiHost's CanvasLayer rather than the scene tree) can be opened from scenarios. Unlike Show/Hide methods that use Widget lifecycle, scene controls are toggled through Godot's native Visible property directly, so this works on non-Widget controls as well. </summary>
public class TogglePanelAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary> Registered as "ui.toggle_panel" — toggles the visibility of any Control-derived node in the scene by name; if no scene node matches, the name is treated as a mod UI entry id and toggled through the UI registry. The toggle is unconditional — if neither exists, it logs a warning rather than creating anything. </summary>
public string Name=>"ui.toggle_panel";/// <summary> Reads the "name" variable, locates the Control node via recursive scene tree search, and flips its Visible property. Falls back to UiRegistry.Toggle(id) for hosted panels. Logs both the toggle result (new visibility state) and the not-found case. Returns early with a warning if "name" is missing. </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var name=ctx.GetParam("name");if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(name)){ctx.Log("EVENT","TogglePanelAction: missing 'name' variable");return;}var panel=ctx.Scene.Find<Control>(name);if(panel!=null){panel.Visible= !panel.Visible;ctx.Log("WIDGET",$"TogglePanelAction: toggled '{name}' visibility to {panel.Visible}");return;}if(AppServices.Current.Ui.GetById(name)!=null){AppServices.Current.Ui.ToggleEntry(name);ctx.Log("WIDGET",$"TogglePanelAction: toggled hosted panel '{name}'");return;}ctx.Log("EVENT",$"TogglePanelAction: panel '{name}' not found");}}

using Cthangover.Core.Settings;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions{/// <summary> Delegates character operations to GameData.Instance.Runtime.CharacterData. The type string is a character ID — it is passed directly to CharacterData without parsing. Malformed or missing IDs are handled inside CharacterData (null-character fallback for unknown IDs). </summary>
public class CharacterServiceImpl:ICharacterService{/// <summary> Passes the type string directly to CharacterData.AddCharacterToParty. The character ID is resolved through CharacterFactory; an unknown ID is refused (error log, party unchanged) so a typo in scenario content cannot add a broken party member. A valid character is added to the runtime party and persists through the save system. </summary>
public void AddToParty(string type){var characterData=GameData.Instance.Runtime.CharacterData;characterData.AddCharacterToParty(type);}/// <summary> Passes the type string directly to CharacterData.SendAddNotification. Unlike AddToParty, this only triggers the UI popup without modifying the party roster. Useful when a character was recruited earlier (or externally) but the notification needs to appear at a specific story beat. </summary>
public void SendNotification(string type){var characterData=GameData.Instance.Runtime.CharacterData;characterData.SendAddNotification(type);}/// <summary> Passes the skill ID to the skills subsystem through <see cref="SkillsBridge"/>. The grant implementation owns both halves of an acquisition — the skill entry and the action card it may grant — and rejects unknown skill IDs with a warning, so a typo in a scenario cannot corrupt the runtime state. </summary>
public void AddSkill(string id){SkillsBridge.Grant(id);}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Events;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions;/// <summary> GDScript-facing action context passed to <c>run(ctx)</c> of GDScript scenario actions (see <see cref="GDScriptScenarioAction"/>). Mirrors the <see cref="IActionContext"/> surface with snake-callable wrappers: subsystem services (<see cref="Quests"/>, <see cref="Character"/>, <see cref="Lighting"/>, <see cref="Scene"/>, <see cref="Inventory"/>, <see cref="ModRegistry"/>), parameter access (<see cref="GetParam"/>), logging, and event publishing. The backing C# context is attached just before the call via <see cref="GDActionContextCore.Inner"/>, so a GDScript action sees exactly the state a C# action would. </summary>
[GlobalClass]public partial class GDActionContext:RefCounted{internal GDActionContextCore Core=new();/// <summary>Quest subsystem: status, tags, and UI notifications.</summary>
public GDQuestService Quests=>Core.Quests;/// <summary>Character subsystem: party recruitment and join notifications.</summary>
public GDCharacterService Character=>Core.Character;/// <summary>Lighting subsystem: depth/albedo maps and time-of-day lighting.</summary>
public GDLightingService Lighting=>Core.Lighting;/// <summary>Scene node subsystem: instantiate, remove, and find nodes.</summary>
public GDSceneNodeService Scene=>Core.Scene;/// <summary>Player inventory subsystem.</summary>
public Items.GDInventoryService Inventory=>Core.Inventory;/// <summary>Mod registry: query loaded mods and their metadata.</summary>
public Mods.GDModRegistryService ModRegistry=>Core.ModRegistry;/// <summary>Reads a named dialog variable (GDScript: <c>ctx.GetParam("quest_id")</c>). Returns null when unset.</summary>
public string GetParam(string name)=>Core.GetParam(name);/// <summary>Emits a log entry to the central game log under the given category.</summary>
public void Log(string category,string message)=>Core.Log(category,message);/// <summary>Emits a warning-level log entry (prefixed with "[WARN]").</summary>
public void LogWarning(string category,string message)=>Core.LogWarning(category,message);/// <summary> GDScript: ctx.PublishEvent("cooking_meal_ready", {"dish": "wolf_stew"}) Publishes an event to the global bus for inter-mod communication. </summary>
public void PublishEvent(string eventKey,Godot.Collections.Dictionary data){ModEventBus.Instance?.Publish(eventKey,data);}}

===== FILE Core/Actions/GDActionContextCore.cs =====
namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions;/// <summary> Shared backing state for the GDScript-facing context wrappers. Holds the six GD service singletons and the C# <see cref="IActionContext"/> they delegate to. Assigning <see cref="Inner"/> fans the context out to every service at once, so <see cref="GDScriptScenarioAction"/> can bind a freshly created <see cref="GDActionContext"/> to the running dialog context with a single property set. All members are null-safe: before binding, calls silently no-op instead of throwing inside GDScript. </summary>
public class GDActionContextCore{/// <summary> The live C# context of the running scenario action. Setting it propagates the underlying services into every GD wrapper field. Null while the context is not bound to a running action. </summary>
public IActionContext Inner{get=>_inner;set{_inner=value;Quests.Inner=value?.Quests;Character.Inner=value?.Character;Lighting.Inner=value?.Lighting;Scene.Inner=value?.Scene;Inventory.Inner=value?.Inventory;ModRegistry.Inner=value?.ModRegistry;}}/// <summary>Delegates to the bound context; returns null before binding.</summary>
public string GetParam(string name)=>_inner?.GetParam(name);/// <summary>Delegates to the bound context; no-op before binding.</summary>
public void Log(string category,string message)=>_inner?.Log(category,message);/// <summary>Delegates to the bound context; no-op before binding.</summary>
public void LogWarning(string category,string message)=>_inner?.LogWarning(category,message);/// <summary>Quest subsystem wrapper bound by <see cref="Inner"/>.</summary>
public readonly GDQuestService Quests=new();/// <summary>Character subsystem wrapper bound by <see cref="Inner"/>.</summary>
public readonly GDCharacterService Character=new();/// <summary>Lighting subsystem wrapper bound by <see cref="Inner"/>.</summary>
public readonly GDLightingService Lighting=new();/// <summary>Scene node subsystem wrapper bound by <see cref="Inner"/>.</summary>
public readonly GDSceneNodeService Scene=new();/// <summary>Inventory subsystem wrapper bound by <see cref="Inner"/>.</summary>
public readonly Items.GDInventoryService Inventory=new();/// <summary>Mod registry wrapper bound by <see cref="Inner"/>.</summary>
public readonly Mods.GDModRegistryService ModRegistry=new();private IActionContext _inner;}

===== FILE Core/Actions/GDScriptScenarioAction.cs =====
using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions;/// <summary> Adapter that exposes a GDScript object with <c>get_name()</c> + <c>run(ctx)</c> as a regular <see cref="IScenarioAction"/>. Created by <c>ModGDScriptLoader</c> for every matching <c>.gd</c> file and registered in <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls.ScenarioActionFactory"/> like any C# action, so the DSL <c>action</c> command cannot tell the two apart. </summary>
public class GDScriptScenarioAction:IScenarioAction{private readonly GodotObject _instance;/// <summary> Wraps a compiled GDScript instance. </summary> <param name="name">Action name returned by the script's <c>get_name()</c>; becomes the DSL registry key.</param> <param name="instance">Live GodotObject backing the GDScript; <c>run(ctx)</c> is invoked on it.</param>
public GDScriptScenarioAction(string name,GodotObject instance){Name=name;_instance=instance;}/// <summary>DSL action name from the script's <c>get_name()</c> (e.g. "cooking.meal_cooked").</summary>
public string Name{get;}/// <summary> Invokes the script's <c>run(ctx)</c> with a <see cref="GDActionContext"/> bound to the C# context, giving the script access to dialog variables and all subsystem services. </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var gdCtx=new GDActionContext();gdCtx.Core.Inner=ctx;_instance.Call("run",gdCtx);}}

===== FILE Core/Actions/IActionContext.cs =====
using Cthangover.Core.Items;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions;/// <summary> Context passed to IScenarioAction.Run — provides dialog variable access (GetParam) and references to all subsystem service interfaces. Acts as a facade: a single object that grants the action access to quests, characters, lighting, scene nodes, mod registry, and inventory, plus logging. GetParam reads from the DialogRuntime's variable store, so actions can consume values set by the scenario DSL's "set" command or by earlier actions. </summary>
public interface IActionContext{/// <summary> Quest subsystem: full CRUD over quest state, status, tags, and UI notifications. Backed by QuestServiceImpl which uses QuestFactory for lookup and TryGet for safe fallback on missing quests. </summary>
IQuestService Quests{get;}/// <summary> Character subsystem: add characters to the player's party and dispatch "character joined" UI notifications. Accepts character ID strings from scenario parameters. </summary>
ICharacterService Character{get;}/// <summary> Lighting subsystem: controls depth/albedo texture maps on the UiLightController singleton and toggles time-of-day lighting. Used for scene transitions with different lighting setups. </summary>
ILightingService Lighting{get;}/// <summary> Scene node subsystem: runtime instantiation, removal, and typed lookup of nodes within the current scene tree. All operations go through SceneContextNode.Instance as the scene root. </summary>
ISceneNodeService Scene{get;}/// <summary> Mod registry reference: allows scenario actions to query loaded mods, their metadata, and custom action registrations at runtime. Singleton instance shared across all contexts. </summary>
IModRegistry ModRegistry{get;}/// <summary> Player inventory reference, obtained from GameData at context construction time. May be null if game data hasn't fully loaded yet — consumers must tolerate a null inventory. </summary>
IInventory Inventory{get;}/// <summary> World map subsystem: open/close zones for travel and show/hide them on the map. Backed by <c>MapZoneServiceImpl</c> over the process-wide <c>MapZoneService</c> singleton; state changes are persisted by the core save slot and invalidate scenario conditions through <c>ConditionStateMonitor</c>. </summary>
IMapZoneService Map{get;}/// <summary> Reads a named variable from the dialog runtime's variable store. Variables are populated by the scenario DSL's "set" command or by earlier actions during dialog execution. Returns null when the variable doesn't exist — callers must null-check. This is the sole data channel between scenario actions and the dialog system. </summary>
string GetParam(string name);/// <summary> Emits a debug-level entry to the central game log. The category string groups related entries (convention: "EVENT", "QUEST", "BATTLE", "SCENE", "WIDGET"). Consistent categories enable log filtering during debugging of scenario scripts. </summary>
void Log(string category,string message);/// <summary> Emits a warning-level entry to the central game log. The message is prefixed with "[WARN]" and logged at LogLevel.Warning. Use for non-fatal issues that scenario authors should investigate (missing variables, unregistered quests, etc.) without halting dialog execution. </summary>
void LogWarning(string category,string message);}

===== FILE Core/Actions/ILightingService.cs =====
namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions;/// <summary> Lighting control contract for scenario actions. ClearDepthMap resets the depth/albedo textures on the UiLightController singleton, effectively removing scene-specific lighting masks. SetUseTime toggles time-of-day lighting on/off. </summary>
public interface ILightingService{/// <summary> Resets both the depth texture and albedo texture on the UiLightController singleton to null. This disables scene-specific lighting masks, reverting the shader to default flat lighting. Both maps are cleared together because partial clearing would leave the lighting shader in an inconsistent state. Used during scene transitions — call before entering a scene that doesn't use depth-based lighting, or when switching between scenes with different lighting setups. </summary>
void ClearDepthMap();/// <summary> Enables or disables time-of-day lighting on the UiLightController. When enabled, the controller adjusts scene lighting based on the in-game time; when disabled, lighting remains static. Use this when entering interior scenes (disable) or exterior scenes (enable) to match the environmental context. </summary>
void SetUseTime(bool useTime);}

using Cthangover.Core.Quests;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions;/// <summary> Quest manipulation contract for scenario actions. Provides full CRUD over quest state: Get by ID, status change (parsed via Enums&lt;QuestStatus&gt;), data-level status tracking, tag management, and UI notification dispatch. Separates quest.Status (global state like Active/Completed) from quest.Data.Status (incremental progress within the quest). </summary>
public interface IQuestService{/// <summary> Retrieves a quest by its string ID from QuestFactory. Throws KeyNotFoundException if the quest doesn't exist — prefer Exists() or the safe TryGet() pattern in the implementation when the quest may legitimately be absent. </summary>
IQuest Get(string id);/// <summary> Checks whether a quest with the given ID is registered in QuestFactory. Returns false on any exception (missing data, corrupted save), treating "can't read" as "doesn't exist" to prevent scenario scripts from crashing. </summary>
bool Exists(string id);/// <summary> Sets the global lifecycle state of a quest (Active, Completed, Failed, etc.). The status string is parsed via Enums&lt;QuestStatus&gt;.Parse — case-sensitive. Invalid status strings are caught and logged as errors without throwing. </summary>
void SetStatus(string id,string status);/// <summary> Sets the numeric progress level within a quest's Data.Status field. This is incremental progress (e.g. "2/5 wolves killed"), separate from the global quest state managed by SetStatus(). The quest's data object tracks the level for display and completion checks. </summary>
void SetDataStatus(string id,int level);/// <summary> Attaches a string tag to a quest for use in conditional logic. Tags are stored in the quest's save data and queried by scenario scripts via the "has_tag" condition to branch dialog or gate quest progression. Adding a tag that already exists is a no-op. </summary>
void AddTag(string id,string tag);/// <summary> Removes a string tag from a quest. Used to clear temporary conditions — for example, removing a "witnessed_event" tag after the event has been addressed. Removing a non-existent tag is a no-op. </summary>
void RemoveTag(string id,string tag);/// <summary> Triggers a UI notification for the quest (e.g. "Quest Updated" or "New Quest" popup). This is the visual feedback companion to state changes — call after SetStatus/SetDataStatus for the player to see the update. The notification itself does not change quest state. </summary>
void SendNotification(string id);}

===== FILE Core/Actions/IScenarioAction.cs =====
namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions;/// <summary> Contract for atomic scenario actions — named commands that the scenario DSL dispatches at runtime via ScenarioActionFactory. Each action has a unique Name (e.g. "quest.set_status", "battle.init") used as the registry key. Actions receive an IActionContext giving access to dialog variables and core subsystem services (quests, characters, lighting, scene, inventory); gameplay subsystems implemented in mods can receive extra data through dialog variables instead of new context services. Implementations are discovered via reflection and require no manual registration — the factory scans all assemblies for IScenarioAction types. </summary>
public interface IScenarioAction{/// <summary> Unique action identifier used as the registry key in ScenarioActionFactory. Follows the "subsystem.verb" convention (e.g. "quest.set_status", "battle.init", "scene.instantiate"). This is the name that scenario DSL scripts use after the "action" keyword. Must be unique across all registered actions — if a mod registers an action with a duplicate name, it is silently ignored (earliest registration wins). </summary>
string Name{get;}/// <summary> Executes the action using the provided context. The context provides access to dialog variables (via GetParam) and all subsystem services. Run() is called synchronously by the dialog engine when it encounters the corresponding action command in a scenario script — the dialog pauses until Run() returns, so actions must not block indefinitely. </summary>

public interface ISceneNodeService{/// <summary> Loads a PackedScene from the given resource path via GD.Load&lt;PackedScene&gt;, instantiates it, assigns the given node name, and attaches it as a child of SceneContextNode.Instance (the current scene's autoload root). using System;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions{/// <summary> Core-side bridge for the scene lighting stack. The implementation (locating the scene's lighting controller and pushing maps to it) lives in the time_base engine mod; the kernel — SceneManager's scene-switch reset and background updates — only knows these delegate slots. The mod installs its hooks through <see cref="Register"/> when the mod pipeline reaches <c>IModInitializer.OnModResourcesReady</c>. Registration is first-wins: reloading the mod re-runs its static initializers, and a second hook pair must never stack on top of the first. While no hooks are bound (kernel built without the time mod, or calls before mods load) invocations are skipped with a warning instead of throwing, so a scene switch cannot crash the runtime. </summary>
public static class LightingBridge{private static readonly object Gate=new();private static Action _clearSceneLights;private static Action<Texture2D,Texture2D>_setupBackgroundMaps;/// <summary>Installs the lighting hooks; first registration wins, re-registrations are logged and ignored.</summary>
public static void Register(Action clearSceneLights,Action<Texture2D,Texture2D>setupBackgroundMaps){if(clearSceneLights==null||setupBackgroundMaps==null)return;lock(Gate){if(_clearSceneLights!=null){GameLogger.Log("LIGHT","LightingBridge: lighting hooks already registered; ignoring re-registration",LogLevel.Warning);return;}_clearSceneLights=clearSceneLights;_setupBackgroundMaps=setupBackgroundMaps;}}/// <summary> Resets static lights and both lighting maps for the outgoing scene. Skipped with a warning when no time_base implementation is bound. </summary>
public static void ClearSceneLights(){Action hook;lock(Gate)hook=_clearSceneLights;if(hook==null){GameLogger.Log("LIGHT","LightingBridge: no lighting hooks bound (time_base not loaded); scene light reset skipped",LogLevel.Warning);return;}hook();}/// <summary> Pushes background depth/albedo textures onto the lighting controller. Skipped with a warning when no time_base implementation is bound. </summary>
public static void SetupBackgroundMaps(Texture2D depth,Texture2D albedo){Action<Texture2D,Texture2D>hook;lock(Gate)hook=_setupBackgroundMaps;if(hook==null){GameLogger.Log("LIGHT","LightingBridge: no lighting hooks bound (time_base not loaded); background maps update skipped",LogLevel.Warning);return;}hook(depth,albedo);}}}

using System;using Cthangover.Core.UI.Tool;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions{/// <summary> Core-side bridge for the world map zone state. The state owner (the zone list plus runtime open/visible overrides) lives in the map_base engine mod; the kernel only touches it through these delegate slots — <c>RuntimeSerializer</c> persists the overrides into the <c>__core__</c> save slot and <c>AppServices</c> resets them when a new game starts. The mod installs its hooks through <see cref="Register"/> when the mod pipeline reaches <c>IModInitializer.OnModResourcesReady</c>. Registration is first-wins: reloading the mod re-runs its static initializers, and a second hook set must never stack on top of the first. While no hooks are bound (kernel built without the map mod, or calls before mods load) exports yield an empty delta — a save without a map mod stays loadable — and imports/resets are skipped with a warning instead of throwing, mirroring <see cref="SkillsBridge"/>. </summary>

public static MapZoneStateData ExportState(){Func<MapZoneStateData>hook;lock(Gate)hook=_exportState;if(hook==null){GameLogger.Log("MAP","MapStateBridge: no zone-state hooks bound (map_base not loaded); exporting empty map state",LogLevel.Warning);return new MapZoneStateData();}return hook();}/// <summary>Replaces the overrides with the values from a loaded save; skipped with a warning when no map mod is bound.</summary>
public static void ImportState(MapZoneStateData data){Action<MapZoneStateData>hook;lock(Gate)hook=_importState;if(hook==null){GameLogger.Log("MAP","MapStateBridge: no zone-state hooks bound (map_base not loaded); map state restore skipped",LogLevel.Warning);return;}hook(data);}/// <summary>Forgets every override when a new game starts; skipped with a warning when no map mod is bound.</summary>
public static void ResetOverrides(){Action hook;lock(Gate)hook=_resetOverrides;if(hook==null){GameLogger.Log("MAP","MapStateBridge: no zone-state hooks bound (map_base not loaded); map reset skipped",LogLevel.Warning);return;}hook();}}}

===== FILE Core/Actions/SceneNodeServiceImpl.cs =====
using Cthangover.Core.Scenes;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions{/// <summary> Scene node operations implementation. Instantiate loads a PackedScene by path and attaches it to SceneContextNode.Instance — the current scene's autoload root. Remove delegates to SceneContextNode.RemoveEventObject before the raw RemoveChild+QueueFree, suggesting the event system tracks instantiated objects and needs cleanup notification. Find uses SceneContextNode.FindNode for typed recursive lookup across the scene tree. </summary>
public class SceneNodeServiceImpl:ISceneNodeService{/// <summary> Loads a PackedScene by resource path via GD.Load, instantiates it, assigns the node name, and adds it as a child of SceneContextNode.Instance (the current scene's autoload root). If the resource fails to load (wrong path, missing file), logs an error and returns without throwing — the dialog continues. The instantiated node becomes visible immediately. </summary>
public void Instantiate(string scenePath,string nodeName){var packedScene=GD.Load<PackedScene>(scenePath);if(packedScene==null){GameLogger.Log("SCENE",$"SceneNodeService: failed to load '{scenePath}'",LogLevel.Error);return;}var instance=packedScene.Instantiate();instance.Name=nodeName;SceneContextNode.Instance?.AddChild(instance);}/// <summary> Removes a named child node from SceneContextNode.Instance. First notifies the event system via RemoveEventObject to clean up any event subscriptions referencing the node, then performs RemoveChild + QueueFree. Safe to call on non-existent nodes (silently returns if the context or child is null). </summary>
public void Remove(string nodeName){var ctx=SceneContextNode.Instance;if(ctx==null)return;ctx.RemoveEventObject(nodeName);var child=ctx.FindChild(nodeName,false,false);if(child!=null){ctx.RemoveChild(child);child.QueueFree();}}/// <summary> Typed recursive lookup by node name across the entire scene tree via SceneContextNode.FindNode. Returns null if no matching node of type T with the given name exists. Used by TogglePanelAction to locate UI controls at any nesting depth. </summary>
public T Find<T>(string nodeName)where T:Node{return SceneContextNode.FindNode<T>(nodeName);}}}

using System;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Actions{/// <summary> Core-side bridge for skill grants. The grant logic itself (resolving the definition and pairing the skill with its granted action card) lives in the skills_base engine mod; the kernel only knows this delegate slot. The mod installs its implementation through <see cref="Register"/> when the mod pipeline reaches <c>IModInitializer.OnModResourcesReady</c>. Registration is first-wins: reloading the mod re-runs its static initializers, and a second delegate must never stack on top of the first. While no sink is bound (kernel built without the skills mod, or the call happens before mods load) grants are rejected with a warning instead of throwing, so a scenario cannot crash the runtime. </summary>
public static class SkillsBridge{private static readonly object Gate=new();private static Func<string,bool>_grantSkill;/// <summary>Installs the grant implementation; first registration wins, re-registrations are logged and ignored.</summary>
public static void Register(Func<string,bool>grantSkill){if(grantSkill==null)return;lock(Gate){if(_grantSkill!=null){GameLogger.Log("SKILL","SkillsBridge: grant sink already registered; ignoring re-registration",LogLevel.Warning);return;}_grantSkill=grantSkill;}}/// <summary> Grants a skill through the bound sink. Returns <c>false</c> when no skills mod is loaded (with a warning) or when the sink rejects the ID — mirroring the old direct <c>SkillService.GrantSkill</c> result. </summary>
public static bool Grant(string id){Func<string,bool>sink;lock(Gate)sink=_grantSkill;if(sink==null){GameLogger.Log("SKILL",$"SkillsBridge: no grant sink bound (skills_base not loaded); skill '{id}' rejected",LogLevel.Warning);return false;}return sink(id);}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Audio{/// <summary> Contract for the central audio service. Separates per-bus playback (music, ambient, SFX) and volume/enabled control. The PlaySound overload with <c>variations</c> picks a random suffix from 1..N, enabling sound variation without explicit variant IDs in callers. </summary>
public interface IAudioService{/// <summary> Loads a music track by asset <paramref name="id"/> through the audio engine mod's music factory and assigns it to the dedicated Music <c>AudioStreamPlayer</c>. The <paramref name="musicType"/> tag is informational — it does not change playback routing; the caller is responsible for using the correct type so that auto-advance logic in the audio engine mod's music player picks the right playlist bucket on track end. </summary>
void PlayMusic(string id,MusicType musicType);/// <summary> Immediately stops the dedicated music player. Any saved playback position in <c>PlaylistContext</c> is preserved, allowing a later <c>PlayMusic</c> or auto-advance to pick a fresh track or resume the saved one. </summary>
void StopMusic();/// <summary> Pauses or resumes the music stream in-place via <c>StreamPaused</c>. The current track is not evicted, so a subsequent <c>PauseMusic(false)</c> continues from the exact sample where audio was suspended. </summary>
void PauseMusic(bool pause);/// <summary> Plays a single sound effect identified by <paramref name="id"/> through the per-<see cref="SoundType"/> player pool. If a sound of the same <paramref name="soundType"/> is already playing it is cut off, while sounds of different types stack independently. </summary>
void PlaySound(string id,SoundType soundType);/// <summary> Plays a sound effect with random variation. When <paramref name="variations"/> is greater than 1, a suffix <c>"_N"</c> (1..variations) is appended to <paramref name="id"/> so the caller can provide a base name like <c>"footstep"</c> and get <c>"footstep_3"</c> at runtime without enumerating variants manually. </summary>
void PlaySound(string id,int variations,SoundType soundType);/// <summary> Stops the player associated with the given <paramref name="type"/> pool. Other <see cref="SoundType"/> players are unaffected. </summary>
void StopSound(SoundType type);/// <summary> Pauses the per-type sound player. Only the specified <paramref name="type"/> is affected; other pools keep playing. Use <c>PlaySound</c> to restart — the stream resumes from where it was paused because <c>Play()</c> on an already-loaded <c>AudioStreamPlayer</c> continues from the paused position. </summary>
void PauseSound(SoundType type);/// <summary> Starts or restarts an ambient loop on the dedicated Ambient bus. If the same ambient stream is already playing the call is silently ignored, preventing an audible reset glitch. On track end the player automatically re-plays the stream. </summary>
void PlayAmbient(string id);/// <summary> Stops the ambient loop. Unlike the music bus there is no auto-advance or saved state — calling <c>PlayAmbient</c> again starts the stream from the beginning. </summary>
void StopAmbient();/// <summary> Sets the linear volume (0–1) for the audio bus identified by <paramref name="type"/>. The value is converted to dB via <c>LinearToDb</c> before being pushed to <c>AudioServer.SetBusVolumeDb</c>. Changes are immediate and independent across the three buses. </summary>
void SetVolume(MixerType type,float volume);/// <summary> Mutes the bus by forcing its volume to -80 dB when <paramref name="enabled"/> is <c>false</c>. When <paramref name="enabled"/> is <c>true</c> the method is a no-op — normal volume is restored by a subsequent <c>SetVolume</c> or settings poll. </summary>
void SetEnabled(MixerType type,bool enabled);}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Factories;using Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;using Cthangover.Core.Mods.Resolvers;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnBuild;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing;using Cthangover.Core.Settings;using Cthangover.Core.UI;using Cthangover.Core.UI.Menu;using Cthangover.Core.UI.Tool;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap{/// <summary> Composition root of the game. Owns every service, registry and factory the core creates, in one place, with explicit construction order. Lifecycle: Boot creates a fresh instance at the start of every boot and publishes it through SetCurrent. Outside the running game (xUnit tests, design-time tooling) Current materializes a default instance on first touch, so facades keep working without a boot; construction of individual services stays lazy (each slot below is a Lazy of T) and is therefore timing-preserving. The default instance is throwaway: boot replaces it, so early read-only access is safe, but anything registered on it (resettables) would be discarded — runtime code registers only after the boot pipeline has begun (mod initializers run inside it). Two data-driven loops live here: - Registries: IGameRegistry.Rebuild/Clear replace hand-maintained lists in ModManager.Reload; - Resettables: ResetForNewGame replaces scattered per-owner reset calls and NewGameStartedEvent subscriptions; mods register extra owners via RegisterResettable from an IModInitializer. Migration note: factory static facades (BackgroundFactory.Instance and friends) delegate into the matching slot here. The facades stay as the public API until all consumers are migrated to explicit injection. A few process-wide singletons are still owned outside this class — ModRegistry/ModManager (mod pipeline) and MapZoneService (reset through the lambda resettables below) — migrating them is a documented follow-up. Quest state moved to the quests_base engine mod, whose initializer registers its own resettable with the same "quests" id through <see cref="RegisterResettable"/>. </summary>
public sealed class AppServices{private static AppServices current;private static readonly object CurrentLock=new();/// <summary> The active service set. In a running game this is the instance the boot pipeline published; in tests and tools it is a lazily created default. Never null after the first touch. </summary>
public static AppServices Current{get{var snapshot=current;if(snapshot!=null)return snapshot;return CreateDefault();}}/// <summary> Publishes the boot-created service set. Called once per process by Boot before any phase runs; replaces a default instance if tests happened to materialize one earlier. </summary>
public static void SetCurrent(AppServices instance){if(instance==null)throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(instance));lock(CurrentLock)current=instance;}private static AppServices CreateDefault(){lock(CurrentLock){if(current==null)current=new AppServices();return current;}}/// <summary>Mod-derived registries, cleared and rebuilt as a set.</summary>
public IReadOnlyList<IGameRegistry>Registries{get;}/// <summary>Typed accessors for the registries the static facades delegate to.</summary>
public ModConflictRegistry Conflicts{get;}/// <summary>Mod-declared GUI entries (panels and overlays); <see cref="UiBuilder"/> reads it to build the toolbar.</summary>
public UiRegistry Ui{get;}/// <summary>Menu items (buttons with their bindings) and reusable panels, from mod manifests and runtime registration.</summary>
public MenuRegistry Menus{get;}/// <summary>Executable scene events discovered via attributes or registered by mods at runtime.</summary>
public SceneEventRegistry SceneEvents{get;}/// <summary>Logical scene names mapped to .tscn paths, registered by mod initializers.</summary>
public SceneRouteRegistry SceneRoutes{get;}/// <summary>Scene definitions collected from mod manifests, with an instance-level cache.</summary>
public SceneDefinitions SceneDefs{get;}/// <summary>.tscn external-resource builders, indexed by resource type.</summary>
public ExtResourceBuilderRegistry ExtResourceBuilders{get;}/// <summary>Ordered node property resolvers for .tscn building; first match wins.</summary>
public PropertyResolverRegistry PropertyResolvers{get;}/// <summary>.tscn sub-resource builders, indexed by resource type.</summary>
public SubResourceBuilderRegistry SubResourceBuilders{get;}/// <summary>.tscn text section parsers, indexed by section type.</summary>
public SectionParserRegistry SectionParsers{get;}private readonly List<IResettable>resettables=new();private readonly object resettablesLock=new();/// <summary>Owners of playthrough state, reset together on a new game.</summary>
public IReadOnlyList<IResettable>Resettables=>resettables;/// <summary> Constructs the service set. Registries are created immediately because they are cheap and side-effect free by contract; core resettables (map zones) are registered here with lambda-deferred construction so the first reset keeps the pre-migration touch order; mod-owned subsystems (quests) register theirs from initializers. Factory slots stay lazy (see the slot list below). </summary>
public AppServices(){// Registry instances are cheap and side-effect free by contract; Rebuild fills them from the loaded mod set.
Conflicts=new ModConflictRegistry();Ui=new UiRegistry();Menus=new MenuRegistry();SceneEvents=new SceneEventRegistry();SceneRoutes=new SceneRouteRegistry();SceneDefs=new SceneDefinitions();ExtResourceBuilders=new ExtResourceBuilderRegistry();PropertyResolvers=new PropertyResolverRegistry();SubResourceBuilders=new SubResourceBuilderRegistry();SectionParsers=new SectionParserRegistry();Registries=new IGameRegistry[]{Conflicts,Ui,Menus,SceneEvents,SceneRoutes,SceneDefs,ExtResourceBuilders,PropertyResolvers,SubResourceBuilders,SectionParsers,};// Core state owners. Lambdas keep construction deferred until the first real reset, exactly like the pre-migration touch order. Quest state is owned by the quests_base mod and registers its own "quests" resettable from QuestsModInitializer.OnModResourcesReady.
RegisterResettable(new LambdaResettable("map_zones",()=>Cthangover.Core.Actions.MapStateBridge.ResetOverrides()));}/// <summary> Registers an additional new-game state owner (mods register theirs from an IModInitializer, i.e. after the boot pipeline has begun). Registering on Current before SetCurrent would target the throwaway default instance and be lost. Duplicates by IResettable.Id are ignored. </summary>
public void RegisterResettable(IResettable resettable){if(resettable==null)return;lock(resettablesLock){foreach(var existing in resettables){if(string.Equals(existing.Id,resettable.Id,StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))return;}resettables.Add(resettable);}}/// <summary>Resets every registered state owner, in registration order.</summary>
public void ResetForNewGame(){IResettable[]snapshot;lock(resettablesLock)snapshot=resettables.ToArray();foreach(var resettable in snapshot){try{resettable.ResetForNewGame();GameLogger.Log("BOOT","reset: "+resettable.Id);}catch(Exception ex){GameLogger.Log("BOOT","reset "+resettable.Id+" FAILED: "+ex.Message,LogLevel.Error);}}}/// <summary>Clears every registry (mod reload entry point).</summary>
public void ClearRegistries(){foreach(var registry in Registries){try{registry.Clear();GameLogger.Log("BOOT","cleared: "+registry.Id,LogLevel.Debug);}catch(Exception ex){GameLogger.Log("BOOT","clear "+registry.Id+" FAILED: "+ex.Message,LogLevel.Error);}}}/// <summary>Rebuilds every registry from the currently loaded mods.</summary>
public void RebuildRegistries(){foreach(var registry in Registries){try{registry.Rebuild();GameLogger.Log("BOOT","rebuilt: "+registry.Id,LogLevel.Debug);}catch(Exception ex){GameLogger.Log("BOOT","rebuild "+registry.Id+" FAILED: "+ex.Message,LogLevel.Error);}}}// ---- Service slots ------------------------------------------------ Each slot is a Lazy of T so construction timing is identical to the pre-migration Lazy singletons; facades on the service classes delegate here (AppServices.Current.Slot.Value). <summary>Background images shown behind dialog scenes, resolved through the mod resource pipeline.</summary>
public Lazy<BackgroundFactory>Backgrounds{get;}=new(()=>new BackgroundFactory());/// <summary>Full-size UI panel textures (frames, overlays, menu backgrounds).</summary>
public Lazy<UITextureFactory>UITextures{get;}=new(()=>new UITextureFactory());/// <summary>Small UI icons (toolbar buttons, badges) from the <c>ui/icons</c> group.</summary>
public Lazy<UIIconFactory>UIIcons{get;}=new(()=>new UIIconFactory());/// <summary>Inventory item icons, with a dedicated LRU cache budget.</summary>
public Lazy<ItemSpriteFactory>ItemSprites{get;}=new(()=>new ItemSpriteFactory());/// <summary>Skill definitions for the card-based skill system (migrated to the skills_base engine mod).</summary> SkillFactory lives in mods/skills_base now; the AppServices slot is gone by design. <summary>Interactive object definitions for scene hotspots (migrated to the interactive_base engine mod).</summary> InteractiveFactory lives in mods/interactive_base now; the AppServices slot is gone by design. <summary>DSL scenario actions indexed by their registered <c>Name</c> (e.g. <c>"map.open_zone"</c>).</summary>
public Lazy<ScenarioActionFactory>ScenarioActions{get;}=new(()=>new ScenarioActionFactory());/// <summary>Dev tool windows (<see cref="IToolProvider"/> implementations), discovered by reflection.</summary>
public Lazy<ToolFactory>Tools{get;}=new(()=>new ToolFactory());/// <summary>Toolbar button definitions for dev tools (<see cref="IToolBoxButton"/> implementations).</summary>
public Lazy<ToolBoxButtonFactory>ToolBoxButtons{get;}=new(()=>new ToolBoxButtonFactory());/// <summary>Mod pipeline configuration (asset groups, assembly caching, file mappings) from <c>mod_config.json</c>.</summary>
public Lazy<ModConfig>ModConfigService{get;}=new(()=>ModConfig.CreateInstance());/// <summary>Game configuration (audio, display, language, logging) from <c>game_config.json</c>.</summary>
public Lazy<GameConfig>GameConfigService{get;}=new(()=>GameConfig.CreateInstance());/// <summary>Trivial IResettable adapter over a delegate.</summary>
private sealed class LambdaResettable:IResettable{private readonly Action reset;/// <summary>Binds an id and the reset delegate it forwards to.</summary>
public LambdaResettable(string id,Action reset){Id=id;this.reset=reset;}/// <summary>Stable resettable id used for logging and duplicate detection.</summary>
public string Id{get;}/// <summary>Runs the wrapped reset delegate.</summary>

using System;using System.Linq;using System.Threading;using System.Threading.Tasks;using Cthangover.Core.Localization;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes;using Cthangover.Core.Settings;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap{/// <summary> Phases of the unified boot pipeline, in execution order. Comparison by value is meaningful: a later phase implies that all earlier ones finished. </summary>
public enum BootPhase{NotStarted=0,/// <summary>Godot-bound paths resolved on the main thread (mod roots, caches, config).</summary>
PreparingPaths,/// <summary>Discovery, manifest reading and Roslyn compilation of mod assemblies.</summary>
Discovering,/// <summary>Compiled assemblies registered, GDScript loaded, mod load order fixed.</summary>
FinalizingMods,/// <summary>Mod set is final: factories and resolvers may read mod data.</summary>
ModsReady,/// <summary>Locale merged from all loaded mods and activated.</summary>
Locale,/// <summary>Scene/UI registries collected, mod initializers notified, mod settings loaded.</summary>
Scenes,/// <summary>Everything is usable.</summary>
Ready,}/// <summary>How the boot pipeline is being executed.</summary>
public enum BootMode{None,/// <summary>Launcher-driven: heavy phases on a background thread, boot overlay visible.</summary>
LauncherAsync,/// <summary>Blocking synchronous run before the main scene (tests, direct scene launches).</summary>
HeadlessSync,}/// <summary> Single orchestrator of game initialization. Owns the exact order of boot phases. Both entry points drive the SAME sequence through this class: <list type="bullet"> <item><see cref="RunLauncherAsync"/> — the pre-game launcher renders a boot overlay while discovery and Roslyn compilation run on a background thread;</item> <item><see cref="RunSync"/> — direct scene launches and integration tests, executed from the SceneManager autoload _Ready so the whole pipeline completes before any main-scene node runs.</item> </list> Thread contract (mirrors the old launcher-driven flow): path preparation, finalize, runtime, locale and scene registries run on the Godot main thread; only discovery/compilation is pure .NET and moves to a background thread in the launcher mode. Until <see cref="ModsReady"/>, no subsystem may pull data through <see cref="ModRegistry"/> or the factories: lazy self-initialization was removed deliberately, and <see cref="ModRegistry"/> logs a loud error instead of silently booting on first touch. From <see cref="ModsReady"/> on the mod set is final and the pipeline itself consumes it (runtime, starter inventory). If a new caller triggers that refusal error, the fix is to consume the data after readiness (or behind a readiness guard like the audio mod's music player does) — never to re-add a lazy Initialize. </summary>
public static class Boot{private static readonly object startLock=new();/// <summary>Current pipeline phase; <c>NotStarted</c> before the first run.</summary>
public static BootPhase Phase{get;private set;}=BootPhase.NotStarted;/// <summary>Mode of the current (or last) run; <c>None</c> before the first run.</summary>
public static BootMode Mode{get;private set;}=BootMode.None;/// <summary>True once the full pipeline finished; registries and services are usable.</summary>
public static bool IsReady=>Phase==BootPhase.Ready;/// <summary>True once the mod set is final: factories may read mod data.</summary>
public static bool ModsReady=>Phase>=BootPhase.ModsReady;/// <summary>True while the pipeline is executing in any mode.</summary>
public static bool IsBooting=>Mode!=BootMode.None&& !IsReady;/// <summary> Synchronous boot for everything that is not the pre-game launcher: Integration test scenes, direct scene runs and editor "play current scene". Called from the SceneManager autoload _Ready, which is guaranteed to run after GameData exists and before the main scene's nodes. </summary>
public static void RunSync(SceneManager sceneManager){if(!Begin(BootMode.HeadlessSync))return;try{Phase=BootPhase.PreparingPaths;// The whole pipeline runs under ModRegistry's pipeline lock (pipelineRunning is set for its duration), so a stray concurrent Initialize from a background thread or tooling is serialized instead of racing these phases.
ModManager.Instance.Initialize();Phase=BootPhase.ModsReady;EnsureRuntime();Phase=BootPhase.Locale;LocaleLoader.LoadCurrentLanguage();Phase=BootPhase.Scenes;sceneManager?.Initialize();Phase=BootPhase.Ready;Mods.HotReload.ModHotReloadService.InstallIfEnabled(sceneManager?.GetTree());GameLogger.Log("BOOT","Boot (sync) complete");}catch(OperationCanceledException){GameLogger.Log("BOOT","Boot (sync) cancelled",LogLevel.Warning);}catch(Exception ex){// Phase intentionally left where it failed: readiness guards stay armed and every too-early consumer keeps logging loudly instead of silently working against a half-initialized registry.
GameLogger.Log("BOOT",$"Boot (sync) FAILED at phase {Phase}: {ex.Message}",LogLevel.Error);}}/// <summary> Launcher-driven boot. Yields one frame first so the boot overlay is on screen, runs path preparation on the main thread, discovery and Roslyn compilation on a background thread (cooperatively cancellable when the launcher scene dies), then the Godot-bound phases back on the main thread. Throws <see cref="OperationCanceledException"/> if cancelled. </summary>
public static async Task RunLauncherAsync(Node context,CancellationToken cancellationToken){if(!Begin(BootMode.LauncherAsync))return;// Let the boot overlay render one frame before the heavy phases, mirroring the previous launcher-driven timing.
await context.ToSignal(context.GetTree(),SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);try{Phase=BootPhase.PreparingPaths;BootProgress.EnterPhase(BootPhase.PreparingPaths);ModManager.Instance.PreparePaths();Phase=BootPhase.Discovering;BootProgress.EnterPhase(BootPhase.Discovering);await Task.Run(()=>ModManager.Instance.DiscoverAndCompile(cancellationToken),cancellationToken);Phase=BootPhase.FinalizingMods;BootProgress.EnterPhase(BootPhase.FinalizingMods);ModRegistry.Instance.FinalizeGodotInit();Phase=BootPhase.ModsReady;BootProgress.EnterPhase(BootPhase.ModsReady);EnsureRuntime();Phase=BootPhase.Locale;BootProgress.EnterPhase(BootPhase.Locale);LocaleLoader.LoadCurrentLanguage();Phase=BootPhase.Scenes;BootProgress.EnterPhase(BootPhase.Scenes);context.GetNodeOrNull<SceneManager>("/root/SceneManager")?.Initialize();Phase=BootPhase.Ready;BootProgress.EnterPhase(BootPhase.Ready);Mods.HotReload.ModHotReloadService.InstallIfEnabled(context.GetTree());GameLogger.Log("BOOT","Boot (launcher) complete");}finally{// Phase intentionally left where the run stopped: on cancellation readiness guards stay armed, so post-cancel consumers are loud.
}}/// <summary> Constructs the session RuntimeData at a defined point: after the mod set is final, so the starter inventory is seeded by fully loaded factories. Replaces the old lazy getter on GameData.Runtime whose result silently depended on who touched it first. </summary>
private static void EnsureRuntime(){var data=GameData.Instance;if(data==null){GameLogger.Log("BOOT","GameData autoload missing — RuntimeData not created",LogLevel.Error);return;}// A RuntimeData that slipped through before the mod set was final (e.g. a timer tick racing the launcher boot) seeded its starter inventory against an empty registry, and those skips are permanent. Recreate it now that factories can resolve mod items.
if(data.ConsumePrematureRuntimeCreation()){GameLogger.Log("BOOT","RuntimeData was created before mods were ready — recreating it so the starter inventory seeds from loaded mods",LogLevel.Warning);data.ResetRuntime("created before boot finished; starter inventory was empty");}_=data.Runtime;}/// <summary>Idempotence guard: exactly one boot per process.</summary>
private static bool Begin(BootMode mode){lock(startLock){if(Mode!=BootMode.None){GameLogger.Log("BOOT",$"Run({mode}) ignored: boot already ran (mode={Mode}, phase={Phase})",LogLevel.Warning);return false;}Mode=mode;WaitForDebuggerIfRequested();// Fresh service set for this boot: registries empty, the reset list restored to the core defaults, factory slots unused.
AppServices.SetCurrent(new AppServices());return true;}}/// <summary> Debug entry helper (plan-mod-testing.md §9.2): with the <c>--wait-for-debugger</c> command-line flag, offers the OS debugger selection (Windows JIT dialog) before any boot phase runs, so the developer can attach before mod compilation — the phase where runtime-compiled mod code usually needs inspection. A no-op when a debugger is already attached or the flag is absent; the game continues normally when the user cancels the dialog. </summary>
private static void WaitForDebuggerIfRequested(){if(!GameEnvironment.IsRuntime)return;var requested=OS.GetCmdlineArgs().Any(a=>a=="--wait-for-debugger")||OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs().Any(a=>a=="--wait-for-debugger");if(!requested)return;if(System.Diagnostics.Debugger.IsAttached){GameLogger.Log("BOOT","--wait-for-debugger: debugger already attached, continuing");return;}GameLogger.Log("BOOT","--wait-for-debugger: launching debugger selection (cancel = continue without debugger)");var launched=System.Diagnostics.Debugger.Launch();GameLogger.Log("BOOT",$"--wait-for-debugger: Debugger.Launch -> {launched}");}}}

using System;namespace Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap{/// <summary> Progress source for the launcher boot overlay. The boot pipeline and the mod compiler report coarse phase entries and fine-grained sub-steps here; the launcher UI reads a thread-safe snapshot once per frame and maps it onto a progress bar. Weights live here rather than in the UI so the progress model has a single owner: Discovering dominates real boot time (manifest scanning, hashing, Roslyn compilation), while the Godot-bound phases are comparatively cheap. Values were sampled from GameLogger timestamps on a cold-cache run and are hardcoded on purpose — a config entry would be read before paths exist. </summary>
public static class BootProgress{private static readonly object Sync=new();private static BootPhase _phase=BootPhase.NotStarted;private static float _sub;/// <summary> Marks the start of a pipeline phase. Called from the boot thread(s); sub-progress resets because sub-steps never span phases. </summary>
public static void EnterPhase(BootPhase phase){lock(Sync){_phase=phase;_sub=0f;}}/// <summary>Reports sub-progress (0..1) inside the current phase.</summary>
public static void ReportSub(float sub){sub=Math.Clamp(sub,0f,1f);lock(Sync){if(sub>_sub)_sub=sub;}}/// <summary> Snapshot of overall boot progress (0..1). Weighted by the phase weights below; phases after the current one contribute nothing. </summary>
public static float GetOverall(){lock(Sync){return OverallFor(_phase,_sub);}}private static readonly int WeightPreparingPaths=5;private static readonly int WeightDiscovering=60;private static readonly int WeightFinalizingMods=15;private static readonly int WeightPostMods=20;private const int TotalWeight=100;private static float OverallFor(BootPhase phase,float sub){switch(phase){case BootPhase.Ready:return 1f;case BootPhase.PreparingPaths:return WeightPreparingPaths*sub/TotalWeight;case BootPhase.Discovering:return(WeightPreparingPaths+WeightDiscovering*sub)/TotalWeight;case BootPhase.FinalizingMods:return(WeightPreparingPaths+WeightDiscovering+WeightFinalizingMods*sub)/TotalWeight;case BootPhase.ModsReady:return(WeightPreparingPaths+WeightDiscovering+WeightFinalizingMods)/TotalWeight;case BootPhase.Locale:return(WeightPreparingPaths+WeightDiscovering+WeightFinalizingMods+WeightPostMods/3f)/TotalWeight;case BootPhase.Scenes:return(WeightPreparingPaths+WeightDiscovering+WeightFinalizingMods+WeightPostMods*2f/3f)/TotalWeight;default:return 0f;}}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap{/// <summary> A mod-derived registry that can be rebuilt from the currently loaded mod set and cleared back to its empty state. Registries register themselves in <see cref="AppServices"/> (explicit list in its constructor), which turns mod reload and boot from hand-maintained clear-lists into a data-driven loop: adding a registry is one line in <see cref="AppServices"/>, with no edits in <c>ModManager.Reload</c>. <para/> Implementation contract: the instance constructor must stay cheap and side-effect free (no Godot API, no mod reads); <see cref="Rebuild"/> fills the registry from the loaded mod set and must be safe to call again without a preceding <see cref="Clear"/>; <see cref="Clear"/> returns the registry to its just-constructed state. </summary>

string Id{get;}/// <summary>(Re)fills the registry from the currently loaded mods.</summary>
void Rebuild();/// <summary>Drops all collected entries; the next <see cref="Rebuild"/> re-reads the mods.</summary>
void Clear();}}

using Cthangover.Core.Factories;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> A battle action available to a character (e.g. "Attack", "Heal"). Carries a PropertyData bag keyed by free-form string keys (e.g. "Attack", "Defence", "Turn", "RequiredPoint") rather than typed properties — this allows mods to add custom action parameters without schema changes. Copy() deep-clones Properties to prevent shared state between character instances that may modify action data at runtime (e.g. temporary buffs). </summary>
public class ActionCharacter:IIdentifiable{/// <summary> Unique action identifier, used as the factory lookup key. </summary>
public string ID{get;set;}/// <summary> Display name shown in the battle action menu. </summary>
public string Name{get;set;}/// <summary> Tooltip/description text shown in the battle action menu. </summary>
public string Description{get;set;}/// <summary> Targeting category: <see cref="ActionCharacterType.ToSelf"/> (caster), <see cref="ActionCharacterType.ToAlias"/> (allies), or <see cref="ActionCharacterType.ToEnemy"/> (opponents). </summary>
public ActionCharacterType Type{get;set;}/// <summary> Icon texture for the battle action menu. </summary>
public Texture2D Image{get;set;}/// <summary> String-indexed property bag containing the action's numeric parameters (damage, heal, cost, etc.) keyed by free-form strings. Mods define their own keys without schema changes. </summary>
public PropertyData Properties{get;set;}/// <summary> Reads a string property from <see cref="Properties"/> by key, with an optional default for missing entries. </summary>
public string GetStr(string name,string defaultValue=null)=>Properties.GetStr(name,defaultValue);/// <summary> Reads an integer property from <see cref="Properties"/> by key, with an optional default for missing entries. </summary>
public int GetInt(string name,int defaultValue=0)=>Properties.GetInt(name,defaultValue);/// <summary> Reads a float property from <see cref="Properties"/> by key, with an optional default for missing entries. </summary>
public float GetFloat(string name,float defaultValue=0f)=>Properties.GetFloat(name,defaultValue);/// <summary> Reads a boolean property from <see cref="Properties"/> by key. </summary>
public bool GetBool(string name)=>Properties.GetBool(name);/// <summary> Creates an independent copy of this action. All scalar/string fields are value-copied; <see cref="Properties"/> is deep- cloned via <see cref="PropertyData.Clone"/> to prevent shared state mutations (e.g. temporary effect modifiers) from leaking across character instances. </summary>
public ActionCharacter Copy(){return new ActionCharacter(){ID=ID,Name=Name,Description=Description,Type=Type,Image=Image,Properties=Properties?.Clone(),};}}}

===== FILE Core/Characters/Attribute.cs =====
using System;namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> Mutable stat with event-driven change tracking. Value is the current (potentially modified) value; BaseValue is the unmodified maximum. Percent gives the 0–1 ratio for health bars and stat displays. The OnChange delegate fires on every Value set — even if the value hasn't changed — making it a notification mechanism rather than a diff detector. This is important for UI that must react to "was modified" events regardless of whether the value actually changed (e.g. a heal that fizzles at full health should still trigger visual feedback). </summary>
[Serializable]public class Attribute{/// <summary> Fires on every <see cref="Value"/> setter call, regardless of whether the value actually changed. Subscribers receive (currentValue, baseValue) — this is a notification mechanism, not a diff detector. Important for UI that must react to "was modified" events even when the value is unchanged (e.g. a heal that fizzles at full health should still trigger visual feedback). </summary>
public event ChangeAttribute OnChange;private int val;/// <summary> The current (potentially modified) value of this attribute. Setting triggers <see cref="OnChange"/> with both the new value and <see cref="BaseValue"/> for percentage computation. </summary>
public int Value{get{return val;}set{this.val=value;OnChange?.Invoke(this.val,BaseValue);}}/// <summary> The unmodified maximum/base value. Together with <see cref="Value"/>, this drives the <see cref="Percent"/> ratio used by health bars and stat displays. </summary>
public int BaseValue{get;set;}/// <summary> Sets both <see cref="Value"/> and <see cref="BaseValue"/> to the same starting value. Used during character initialization to establish the baseline before any modifications. </summary> <param name="val">The initial value for both current and base.</param>
public void Init(int val){Value=val;BaseValue=val;}/// <summary> Current value as a fraction of base value (0.0 to 1.0+ if value exceeds base). Returns 0 when <see cref="BaseValue"/> is 0 to avoid division by zero. Used by health bar fill ratios and stat comparison displays. </summary>
public float Percent=>BaseValue==0?0f:(float)Value/BaseValue;/// <summary> Creates an independent copy with the same <see cref="Value"/> and <see cref="BaseValue"/>. The <see cref="OnChange"/> event subscribers are NOT copied — the clone starts with an empty delegate list, which is correct for battle instances that need their own UI bindings. </summary>
public Attribute Copy(){return new Attribute(){Value=Value,BaseValue=BaseValue,};}}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Factories;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> Core character data model used in both the character factory and battle runtime. The Behaviour string is an extensibility hook — it names a behaviour class not defined here, resolved externally (likely by the AI or battle system). RecruitmentChance is the percentage for the recruit system. Copy() deep-clones Attributes so battle stat changes do not leak back into the template data. Battle-only state that is not part of the character identity (for example status effects) is owned by the battle mod in a side table keyed by the character instance, so this model stays free of battle subsystems. </summary>
public class Character:IIdentifiable{/// <summary> Unique identifier string used as the factory lookup key and save-data reference. Must match the ID in the character's JSON data file (CharacterInfo.ID). </summary>
public string ID{get;set;}/// <summary> Name of the behaviour class that controls this character's AI during battle. Resolved externally by the battle engine or AI system — not defined within this assembly. Null for player- controlled characters or simple enemies. </summary>
public string Behaviour{get;set;}/// <summary> Current character level. Loaded from the template and carried forward into CharacterInfoData on recruitment. </summary>
public int Level{get;set;}/// <summary> Current experience points. Accumulated through combat and used by the leveling system to determine when a level-up occurs. </summary>
public int Exp{get;set;}/// <summary> Percentage chance (0–100) that a defeated enemy becomes recruitable via the recruit system. Read by battle resolution to determine if the "recruit" option appears post-combat. </summary>
public int RecruitmentChance{get;set;}/// <summary> Display name shown in the UI. Localized via TranslationServer when presented to the player (e.g. in party roster). </summary>
public string Name{get;set;}/// <summary> Full-body character portrait texture for the character detail screen. Loaded from disk at factory construction time. </summary>
public Texture2D Image{get;set;}/// <summary> Small portrait frame texture for list views (party roster, battle HUD). Typically a cropped or smaller version of Image. </summary>
public Texture2D Frame{get;set;}/// <summary> List of battle actions available to this character. Drawn from the character's JSON data file and populated by the factory. </summary>
public List<ActionCharacter>Actions{get;set;}/// <summary> Complete stat block: Health, Defence, Attack, Strength, Magic, Point (all <see cref="Attribute"/>-wrapped) plus raw Discipline, Fullness. Deep-copied by <see cref="Copy"/>. </summary>
public CharacterAttributes Attributes{get;set;}/// <summary> Loot drop table for when this character is defeated as an enemy. Each <see cref="LootEntry"/> defines an item, count range, and drop probability. </summary>
public List<LootEntry>Loot{get;set;}/// <summary> Default constructor. Initializes Actions and Attributes with empty/default collections to prevent null-reference errors in downstream code that iterates them. </summary>
public Character(){Actions=new List<ActionCharacter>();Attributes=new CharacterAttributes();}/// <summary> Creates an independent deep copy of this character. All scalar fields are value-copied. <see cref="Attributes"/> is deep-cloned — this is critical for battle, where each combatant operates on an isolated copy so temporary stat changes don't leak back into the character template. </summary>
public Character Copy(){var character=new Character(){ID=ID,Behaviour=Behaviour,Level=Level,Exp=Exp,Name=Name,Image=Image,Frame=Frame,Actions=Actions,RecruitmentChance=RecruitmentChance,Loot=Loot,Attributes=Attributes?.Copy(),};return character;}}}

The initial party roster is populated by mods through IModInitializer implementations — each mod adds its default starter characters during mod loading. public class CharacterData{/// <summary> Set of character IDs currently in the active battle party. Populated when characters join the party via <see cref="AddCharacterToParty"/> and consulted by the battle system to determine available combatants. </summary>

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> Kernel access point for character template resolution, decoupling the core from the engine mod that owns the factory (<c>mods/characters_base</c>). The mod's initializer assigns <see cref="Provider"/> during <c>IModInitializer.OnModLoaded</c>; all core-side consumers (<see cref="CharacterData"/>, inventory and skills UI) resolve templates through <see cref="Get"/>. Before the mod registers — tests, tools, very early boot — <see cref="Get"/> returns <c>null</c>, which <see cref="CharacterData.Create"/> already treats as the unknown-ID fallback path. <para/> The registry deliberately exposes two flavors, mirroring the project's lookup policy: <see cref="Get"/> is the lenient content lookup (a typo in scenario content degrades UI gracefully), while <see cref="GetRequired"/> is the fail-fast twin for engine-critical paths — boot wiring, tools, tests — where continuing without the template would hide the defect. The same split exists in the scenario action registry (<c>ScenarioActionFactory.Get/GetRequired</c>) and in <c>BattleCoreRegistry</c>, which throws on unknown core IDs. </summary>
public static class CharacterTemplateRegistry{/// <summary>Provider published by the characters engine mod; <c>null</c> until the mod loads.</summary>
public static ICharacterTemplateProvider Provider{get;set;}/// <summary>Returns an independent copy of the character template, or <c>null</c> when no provider is registered or the ID is unknown.</summary>
public static Character Get(string id)=>Provider?.Get(id);/// <summary> Resolves a character template and fails fast when it cannot: either no provider is registered yet (the characters engine mod has not loaded — a kernel wiring bug, not a content problem) or the ID is not declared in any loaded mod. Never returns null. </summary> <exception cref="InvalidOperationException">No provider registered — <see cref="Provider"/> is still null.</exception> <exception cref="KeyNotFoundException">The ID has no template declaration.</exception>
public static Character GetRequired(string id){if(Provider==null)throw new InvalidOperationException("CharacterTemplateRegistry has no provider: the characters engine mod has not published CharacterFactory yet.");return Provider.Get(id)??throw new KeyNotFoundException($"Character template '{id}' is not declared in any loaded mod. "+"Check the Id field in the character JSON or the reference spelling.");}}}

===== FILE Core/Characters/IPropertyInterceptor.cs =====
namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> Contract for intercepting property writes in <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Utils.PropertyData"/>. Each interceptor is bound to a single property key via <see cref="PropertyName"/> and is called in registration order when that property is written through any typed setter (<c>SetStr</c>, <c>SetInt</c>, <c>SetFloat</c>, <c>SetBool</c>, <c>SetLong</c>). Multiple interceptors for the same property form a pipeline: each receives the value returned by the previous one, so interceptors can compose (e.g. one doubles healing, another caps max HP). </summary> <remarks> Registration is per-instance via <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Utils.PropertyData.AddInterceptor"/>. Interceptors are NOT copied by <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Utils.PropertyData.Clone"/> — they are runtime behaviour scoped to a specific character's property bag. </remarks>
public interface IPropertyInterceptor{/// <summary> Called before the value is stored in the backing dictionary. Receives the previous string value (<c>null</c> if the property didn't exist) and the new value (possibly already modified by earlier interceptors). Returns the value to store after this interceptor's transformation. </summary> <param name="prevValue"> Raw string value before this write, or <c>null</c> if the property was absent. Use <see cref="PropertyInterceptor{T}"/> for type-safe access — it handles parsing and formatting. </param> <param name="newValue"> Value being written — may have been modified by earlier interceptors in the chain. Guaranteed non-null: all <c>SetXxx</c> methods produce a non-null string. </param> <returns>The (possibly modified) string value to store.</returns>
string Intercept(string prevValue,string newValue);/// <summary> The property key this interceptor watches. <see cref="PropertyData.Set{T}"/> only calls interceptors whose <see cref="PropertyName"/> matches the key being written. </summary>
string PropertyName{get;}}}

===== FILE Core/Characters/LootEntry.cs =====
using System;using System.Text.Json.Serialization;using Cthangover.Core.Mods.Patches;namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> Loot drop definition for enemies: ItemId, min/max count range, and probability (0–100 percentage). Implements <see cref="IMergeable"/> with <c>ItemId</c> as the identity key so that <c>Loot$add</c> and <c>Loot$remove</c> patches can match entries by item rather than by exact JSON text. </summary>
public class LootEntry:IMergeable{string IMergeable.MergeKeyProperty=>nameof(ItemId);/// <summary> Item identifier string for the loot drop. Resolved against the item registry at drop time. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("ItemId")]public string ItemId{get;set;}/// <summary> Minimum quantity of this item to drop when the roll succeeds. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("MinCount")]public int MinCount{get;set;}/// <summary> Maximum quantity of this item to drop when the roll succeeds. Together with <see cref="MinCount"/> defines an inclusive range for randomized drop amounts. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("MaxCount")]public int MaxCount{get;set;}/// <summary> Drop probability as a percentage (0–100). Evaluated by the loot system after battle to determine whether this entry produces a drop. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("Probability")]public int Probability{get;set;}/// <summary> How many items this entry drops on one roll: 0 when the <see cref="Probability"/> (percent, clamped to 0–100) misses, otherwise a count between <see cref="MinCount"/> and <see cref="MaxCount"/> inclusive. Swapped bounds are read in either order and negative counts drop nothing — a slip in a loot table must not throw on the victory screen, which rolls every entry. </summary>
public int Roll(Random random){var probability=Math.Clamp(Probability,0,100);if(probability==0||(probability<100&&random.Next(1,101)>probability))return 0;var low=Math.Max(0,Math.Min(MinCount,MaxCount));var high=Math.Max(0,Math.Max(MinCount,MaxCount));return random.Next(low,high+1);}}}

===== FILE Core/Characters/PropertyInterceptor.cs =====
using System;using System.Globalization;using Cthangover.Core.Utils.Types;namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> Typed base for <see cref="IPropertyInterceptor"/> implementations. Eliminates manual string parsing/formatting — the interceptor author overrides <see cref="Intercept(T, T)"/> working with typed values, and the base class handles conversion through <see cref="IParse{T}"/> (resolved via <see cref="TParser"/>). </summary> <typeparam name="T"> The value type this interceptor operates on. Must match a parser registered in <see cref="TParser"/> (e.g. <c>int</c>, <c>int?</c>, <c>float</c>, <c>bool</c>, <c>string</c>). </typeparam> <remarks> <para> <c>prevValue</c> parses to <c>default(T)</c> when the property didn't exist (null for nullable types, 0/0f/false for primitives). The converted result uses <see cref="Convert.ToString(object, IFormatProvider)"/> with <see cref="CultureInfo.InvariantCulture"/> to ensure round-trip compatibility with <see cref="FloatParse"/>. </para> <para> Example — double healing: <code> class DoubleHeal : PropertyInterceptor&lt;int&gt; { public override string PropertyName => "Health"; protected override int Intercept(int prev, int next) => next > prev ? prev + (next - prev) * 2 : next; } </code> </para> </remarks>
public abstract class PropertyInterceptor<T>:IPropertyInterceptor{private static readonly IParse<T>_parse=TParser.Resolve<T>();/// <inheritdoc cref="IPropertyInterceptor.Intercept"/>
public string Intercept(string prevValue,string newValue){var prev=_parse.Parse(prevValue);var next=_parse.Parse(newValue);var result=Intercept(prev,next);return Convert.ToString(result,CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);}/// <summary> Type-safe interception point. Called when a property matching <see cref="PropertyName"/> is written. Receives the parsed previous and new values, returns the (possibly modified) new value. </summary> <param name="prevValue"> Parsed previous value. For nullable types, <c>null</c> means the property didn't exist. For primitive types, 0/false means either absent or genuinely zero. </param> <param name="newValue"> Parsed new value being written, possibly modified by earlier interceptors in the chain for the same property. </param>
protected abstract T Intercept(T prevValue,T newValue);/// <inheritdoc/>
public abstract string PropertyName{get;}}}
