using System.Threading;using Cthangover.Core.Events;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes{/// <summary> Single "freshness flag" of scenario condition results. Subscribes to every state-change event conditions depend on (quest tags/statuses, flags, save restore, interactives, map zones) and increments the monotonic Version. Consumers (ScenarioEvent caches its condition result) treat a cached result as valid while Version stays the same. Every increment is also published as <see cref="ConditionStateChangedEvent"/>, so event chains react to changes instead of polling Version. MarkStateChanged() is the public manual invalidator for mods with custom state outside quests; Notify&lt;T&gt; is public for unit tests without Godot. Caution: ModEventBus.ClearAll() drops the subscriptions; the game never calls it, but after such a call EnsureSubscribed() must be called again. </summary>
public static class ConditionStateMonitor{private static long _version;private static readonly object Lock=new();private static bool _subscribed;/// <summary> Monotonically growing counter of state changes. Every event the monitor subscribes to increments it by 1; equal values mean "the state did not change since the last read". </summary>
public static long Version=>Interlocked.Read(ref _version);/// <summary> Manual invalidator: forces Version to grow outside the regular events (for mods with custom state that conditions read). Publishes the new version as <see cref="ConditionStateChangedEvent"/> — event chains subscribe to it instead of polling Version. </summary>
public static void MarkStateChanged(){var version=Interlocked.Increment(ref _version);ModEventBus.Publish(new ConditionStateChangedEvent{Version=version});}/// <summary>Handler of every monitored event — bumps the version.</summary>
public static void Notify<T>(T evt)where T:ModEvent{MarkStateChanged();}/// <summary> Ensures the monitor is subscribed to every state-change event. Idempotent — repeated calls do nothing. Called from the static constructor; calling it again is only needed after <c>ModEventBus.ClearAll()</c> dropped the static subscriptions. </summary>
public static void EnsureSubscribed(){lock(Lock){if(_subscribed)return;_subscribed=true;ModEventBus.Subscribe<QuestTagChangedEvent>(Notify);ModEventBus.Subscribe<QuestStatusChangedEvent>(Notify);ModEventBus.Subscribe<QuestDataStatusChangedEvent>(Notify);ModEventBus.Subscribe<FlagChangedEvent>(Notify);ModEventBus.Subscribe<QuestStateRestoredEvent>(Notify);ModEventBus.Subscribe<InteractiveStateChangedEvent>(Notify);ModEventBus.Subscribe<MapZoneChangedEvent>(Notify);}}static ConditionStateMonitor(){EnsureSubscribed();}}}

===== FILE Core/Scenes/FlagCondition.cs =====
namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes{/// <summary> An AST leaf node representing a comparison between a named runtime flag and a literal value. Looks up the flag key in the <see cref="EvaluationContext.Flags"/> dictionary at evaluation time. Supports both numeric and string comparisons; if both the stored and expected values parse as integers, a numeric comparison is performed via <see cref="ConditionCompare.Compare"/>. When the flag is absent from the dictionary, the condition returns <c>true</c> for <c>!=</c> and <c>false</c> for all other operators — this "missing means not-equal" semantics allows scenario scripts to gate on flags that may not yet have been set. </summary>
public class FlagCondition:ConditionNode{/// <summary>The flag key to look up in the runtime flag dictionary.</summary>
public string Key{get;}/// <summary>The comparison operator (<c>==</c>, <c>!=</c>, etc.).</summary>
public string Op{get;}/// <summary>The literal value to compare the flag against.</summary>
public string Value{get;}/// <summary> Creates a flag comparison condition node. </summary> <param name="key">The flag key.</param> <param name="op">The comparison operator.</param> <param name="value">The literal value to compare against.</param>
public FlagCondition(string key,string op,string value){Key=key;Op=op;Value=value;}/// <summary>Reads the live flag value and compares it; a missing flag counts as "not equal".</summary>
public override bool Evaluate(EvaluationContext ctx){if(!ctx.Flags.TryGetValue(Key,out var current))return Op=="!=";if(int.TryParse(current,out var ci)&&int.TryParse(Value,out var fi))return ConditionCompare.Compare(Op,ci,fi);return Op switch{"=="=>current==Value,"!="=>current!=Value,_=>false};}}}

Godot's <c>GD.Load&lt;PackedScene&gt;</c> cannot see files inside <c>mods/</c> (the folder is <c>.gdignore</c>d), so code that instantiates mod-provided scenes stores a mod-relative path and defers to <see cref="TscnScenes"/>. public string Path=>path;/// <summary>Builds a new instance and casts it to <typeparamref name="T"/>; null when unavailable.</summary>
public T Instantiate<T>()where T:Node{return TscnScenes.LoadAndBuild(path)as T;}/// <summary>Builds a new untyped instance; null when the scene cannot be resolved.</summary>
public Node Instantiate(){return TscnScenes.LoadAndBuild(path);}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Nodes.Impls{/// <summary> AST node for boolean AND — evaluates <see cref="Left"/> first, then <see cref="Right"/> only if <see cref="Left"/> is <c>true</c>. This short-circuit behaviour is inherited from the C# <c>&amp;&amp;</c> operator and requires no explicit control flow. Produced by <see cref="ConditionParser"/> from the <c>&amp;&amp;</c> token in condition expressions. When a mod constructs an AST manually, it wraps <see cref="Left"/> and <see cref="Right"/> directly without involving the parser. </summary>
public class AndNode:ConditionNode{/// <summary>Evaluated first; if <c>false</c>, <see cref="Right"/> is skipped.</summary>
public ICondition Left{get;}/// <summary>Evaluated only when <see cref="Left"/> returns <c>true</c>.</summary>
public ICondition Right{get;}/// <summary>Creates an AND node over two operand sub-expressions.</summary> <param name="left">Operand evaluated first.</param> <param name="right">Operand evaluated only when <paramref name="left"/> is true.</param>
public AndNode(ICondition left,ICondition right){Left=left;Right=right;}/// <summary>Short-circuits: <see cref="Right"/> runs only when <see cref="Left"/> is true.</summary>
public override bool Evaluate(EvaluationContext ctx)=>Left.Evaluate(ctx)&&Right.Evaluate(ctx);}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing.Impls;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing{/// <summary> Pratt precedence-climbing parser that converts a token list into an <see cref="ICondition"/> tree. Operators are resolved through <see cref="OperatorRegistry"/>; leaf values through <see cref="LeafParserRegistry"/>. Precedence values: higher = tighter binding. Infix operators use <c>op.Precedence</c> for the right operand to enforce left- associativity. The loop condition is strict greater-than (<c>></c>) so that operators at the current precedence level are consumed from left to right. The parser makes a single left-to-right pass over the token list, consuming each token exactly once. No backtracking, no regex. </summary>
public class ExpressionParser{private TokenPeeker _peeker;static ExpressionParser(){OperatorRegistry.Register(new AndOpParser());OperatorRegistry.Register(new OrOpParser());OperatorRegistry.Register(new NotOpParser());}/// <summary> Parses a complete token list into an <see cref="ICondition"/> tree. </summary>
public ICondition Parse(List<ConditionParser.Token>tokens){_peeker=new TokenPeeker(tokens,null);var parseSubExpr=new Func<ICondition>(()=>ParseExpr(0));_peeker=new TokenPeeker(tokens,parseSubExpr);var result=ParseExpr(0);if(!_peeker.AtEnd&&_peeker.Peek.Type!=ConditionParser.TokenType.EOF)throw new FormatException($"Condition parse error: unexpected token '{_peeker.Peek.Value}' at end of expression");return result;}private ICondition ParseExpr(int minPrecedence){var left=ParsePrefix();while(!_peeker.AtEnd){var op=OperatorRegistry.Get(_peeker.Peek.Type);if(op==null|| !op.IsInfix||op.Precedence<=minPrecedence)break;_peeker.Advance();var right=ParseExpr(op.Precedence);left=op.BuildInfix(left,right);}return left;}private ICondition ParsePrefix(){if(_peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.LParen)){_peeker.Advance();var expr=ParseExpr(0);_peeker.Expect(ConditionParser.TokenType.RParen,"expected ')' after expression");return expr;}var op=_peeker.AtEnd?null:OperatorRegistry.Get(_peeker.Peek.Type);if(op!=null&&op.IsPrefix){_peeker.Advance();var operand=ParseExpr(op.Precedence);return op.BuildPrefix(operand);}var leafParser=LeafParserRegistry.FindParser(_peeker);if(leafParser==null)throw new FormatException($"Condition parse error: unexpected token '{(_peeker.AtEnd ? "EOF" : _peeker.Peek.Value)}'");return leafParser.Parse(_peeker,()=>ParseExpr(0));}}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing{/// <summary> Condition leaf node backed by a GDScript custom condition (registered by <c>ModGDScriptLoader</c> through <see cref="GDLeafParser"/>). Evaluation converts the flag dictionary to a Godot Dictionary and invokes the script's <c>evaluate(flags, args)</c> method, so the whole custom-condition contract stays in GDScript without C# glue per mod. </summary>
public class GDCondition:ConditionNode{private readonly GodotObject _instance;private readonly Godot.Collections.Dictionary _args;/// <summary>Wraps a GDScript instance and the positional arguments parsed after the condition name.</summary> <param name="instance">Live GodotObject exposing <c>evaluate(flags, args)</c>.</param> <param name="args">Positional call arguments keyed by their string index ("0", "1", …).</param>
public GDCondition(GodotObject instance,Godot.Collections.Dictionary args){_instance=instance;_args=args;}/// <summary>Copies flags into a Godot Dictionary and calls the script's <c>evaluate</c> method.</summary>
public override bool Evaluate(EvaluationContext ctx){var gdFlags=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary();foreach(var kv in ctx.Flags)gdFlags[kv.Key]=kv.Value;return _instance.Call("evaluate",gdFlags,_args).AsBool();}}}

using System;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing{/// <summary> Leaf parser for GDScript custom conditions such as <c>gds.is_rain</c> or <c>gds.flag_equals("victory")</c>. Created by <c>ModGDScriptLoader</c> and inserted at the front of the <see cref="LeafParserRegistry"/> list, so a GDScript condition wins over the built-in quest/flag parsers. Matches when the next two identifiers joined by a dot equal the script's <c>get_condition_name()</c> value. </summary>
public class GDLeafParser:ILeafParser{private readonly string _conditionName;private readonly GodotObject _instance;/// <summary>Creates a parser bound to one GDScript condition name.</summary> <param name="conditionName">Value returned by the script's <c>get_condition_name()</c>, e.g. "gds.is_rain".</param> <param name="instance">Live GodotObject whose <c>evaluate(flags, args)</c> computes the result.</param>
public GDLeafParser(string conditionName,GodotObject instance){_conditionName=conditionName;_instance=instance;}/// <summary>True when the next <c>ident.ident</c> pair matches this parser's condition name (checked on a positional snapshot).</summary>
public bool CanParse(TokenPeeker peeker){if(peeker.AtEnd||peeker.Peek.Type!=ConditionParser.TokenType.Ident)return false;var snapshot=peeker.Snapshot();var ident=snapshot.Advance().Value;if(snapshot.AtEnd||snapshot.Peek.Type!=ConditionParser.TokenType.Dot)return false;snapshot.Advance();if(snapshot.AtEnd||snapshot.Peek.Type!=ConditionParser.TokenType.Ident)return false;var method=snapshot.Advance().Value;return$"{ident}.{method}"==_conditionName;}/// <summary>Consumes the condition name and an optional parenthesised argument list, producing a <see cref="GDCondition"/>.</summary>
public ICondition Parse(TokenPeeker peeker,Func<ICondition>parseSubExpr){peeker.Advance();// ident
peeker.Expect(ConditionParser.TokenType.Dot,"expected '.' after mod prefix");peeker.Advance();// method name
var args=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary();if(!peeker.AtEnd&&peeker.Peek.Type==ConditionParser.TokenType.LParen){peeker.Advance();// '('
if(!peeker.AtEnd&&peeker.Peek.Type!=ConditionParser.TokenType.RParen){var argIndex=0;while(true){if(peeker.AtEnd)throw new FormatException("Condition parse error: unexpected end of arguments");args[argIndex.ToString()]=peeker.Advance().Value;argIndex++;if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Comma)){peeker.Advance();continue;}break;}}peeker.Expect(ConditionParser.TokenType.RParen,"expected ')'");}return new GDCondition(_instance,args);}}}

using System;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing{/// <summary> Parses a leaf value from the token stream — a literal, a flag comparison, a quest method call, or any other terminal expression that produces an <see cref="ICondition"/>. Registered in <see cref="LeafParserRegistry"/>. Mods add custom leaf types (e.g. weather conditions, skill checks) by implementing this interface and calling <see cref="LeafParserRegistry.Register"/>. <see cref="CanParse"/> receives a <see cref="TokenPeeker"/> — a read-only view of upcoming tokens — and must return true only when this parser can handle the input. No tokens are consumed during the check. <see cref="Parse"/> receives a mutable stream and the <paramref name="parseSubExpr"/> callback for recursive sub-expression parsing (used when a leaf contains parentheses, e.g. flag arguments that are themselves expressions). </summary>
public interface ILeafParser{/// <summary> Checks whether this parser can handle the tokens at the current position. Peek only — do not advance the stream. </summary>
bool CanParse(TokenPeeker peeker);/// <summary> Consumes tokens from the stream and returns the parsed <see cref="ICondition"/>. </summary> <param name="peeker">Mutable token stream — advance past consumed tokens.</param> <param name="parseSubExpr">Callback for nested sub-expression parsing, e.g. content inside parentheses.</param>
ICondition Parse(TokenPeeker peeker,Func<ICondition>parseSubExpr);}}

using System;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing{/// <summary> Parses a binary or unary operator token into an <see cref="ICondition"/> subtree. Registered in <see cref="OperatorRegistry"/> — mods can add custom operators (e.g. XOR, NAND) by implementing this interface and calling <see cref="OperatorRegistry.Register"/> during mod initialisation. <see cref="Precedence"/> controls binding strength: higher values mean looser binding. In <c>A && B || C</c>, <c>||</c> has higher precedence (binds looser) than <c>&&</c>, so the tree is <c>||(&&(A, B), C)</c>. For infix operators (<c>&&</c>, <c>||</c>), <see cref="ExpressionParser"/> calls <see cref="BuildInfix"/> with left and right operands. For prefix operators (<c>!</c>), it calls <see cref="BuildPrefix"/> with the single operand. </summary>
public interface IOperatorParser{/// <summary>The token type this parser handles.</summary>
ConditionParser.TokenType Token{get;}/// <summary>Binding precedence — higher = looser binding (||=40, &&=30, !=50).</summary>
int Precedence{get;}/// <summary>True for prefix unary operators (!A).</summary>
bool IsPrefix{get;}/// <summary>True for infix binary operators (A && B).</summary>
bool IsInfix{get;}/// <summary>Constructs an infix node from left and right operands. Returns null when <see cref="IsInfix"/> is false.</summary>
ICondition BuildInfix(ICondition left,ICondition right);/// <summary>Constructs a prefix node from its operand. Returns null when <see cref="IsPrefix"/> is false.</summary>
ICondition BuildPrefix(ICondition operand);}}

public ConditionParser.TokenType Token=>ConditionParser.TokenType.And;/// <summary>Precedence 20 — tighter than <c>||</c> (10), looser than prefix <c>!</c> (50).</summary>
public int Precedence=>20;/// <summary><c>&amp;&amp;</c> is strictly an infix operator.</summary>

using System;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing.Impls{/// <summary> Parses flag comparison expressions: <c>flag_name OP literal</c>. Matches when the stream contains an identifier followed by a comparison operator (== != >= <= > <). Must be tried AFTER <see cref="QuestParser"/> and <see cref="BoolLiteralParser"/> in the registry — those parsers also start with an identifier but consume the dot or check for true/false respectively. By the time <see cref="CanParse"/> is called here, any dot-followed or keyword identifiers have already been claimed. </summary>
public class FlagParser:ILeafParser{/// <summary>True for identifiers immediately followed by a comparison operator (dot-forms are claimed by earlier parsers).</summary>
public bool CanParse(TokenPeeker peeker){if(peeker.AtEnd||peeker.Peek.Type!=ConditionParser.TokenType.Ident)return false;var next=peeker.PeekAhead(1);return next.Type==ConditionParser.TokenType.Eq||next.Type==ConditionParser.TokenType.Neq||next.Type==ConditionParser.TokenType.Ge||next.Type==ConditionParser.TokenType.Le||next.Type==ConditionParser.TokenType.Gt||next.Type==ConditionParser.TokenType.Lt;}/// <summary>Consumes <c>key OP literal</c> (string or number literal) and builds a <see cref="FlagCondition"/>.</summary>
public ICondition Parse(TokenPeeker peeker,Func<ICondition>parseSubExpr){var key=peeker.Advance().Value;var op=ParseCompOp(peeker);ConditionParser.Token valToken;if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.String)||peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Number))valToken=peeker.Advance();else throw new FormatException($"Condition parse error: expected string or number after operator, got '{peeker.Peek.Value}'");return new FlagCondition(key,op,valToken.Value);}private static string ParseCompOp(TokenPeeker peeker){if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Eq)){peeker.Advance();return"==";}if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Neq)){peeker.Advance();return"!=";}if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Ge)){peeker.Advance();return">=";}if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Le)){peeker.Advance();return"<=";}if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Gt)){peeker.Advance();return">";}if(peeker.Check(ConditionParser.TokenType.Lt)){peeker.Advance();return"<";}throw new FormatException($"Condition parse error: expected comparison operator, got '{peeker.Peek.Value}'");}}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing.Impls;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing{/// <summary> Ordered registry of <see cref="ILeafParser"/> instances, queried by <see cref="ExpressionParser"/> when the next token does not match any registered operator. Parsers are tried in registration order — the first whose <see cref="ILeafParser.CanParse"/> returns true wins. Mods register custom leaf parsers via <see cref="Register"/> (or <see cref="RegisterFirst"/> to take priority). Core parsers (booleans, flags, groups) are registered at static init; the quest parser registers itself from the quests engine mod at <c>IModInitializer.OnModLoaded</c> — the parser set is fully extensible and the core hardcodes no gameplay parsers. </summary>
public static class LeafParserRegistry{private static readonly List<ILeafParser>_parsers=new();static LeafParserRegistry(){Register(new BoolLiteralParser());Register(new FlagParser());Register(new GroupParser());}/// <summary>Appends a parser to the end of the list.</summary>
public static void Register(ILeafParser parser){_parsers.Add(parser);}/// <summary>Inserts a parser at the front of the list so it takes priority.</summary>
public static void RegisterFirst(ILeafParser parser){_parsers.Insert(0,parser);}/// <summary> Returns the first registered parser whose <see cref="ILeafParser.CanParse"/> returns true for the current token position, or null. </summary>
public static ILeafParser FindParser(TokenPeeker peeker){foreach(var parser in _parsers){if(parser.CanParse(peeker))return parser;}return null;}}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Parsing{/// <summary> Read-only view of upcoming tokens used by <see cref="ILeafParser.CanParse"/> and <see cref="ILeafParser.Parse"/>. Wraps a <see cref="ConditionParser.Token"/> list and position index. Peek methods do not advance — only <see cref="Advance"/> consumes. Also carries the <paramref name="parseSubExpr"/> callback injected by <see cref="ExpressionParser"/> so that leaf parsers can recursively parse sub-expressions (e.g. inside parentheses). </summary>
public class TokenPeeker{private readonly List<ConditionParser.Token>_tokens;private int _pos;private readonly Func<ICondition>_parseSubExpr;/// <summary>Creates a peeker over a token list.</summary> <param name="tokens">Full token list produced by <see cref="ConditionParser"/>.</param> <param name="parseSubExpr">Callback for recursively parsing parenthesised sub-expressions; may be null for CanParse-only use.</param>
public TokenPeeker(List<ConditionParser.Token>tokens,Func<ICondition>parseSubExpr){_tokens=tokens;_pos=0;_parseSubExpr=parseSubExpr;}/// <summary>The token at the current position (EOF token when the list is exhausted).</summary>
public ConditionParser.Token Peek=>_tokens[_pos];/// <summary>True when the position moved past the last token.</summary>
public bool AtEnd=>_pos>=_tokens.Count;/// <summary>Returns the token <paramref name="offset"/> positions ahead without consuming; clamps to the EOF token past the end.</summary>
public ConditionParser.Token PeekAhead(int offset){var idx=_pos+offset;return idx<_tokens.Count?_tokens[idx]:_tokens[_tokens.Count-1];}/// <summary>True when the current token has the expected type (never matches at end of input).</summary>
public bool Check(ConditionParser.TokenType type)=> !AtEnd&&Peek.Type==type;/// <summary>Consumes and returns the current token, moving the position forward.</summary>
public ConditionParser.Token Advance(){var token=Peek;_pos++;return token;}/// <summary>Consumes the current token when it matches, otherwise throws with a parser error message.</summary>
public ConditionParser.Token Expect(ConditionParser.TokenType type,string errorMsg){if(AtEnd||Peek.Type!=type)throw new FormatException($"Condition parse error: {errorMsg}, got '{(AtEnd ? "EOF" : Peek.Value)}'");return Advance();}/// <summary>Clones the position for speculative CanParse checks.</summary>
public TokenPeeker Snapshot(){var clone=new TokenPeeker(_tokens,_parseSubExpr);clone._pos=_pos;return clone;}/// <summary>Parses a sub-expression using the injected callback.</summary>
public ICondition ParseSubExpr()=>_parseSubExpr();}}

using System;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Patching{/// <summary> One entry of the <c>_patch_remove_connections</c> list. A selector is a set of <c>key=value</c> pairs joined with <c>;</c> — <c>from</c>, <c>to</c>, <c>signal</c>, <c>method</c> and <c>flags</c> are recognised. Omitted fields are wildcards, which lets a patch remove a connection by target (<c>to=</c>), by signal alone, or by any combination. At least <c>signal</c> and one of <c>from</c>/<c>to</c> are required: with neither, the selector could silently remove every connection of the scene. </summary>
public class ConnectionSelector{/// <summary>Source node path (empty = wildcard).</summary>
public string From{get;set;}/// <summary>Target node path (empty = wildcard).</summary>
public string To{get;set;}/// <summary>Signal name (required by <see cref="TryParse"/>).</summary>
public string Signal{get;set;}/// <summary>Method name (empty = wildcard).</summary>
public string Method{get;set;}/// <summary>Connection flags (null = wildcard).</summary>
public int?Flags{get;set;}/// <summary> Parses one selector string. Returns false with a human-readable <paramref name="error"/> for unknown keys, malformed flags, or a missing signal/source pair so the applier can log and skip instead of removing too much. </summary>
public static bool TryParse(string text,out ConnectionSelector selector,out string error){selector=null;error=null;if(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(text)){error="selector is empty";return false;}var result=new ConnectionSelector();foreach(var rawPart in text.Split(';')){var part=rawPart.Trim();if(part.Length==0)continue;var eq=part.IndexOf('=');if(eq<=0){error=$"selector part '{part}' is not key=value";return false;}var key=part.Substring(0,eq).Trim().ToLowerInvariant();var value=part.Substring(eq+1).Trim();if(value.Length==0){error=$"selector key '{key}' has an empty value";return false;}switch(key){case"from":result.From=value;break;case"to":result.To=value;break;case"signal":result.Signal=value;break;case"method":result.Method=value;break;case"flags":if(!int.TryParse(value,out var flags)){error=$"selector flags '{value}' is not an integer";return false;}result.Flags=flags;break;default:error=$"unknown selector key '{key}'";return false;}}if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(result.Signal)){error="selector requires 'signal'";return false;}if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(result.From)&&string.IsNullOrEmpty(result.To)){error="selector requires 'from' or 'to'";return false;}selector=result;return true;}/// <summary>True when every specified field equals the connection's field.</summary>
public bool Matches(ParsedConnection connection){if(connection==null)return false;if(From!=null&& !string.Equals(From,connection.From,StringComparison.Ordinal))return false;if(To!=null&& !string.Equals(To,connection.To,StringComparison.Ordinal))return false;if(Signal!=null&& !string.Equals(Signal,connection.Signal,StringComparison.Ordinal))return false;if(Method!=null&& !string.Equals(Method,connection.Method,StringComparison.Ordinal))return false;if(Flags.HasValue&&Flags.Value!=connection.Flags)return false;return true;}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Patching{/// <summary> Case-sensitive glob matcher used by scene-patch masks (<c>_patch_delete_nodes</c>, <c>_patch_remove</c>). <c>*</c> matches any run of characters including <c>/</c> (so a node mask can span hierarchy levels), <c>?</c> matches exactly one character. The engine has no general-purpose wildcard helper, and this is deliberately tiny: an iterative two-pointer matcher with backtracking avoids regex compilation per key on the scene-load hot path. </summary>
public static class MaskMatcher{/// <summary> True when <paramref name="value"/> matches the glob <paramref name="pattern"/>. Null/empty patterns never match; a pattern without wildcards is an exact comparison. </summary>
public static bool IsMatch(string pattern,string value){if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(pattern)||value==null)return false;var p=0;var v=0;var star= -1;var mark=0;while(v<value.Length){if(p<pattern.Length&&(pattern[p]=='?'||pattern[p]==value[v])){p++;v++;continue;}if(p<pattern.Length&&pattern[p]=='*'){star=p;mark=v;p++;continue;}if(star>=0){p=star+1;v= ++mark;continue;}return false;}while(p<pattern.Length&&pattern[p]=='*')p++;return p==pattern.Length;}/// <summary>True when the text contains at least one wildcard character.</summary>
public static bool HasMask(string text){if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(text))return false;for(var i=0;i<text.Length;i++){if(text[i]=='*'||text[i]=='?')return true;}return false;}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Patching{/// <summary> Reserved <c>metadata/_patch_*</c> property keys consumed by <see cref="ScenePatchApplier"/>. A scene patch is a normal Godot inherited scene, so every operation Godot can express (property overrides, added nodes, sibling order, groups, resources, connections) is written natively; only operations inheritance cannot express — deleting nodes, deleting inherited properties, mask-based bulk edits, resource GC — are encoded as these metadata markers. <para/> The keys are stripped from the parsed scene before it reaches <see cref="TscnBuild.SceneBuilder"/>, so they never become Godot node metadata. The whole <c>metadata/_patch_*</c> namespace is reserved: a regular mod using such keys for its own metadata will conflict. </summary>
public static class PatchMetadata{/// <summary>Prefix of every reserved key.</summary>
public const string Prefix="metadata/_patch_";/// <summary>Bool on an override node or sub_resource body: remove the target node/sub_resource (nodes cascade to descendants, connections and node-path bindings).</summary>
public const string Delete=Prefix+"delete";/// <summary>String or string list on an override node: delete matching target properties (glob masks, <c>"*"</c> = all).</summary>
public const string Remove=Prefix+"remove";/// <summary>String list on an override node: add groups to the target node.</summary>
public const string AddGroups=Prefix+"add_groups";/// <summary>String list on an override node: remove groups from the target node.</summary>
public const string RemoveGroups=Prefix+"remove_groups";/// <summary>String list on the patch root: delete target nodes by path masks (paths are relative to the root, e.g. <c>MenuContainer/*Btn</c>; the root itself is never matched).</summary>
public const string DeleteNodes=Prefix+"delete_nodes";/// <summary>String list on the patch root: connection selectors (<c>from=...;signal=...;method=...</c>) removing every matching connection.</summary>
public const string RemoveConnections=Prefix+"remove_connections";/// <summary>String list on the patch root: ids of ext_resources to remove when nothing references them anymore.</summary>
public const string RemoveExtResources=Prefix+"remove_ext_resources";/// <summary>Bool on the patch root: run resource garbage collection once after all layers have been applied.</summary>
public const string Gc=Prefix+"gc";}}

The target <see cref="ParsedScene"/> is mutated in place and is expected to already contain the results of previous layers, which is what makes the mod load order a cascade. <para/> <b>Layer order:</b> reserved-key extraction → resource merge/remap → deletions with cascade → overrides → additions → index re-sort → connections → resource removals. patch in patches){var layer=CloneScene(patch.Scene);if(!ApplyLayer(target,layer,patch,out var layerGc))ok=false;gcRequested|=layerGc;}if(gcRequested)CollectGarbage(target);return ok;}private bool ApplyLayer(ParsedScene target,ParsedScene layer,ScenePatch patch,out bool gcRequested){gcRequested=false;var nodeOps=new Dictionary<ParsedNode,NodePatchOperations>();foreach(var node in layer.Nodes)ExtractOperations(node,nodeOps,ref gcRequested);var subDeletes=new List<SubResourceDef>();foreach(var sub in layer.SubResources){if(TakeBool(sub,PatchMetadata.Delete))subDeletes.Add(sub);}if(nodeOps.TryGetValue(root,out var rootOps)&&rootOps.Delete){GameLogger.Log(LogCategory,$"ScenePatchApplier: patch '{patch.SourcePath}' tries to delete the scene root — layer rejected",LogLevel.Error);return false;}var extMap=MergeExtResources(target,layer,patch.TargetExtResourceId);var subMap=MergeSubResources(target,layer,subDeletes);RemapLayerReferences(layer,extMap,subMap);var exactDeletes=nodeOps.Where(kv=>kv.Value.Delete).Select(kv=>NodePathOf(kv.Key)).ToList();var maskDeletes=rootOps?.DeleteNodes??new List<string>();var targetMap=BuildPathMap(target);foreach(var node in layer.Nodes){if(ReferenceEquals(node,root))continue;nodeOps.TryGetValue(node,out var ops);ops??=new NodePatchOperations();if(ops.Delete)continue;var path=NodePathOf(node);var isAddition= !string.IsNullOrEmpty(node.Type)|| skipped",LogLevel.Warning);continue;}target.Nodes.Add(node);targetMap[path]=node;continue;}if(MaskMatcher.HasMask(path)){GameLogger.Log(LogCategory,$"ScenePatchApplier: node selector '{path}' uses a targetRoot=target.Nodes.FirstOrDefault(n=>n.Parent==null);if(targetRoot!=null)ApplyOverride(targetRoot,root,rootOps??new NodePatchOperations());ReorderByIndex(target);ApplyConnections(target,rootOps,layer,patch.SourcePath);RemoveResources(target,rootOps,subDeletes);if(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(layer.EntryPointClass))target.EntryPointClass=layer.EntryPointClass;return using System.Text;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Patching{/// <summary> Minimal scene-patch debugging aid: renders the effective scene — the result after all patch layers were applied — as text and writes it through <see cref="GameLogger"/>. Patch layers are invisible in the Godot editor (each patch sees only the base scene), so when a mash-up of several mods behaves unexpectedly this dump is the ground truth for what the builder will actually receive. <see cref="Format"/> is pure and reused by tests. </summary>
public static class ScenePatchDebug{private const string LogCategory="TSCN";/// <summary>Formats the effective scene as an indented node tree plus resources and connections.</summary>
public static string Format(ParsedScene scene){if(scene==null)return"<null scene>";var sb=new StringBuilder();sb.AppendLine($"scene: format={scene.Format ?? "?"}, entry_point={scene.EntryPointClass ?? "none"}");sb.AppendLine($"nodes ({scene.Nodes.Count}):");foreach(var node in scene.Nodes){var path=NodePathOf(node);var kind= !string.IsNullOrEmpty(node.InstanceRef)?$"instance={node.InstanceRef}":$"type={node.Type ?? "?"}";sb.Append("  ").Append(path.Length==0?"<root>":path).Append(" [").Append(kind);if(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(node.ScriptRef))sb.Append(", script=").Append(node.ScriptRef);if(node.Index.HasValue)sb.Append(", index=").Append(node.Index.Value);sb.AppendLine("]");foreach(var key in node.PropertyOrder)sb.Append("      ").Append(key).Append(" = ").AppendLine(Describe(node.Properties.TryGetValue(key,out var v)?v:null));if(node.Groups is{Length:>0})sb.Append("      groups = [").Append(string.Join(", ",node.Groups)).AppendLine("]");}sb.AppendLine($"ext_resources ({scene.ExtResources.Count}):");foreach(var ext in scene.ExtResources)sb.Append("  ").Append(ext.Id).Append(" -> ").Append(ext.Type).Append(' ').AppendLine(ext.Path);sb.AppendLine($"sub_resources ({scene.SubResources.Count}):");foreach(var sub in scene.SubResources)sb.Append("  ").Append(sub.Id).Append(" : ").AppendLine(sub.Type);sb.AppendLine($"connections ({scene.Connections.Count}):");foreach(var conn in scene.Connections)sb.Append("  ").Append(conn.From).Append('.').Append(conn.Signal).Append(" -> ").Append(conn.To).Append('.').AppendLine(conn.Method);return sb.ToString().TrimEnd();}/// <summary>Logs the effective scene under a label; no-op-safe outside the runtime.</summary>

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using System.Linq;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Patching{/// <summary> Parses patch text into a <see cref="ScenePatch"/>. A patch is a regular .tscn file parsed by the same <see cref="TscnParser"/> as any scene; the only extra contract is the root node: it must carry an <c>instance=ExtResource(...)</c> reference to a <c>PackedScene</c> ext_resource, which is simultaneously the patch header, the editor's inherited-scene marker and the machine-readable target. Files without that shape are not patches (they may be ordinary scenes that happen to live under patches/scenes). </summary>
public static class ScenePatchParser{/// <summary> Parses <paramref name="text"/>. Returns false with a diagnostic <paramref name="error"/> when the file is not a valid patch. </summary>
public static bool TryParse(string text,string modId,string sourcePath,out ScenePatch patch,out string error){patch=null;error=null;if(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(text)){error="patch file is empty";return false;}ParsedScene scene;try{scene=new TscnParser().Parse(text);}catch(Exception ex){error=$"parse failed: {ex.Message}";return false;}var root=scene.Nodes.FirstOrDefault(n=>n.Parent==null);if(root==null){error="patch has no root node";return false;}if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(root.InstanceRef)){error="patch root must instance the target scene (instance=ExtResource(...))";return false;}var refId=ExtractResourceId(root.InstanceRef);var ext=scene.ExtResources.FirstOrDefault(e=>string.Equals(e.Id,refId,StringComparison.Ordinal));if(ext==null){error=$"root instance references unknown ext_resource '{refId}'";return false;}if(!string.Equals(ext.Type,"PackedScene",StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)){error=$"root instance must reference a PackedScene, got '{ext.Type}'";return false;}var target=ScenePatchTargetResolver.Normalize(ext.Path);if(target.Length==0){error="target scene path is empty";return false;}patch=new ScenePatch{ModId=modId,SourcePath=sourcePath,TargetPath=target,TargetExtResourceId=ext.Id,Scene=scene};return true;}/// <summary> Extracts the local id from an <c>ExtResource("id")</c> value. Returns the raw trimmed string when the value has no wrapper so malformed input still produces a readable lookup error. </summary>
private static string ExtractResourceId(string refString){if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(refString))return null;const string prefix="ExtResource(";var start=refString.IndexOf(prefix,StringComparison.Ordinal);if(start<0)return refString.Trim('"');start+=prefix.Length;var end=refString.IndexOf(')',start);if(end<0)return refString.Trim('"');return refString.Substring(start,end-start).Trim().Trim('"');}}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using System.Linq;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;using Cthangover.Core.Mods.Resolvers;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Patching{/// <summary> Discovers and caches scene patches from every loaded mod. Patch files live under <c>patches/scenes/</c> (recursively) and are grouped by the canonical target key they declare in their inherited-scene header; within one mod files apply in path order, across mods in load order, so the returned layer list is exactly the cascade <see cref="ScenePatchApplier"/> expects. <para/> Registered as the <c>"scene_patches"</c> resolver. Unlike JSON patches the key is not an entity kind but the target scene path, because a patch already names its base scene. </summary>
public class ScenePatchResolver:ModAssetResolver{/// <inheritdoc />
public override string Id=>"scene_patches";/// <summary>Directory scanned inside every mod, recursively.</summary>
public const string PatchDirectory="patches/scenes";private Dictionary<string,List<ScenePatch>>_cache;/// <summary> Collects every patch from every loaded mod, keyed by canonical target scene path. Cached until <see cref="ClearCache"/>; later mods append to a key's layer list. </summary>
public Dictionary<string,List<ScenePatch>>Collect(){Context.Initialize();if(_cache!=null)return _cache;var sources=new List<(string ModId,IModFileProvider Provider)>();foreach(var modId in Context.GetOrderedModIds()){var provider=Context.GetMod(modId)?.FileProvider;if(provider!=null)sources.Add((modId,provider));}_cache=CollectFromProviders(sources);if(_cache.Count>0)GameLogger.Log("TSCN",$"ScenePatchResolver: collected {_cache.Sum(kv => kv.Value.Count)} patch(es) for {_cache.Count} scene(s)");return _cache;}/// <summary> All layers targeting <paramref name="sceneKey"/>, in application order. Returns an empty list for a scene without patches so callers can treat "no patches" uniformly. </summary>
public List<ScenePatch>GetPatches(string sceneKey){if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(sceneKey))return new List<ScenePatch>();var result=new List<ScenePatch>();foreach(var kvp in Collect()){if(ScenePatchTargetResolver.MatchesSceneKey(sceneKey,kvp.Key))result.AddRange(kvp.Value);}return result;}/// <summary>True when at least one mod patches the scene.</summary>
public bool HasPatches(string sceneKey)=>GetPatches(sceneKey).Count>0;/// <inheritdoc />
public override void ClearCache(){_cache=null;}/// <summary> Testable collection core: walks each provider's <c>patches/scenes</c> tree in the given order (mod load order), sorts files inside one mod for determinism, and parses every <c>.tscn</c>. Invalid files are logged and skipped so one bad patch cannot break scene loading. </summary>
public static Dictionary<string,List<ScenePatch>>CollectFromProviders(IEnumerable<(string ModId,IModFileProvider Provider)>sources){var result=new Dictionary<string,List<ScenePatch>>(StringComparer.Ordinal);foreach(var(modId,provider)in sources){var files=new List<string>();CollectPatchFiles(provider,PatchDirectory,files);files.Sort(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);foreach(var file in files){if(!file.EndsWith(".tscn",StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))continue;var text=provider.ReadFileText(file);if(!ScenePatchParser.TryParse(text,modId,file,out var patch,out var error)){GameLogger.Log("TSCN",$"ScenePatchResolver: '{modId}/{file}' is not a valid scene patch: {error}",LogLevel.Error);continue;}if(!result.TryGetValue(patch.TargetPath,out var list)){list=new List<ScenePatch>();result[patch.TargetPath]=list;}list.Add(patch);}}return result;}private static void CollectPatchFiles(IModFileProvider provider,string directory,List<string>result){foreach(var entry in provider.ListFiles(directory)){if(entry.EndsWith("/")){CollectPatchFiles(provider,entry.TrimEnd('/'),result);continue;}var prefix=ModPath.NormalizeDirectory(PatchDirectory);if(entry.StartsWith(prefix,StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))result.Add(entry);}}}}

===== FILE Core/Scenes/Patching/ScenePatchTargetResolver.cs =====
using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.Patching{/// <summary> Translates the target path a patch declares in its <c>[ext_resource type="PackedScene"]</c> header into the canonical scene key used by <see cref="TscnSceneResolver"/>. <para/> Three spellings denote the same scene: the resolver key (<c>scenes/menu/main_menu.tscn</c>), the native form (<c>res://scenes/menu/main_menu.tscn</c>) and the on-disk form of a mod scene (<c>res://mods/&lt;mod&gt;/scenes/menu/main_menu.tscn</c>, which is what the Godot editor writes when the mod lives inside the project). Normalisation strips the scheme and the <c>mods/&lt;mod&gt;/</c> prefix; the resolver then matches by suffix against the collected scene index so a patch works regardless of which mod won the override. </summary>
public static class ScenePatchTargetResolver{/// <summary> Converts a declared target path into canonical mod-relative form: forward slashes, no <c>res://</c> scheme, no leading slash, and no <c>mods/&lt;mod&gt;/</c> prefix. Returns an empty string for null/empty input. </summary>
public static string Normalize(string declaredPath){if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(declaredPath))return"";var path=declaredPath.Replace('\\','/');if(path.StartsWith("res://",StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))path=path.Substring("res://".Length);path=path.TrimStart('/');var segments=path.Split('/');if(segments.Length>=3&&segments[0].Equals("mods",StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))path=string.Join("/",segments,2,segments.Length-2);return ModPath.Normalize(path);}/// <summary> True when a patch targeting <paramref name="declaredPath"/> applies to the scene registered under <paramref name="sceneKey"/>. Exact match, or the declared path ends with the scene key (covers extra prefixes the normaliser did not strip). </summary>
public static bool MatchesSceneKey(string sceneKey,string declaredPath){if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(sceneKey)||string.IsNullOrEmpty(declaredPath))return false;var normalized=Normalize(declaredPath);if(normalized.Length==0)return false;if(string.Equals(normalized,sceneKey,StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))return true;return normalized.EndsWith("/"+sceneKey,StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);}/// <summary> Picks the winning scene key for a declared target from the collected scene index. Exact matches win over suffix matches, mirroring how <c>TscnSceneResolver</c> resolves override conflicts (the index itself already holds one entry per key). </summary>
public static string Resolve(string declaredPath,IEnumerable<string>availableKeys){var normalized=Normalize(declaredPath);if(normalized.Length==0||availableKeys==null)return null;string suffixMatch=null;foreach(var key in availableKeys){if(key==null)continue;if(string.Equals(key,normalized,StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))return key;if(suffixMatch==null&&normalized.EndsWith("/"+key,StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))suffixMatch=key;}return suffixMatch;}}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Events;using Cthangover.Core.Quests;using Cthangover.Core.Settings;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes{/// <summary> Evaluates condition expression strings by parsing them into an AST via <see cref="ConditionParser"/> and walking the tree polymorphically — each <see cref="ConditionNode"/> subclass implements its own <see cref="ConditionNode.Evaluate"/> method. Story flags are game state (<see cref="RuntimeData.Flags"/>, saved and reset with the game); they are set via <see cref="SetFlag"/> and injected (along with the quest service) into an <see cref="EvaluationContext"/> carried through the AST walk. Outside a running game (tests, tools) a detached flag set stands in. The polymorphic design means that a mod assembly can define a custom <see cref="ConditionNode"/> and it will be evaluated automatically when present in the AST — no dispatch table, no switch, no registration. </summary>
public static class ScenarioCondition{private static readonly Dictionary<string,string>DetachedFlags=new();private static Dictionary<string,string>Flags=>GameEnvironment.IsRuntime&&GameData.Instance is{}data?data.Runtime.Flags:DetachedFlags;private static readonly Dictionary<string,ConditionNode>AstCache=new();private static readonly object AstLock=new();private static readonly EvaluationContext evalCtx=new();/// <summary> Sets a story flag of the running game (the scenario <c>flag</c> command uses it) so later <see cref="Evaluate"/> calls see it. Publishes a <see cref="FlagChangedEvent"/> only when the value actually changed (setting the same value is a no-op); <see cref="ConditionStateMonitor"/> turns it into a condition rescan, so a waiting scenario can start. </summary> <param name="key">The flag name.</param> <param name="value">The flag value, which may be parsed as integer for numeric comparisons.</param>
public static void SetFlag(string key,string value){var flags=Flags;if(flags.TryGetValue(key,out var current)&&current==value)return;flags[key]=value;ModEventBus.Publish(new FlagChangedEvent{Key=key,Value=value});}/// <summary> Parses and evaluates a condition expression string. Returns <c>true</c> for null or whitespace-only input (vacuous truth). Returns <c>false</c> on parse errors. Supports boolean combinators (<c>&amp;&amp;</c>, <c>||</c>, <c>!</c>), numeric comparisons on flags and quest properties, quest tag membership checks (<c>hasTag</c>, <c>notHasTag</c>), and boolean literals (<c>true</c>, <c>false</c>). The parsed AST is cached per unique condition string (the tree and its static inputs are immutable), while execution still reads live flag and quest state at evaluation time. Parse errors are not cached and re-parse (and fail) on every call. </summary> <param name="condition">The condition expression string to evaluate.</param>
public static bool Evaluate(string condition){if(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(condition))return true;ConditionNode ast;lock(AstLock){if(!AstCache.TryGetValue(condition,out ast)){try{ast=ConditionParser.Parse(condition);}catch(FormatException ex){GameLogger.Log("COND",$"parse error: {ex.Message}",LogLevel.Error);return false;}if(ast==null)return true;AstCache[condition]=ast;}}evalCtx.Flags=Flags;evalCtx.QuestFactory=QuestServiceRegistry.Provider;return ast.Evaluate(evalCtx);}/// <summary> Forgets every cached AST. Leaves of a tree may be nodes of a mod's own leaf parser (quest checks come from <c>quests_base</c>), so a cached tree pins that mod's assembly; when the mod unloads, the unload sweep nulls those references and the cached tree would throw on the next evaluation. Called from <c>ScenarioConditionCacheConsumer</c> before any mod assembly unloads; the next <see cref="Evaluate"/> re-parses with the parsers registered at that moment. </summary>
public static void ClearCache(){lock(AstLock)AstCache.Clear();}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes{/// <summary> Represents a parsed .scenario file entry from a mod manifest. Maps a visual novel scenario script to a target scene with scheduling metadata, condition expressions, and save/permanence flags. Collections of these definitions are built by <see cref="ModManager.CollectScenarioDefinitions"/> and consumed in <see cref="SceneManager.ComposeEvents"/> to produce <see cref="SceneEventInfo"/> entries for the event queue. </summary>
public class ScenarioDefinition{/// <summary> The display name of the scenario, also used as the unique event identifier within its scene. </summary>
public string Name{get;set;}/// <summary> The scene identifier that this scenario is associated with. </summary>
public string Scene{get;set;}/// <summary> Execution priority; lower values execute earlier. Ties are broken by identifier ordering. </summary>
public int Priority{get;set;}/// <summary> The identifier of another event that must execute before this one, enabling topological ordering within a scene's event list. </summary>
public string After{get;set;}/// <summary> A condition expression string parsed by <see cref="ConditionParser"/> and evaluated by <see cref="ScenarioCondition.Evaluate"/>. The event is skipped if the condition evaluates to <c>false</c>. </summary>
public string Condition{get;set;}/// <summary> When set, overrides whether the in-game light clock (time-of-day) progresses during this scenario. <c>null</c> means default behavior. </summary>
public bool?LightUseTime{get;set;}/// <summary> When <c>true</c>, the player is allowed to save during this scenario. </summary>
public bool SaveAllowed{get;set;}/// <summary> When <c>true</c>, this scenario is marked as completed after its first execution and will be filtered out on subsequent scene entries. </summary>
public bool IsOneRun{get;set;}/// <summary> The identifier of the mod that provides this scenario definition. </summary>
public string ModId{get;set;}/// <summary> The file system path to the .scenario file containing the scenario script text. </summary>
public string FilePath{get;set;}}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Events;using Cthangover.Core.Interactive;using Cthangover.Core.UI.Executable;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes{/// <summary> Persistent autoload-style singleton node that caches scene-tree node lookups and manages interactive event objects. Automatically detects Godot scene changes (via <see cref="_Process"/>) and clears all cached references, ensuring stale nodes are never returned. Provides static helpers like <see cref="FindNode{T}"/> for convenience access throughout the codebase. The singleton instance is set during <see cref="_Ready"/> and cleared on <see cref="_ExitTree"/>. </summary>
public partial class SceneContextNode:Node{/// <summary> The singleton instance of <see cref="SceneContextNode"/>. Only one instance is allowed; duplicates log an error and self-disable. </summary>
public static SceneContextNode Instance{get;set;}/// <summary> Tracks the most recently applied background texture ID, used by save/restore flows and lazy reload logic in <see cref="SceneManager"/>. </summary>
public static string LastBackgroundID{get;set;}/// <summary> Returns the root node of the currently active Godot scene, or <c>null</c> if no scene tree is available. </summary>
public static Node CurrentScene=>Instance?.GetTree()?.CurrentScene;private Dictionary<string,object>data=new();private Dictionary<string,IEventObject>eventObjects=new();private HashSet<string>notFoundCache=new();/// <summary>Claims the singleton (duplicates log an error and stay inert), enables always-on processing, and subscribes cache clearing to <see cref="SceneExitedEvent"/>. The interactive subsystem lifecycle lives in the interactive_base engine mod (InteractiveModInitializer).</summary>
public override void _Ready(){if(Instance!=null&&GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(Instance)){var scene=GetTree()?.CurrentScene?.Name??"?";var existingPath=Instance.GetPath().ToString();var myPath=GetPath().ToString();GameLogger.Log("DUPLICATE",$"SceneContextNode._Ready: Instance ALREADY SET by '{existingPath}', ignoring duplicate at '{myPath}' on scene '{scene}'",LogLevel.Error);return;}Instance=this;ProcessMode=ProcessModeEnum.Always;ModEventBus.Subscribe<SceneExitedEvent>(_=>ClearData());}/// <summary>Releases the singleton reference when the node leaves the tree.</summary>
public override void _ExitTree(){if(Instance==this)Instance=null;}/// <summary> Destroys all tracked interactive event objects via <see cref="IEventObject.Destruct"/>, and clears the node-lookup cache and the not-found cache. The interactive subsystem's own scene-exit teardown is wired by the interactive_base engine mod (InteractiveModInitializer). Called automatically when the active Godot scene changes. </summary>
public void ClearData(){GameLogger.Log("SCENE_CTX",$"ClearData: data={data.Count}, notFoundCache={notFoundCache.Count}, eventObjects={eventObjects.Count}");data.Clear();if(Lists.IsNotEmpty(eventObjects)){foreach(var entry in eventObjects)entry.Value.Destruct();eventObjects.Clear();}notFoundCache.Clear();}/// <summary> Statically searches the entire scene tree for a node by name and type, using the singleton instance's <see cref="GetSafeNode{T}"/>. Returns <c>null</c> if the instance is unavailable or the node is not found. </summary> <typeparam name="T">The expected Godot <see cref="Node"/> type.</typeparam> <param name="nodeName">The name of the node to find.</param>
public static T FindNode<T>(string nodeName)where T:Node{if(Instance==null|| !GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(Instance))return null;return Instance.GetSafeNode<T>(nodeName);}/// <summary> Resolves the first node in a Godot group, caching the result in the internal data dictionary. Re-checks on scene change and validates the cached Godot object reference to avoid returning disposed nodes. </summary> <typeparam name="T">The expected Godot <see cref="Node"/> type.</typeparam> <param name="groupName">The Godot group name to query.</param>
public T GetSceneRoot<T>(string groupName)where T:Node{if(data.TryGetValue(groupName,out var value)&&value!=null){if(value is GodotObject go&&GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(go))return value as T;data.Remove(groupName);}var nodes=GetTree().GetNodesInGroup(groupName);if(nodes.Count>0){var v=nodes[0]as T;data[groupName]=v;return v;}GameLogger.Log("SCENE",$"object with group '{groupName}' not found",LogLevel.Error);return null;}/// <summary> Performs a cached recursive node lookup through the scene tree root. On first call for a given name, searches the tree via <see cref="Node.FindChild"/> and caches the result. Subsequent calls return the cached reference after validating it is still a valid Godot object. Failed lookups are stored in a not-found cache to avoid repeated searches within the same scene lifecycle. A lookup is typed: the miss is cached per type and name, and a cached node of another type is a miss for <typeparamref name="T"/> — one caller asking for the wrong type must not hide the node from the others (the same name is looked up as <c>ViewBox</c>, <c>Control</c> and <c>Node</c>). </summary> <typeparam name="T">The expected Godot <see cref="Node"/> type.</typeparam> <param name="nodeName">The name of the node to find.</param>
public T GetSafeNode<T>(string nodeName)where T:Node{if(data.TryGetValue(nodeName,out var value)&&value!=null){if(value is GodotObject go&&GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(go))return value as T;data.Remove(nodeName);}var missKey=typeof(T).FullName+":"+nodeName;if(notFoundCache.Contains(missKey))return null;var tree=GetTree();var root=tree?.Root;if(root==null){GameLogger.Log("SCENE_CTX",$"GetSafeNode<{typeof(T).Name}>('{nodeName}') -> root is NULL (tree={(tree != null ? "exists" : "NULL")})",LogLevel.Error);return null;}GameLogger.Log("SCENE_CTX",$"GetSafeNode<{typeof(T).Name}>('{nodeName}') -> searching tree (root children={root.GetChildCount()}, CurrentScene={tree.CurrentScene?.Name ?? "NULL"})",LogLevel.Debug);T v=root.FindChild(nodeName,true,false)as T;if(v==null){notFoundCache.Add(missKey);GameLogger.Log("SCENE",$"node '{nodeName}' of type {typeof(T).Name} not found",LogLevel.Error);return null;}GameLogger.Log("SCENE_CTX",$"GetSafeNode<{typeof(T).Name}>('{nodeName}') -> FOUND and cached (parent={v.GetParent()?.Name ?? "NULL"})",LogLevel.Debug);data[nodeName]=v;return v;}/// <summary> Destroys and removes a tracked interactive event object by its identifier. Calls <see cref="IEventObject.Destruct"/> before removal. </summary> <param name="id">The unique identifier of the event object to remove.</param>
public void RemoveEventObject(string id){if(eventObjects.TryGetValue(id,out var obj))obj.Destruct();eventObjects.Remove(id);}/// <summary> Removes any entries from the event object dictionary whose values have become <c>null</c>, preventing accumulation of garbage entries. </summary>
public void OptimizeEventObjects(){var keysToRemove=new List<string>();foreach(var pair in eventObjects)if(pair.Value==null)keysToRemove.Add(pair.Key);foreach(var key in keysToRemove)eventObjects.Remove(key);}}}

public class SceneEventRegistry:IGameRegistry{private readonly Dictionary<string,List<SceneEventInfo>>events=new();private bool built;/// <summary> Factory for scenario-backed executable events, published by the dialog_base engine mod on load. SceneManager builds inline scenario events through it; null until the dialog mod registers its factory. </summary>
public IScenarioEventFactory ScenarioEventFactory{get;set;}/// <summary>Shared instance the static facade delegates to.</summary>
private static SceneEventRegistry Owned=>AppServices.Current.SceneEvents;/// <summary> Creates an empty registry: cheap and side-effect free per the IGameRegistry contract. <see cref="Rebuild"/> fills the data. </summary>
internal SceneEventRegistry(){}/// <inheritdoc />
public string Id=>"scene_events";/// <summary> Re-scans all loaded assemblies for <see cref="ExecutableEvent"/> types decorated with <see cref="SceneEventAttribute"/>, replacing the previous table. Forced: safe to call repeatedly. Events registered imperatively (by mod initializers) must re-register afterwards. </summary>
public void Rebuild(){lock(events){events.Clear();RegisterFromAttributes();built=true;}}/// <summary> Drops all registered events; the next build re-scans the assemblies. Called on mod reload through AppServices.ClearRegistries. </summary>
public void Clear(){lock(events){events.Clear();built=false;}}/// <summary> Scans all loaded assemblies for <see cref="ExecutableEvent"/> types decorated with <see cref="SceneEventAttribute"/> and registers them in the event table. Uses double-checked locking for thread safety; keeps the old Initialize idempotence — subsequent calls are no-ops. </summary>
public void EnsureBuilt(){if(built)return;lock(events){if(built)return;RegisterFromAttributes();built=true;}}// ---- Static facade (legacy API, unchanged for callers) ------------ <summary>Legacy entry point; delegates to the shared instance.</summary>
public static void Initialize()=>Owned.EnsureBuilt();/// <summary> Registers a specific <see cref="ExecutableEvent"/> subclass for a scene with optional priority, dependency, and condition parameters. </summary> <typeparam name="T">The <see cref="ExecutableEvent"/> subclass to register.</typeparam> <param name="sceneName">The scene identifier to associate the event with.</param> <param name="priority">Execution priority (lower = earlier). Default 0.</param> <param name="after">Identifier of an event that must precede this one.</param> <param name="condition">Condition expression string evaluated at runtime.</param>
public static void Register<T>(string sceneName,int priority=0,string after=null,string condition=null)where T:class=>Owned.AddEvent(typeof(T),sceneName,priority,after,condition);/// <summary> Non-generic variant of <see cref="Register{T}"/> that accepts a <see cref="Type"/> directly. using System;using System.Linq;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes{/// <summary> Parses the first-class <c>--scene=&lt;logical&gt;</c> launch flag from Godot user arguments (everything after <c>--</c> on the command line). The flag is a core navigation feature, not a test hook: when present, the launcher boots the mod pipeline as usual and then jumps straight into the requested mod-defined scene instead of showing the launcher UI or the main menu. Only logical scene names (resolved through <see cref="SceneManager"/>) are accepted — a raw <c>.tscn</c> path can already be passed to Godot natively as the boot scene. Kept separate from <see cref="SceneManager"/> so argument parsing stays independent of the autoload lifecycle and is trivially reusable by any future entry point. </summary>
public static class SceneLaunchArgs{/// <summary> Returns the logical scene name requested via <c>--scene=&lt;id&gt;</c>, or null when the flag is absent or empty. Only the first occurrence wins; repeated flags are ignored. Guarded by <see cref="GameEnvironment.IsRuntime"/> because <c>OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs()</c> is a Godot API that must not be touched from pure test environments. </summary>
public static string RequestedSceneName(){if(!GameEnvironment.IsRuntime)return null;return OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs().Where(a=>a.StartsWith("--scene=",StringComparison.Ordinal)).Select(a=>a.Substring("--scene=".Length).Trim()).FirstOrDefault(id=> !string.IsNullOrEmpty(id));}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Audio;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes{/// <summary> Declaration of a mod-provided scene route. public bool Fade{get;set;}/// <summary>Scene name passed to playlist resolution; <c>null</c> keeps the current playlist.</summary>
public string MusicScene{get;set;}/// <summary>Music bucket to switch to when the route is entered.</summary>

using System.Linq;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnBuild.PropertyResolvers{/// <summary> Resolves <c>ExtResource("id")</c> properties. public class ExtResourcePropertyResolver:IPropertyResolver{/// <summary>Claims every property whose value is an <c>ExtResource(...)</c> reference.</summary>
public bool CanResolve(string k,object v)=>v is TscnPropertyValue pv&&pv.IsExtResourceRef;/// <summary>PackedScene refs are built recursively and packed; other types go through the fallback resource resolver. Script refs on already-created nodes are ignored.</summary>
public void Apply(Node node,string key,object value,PropertyContext ctx){var pv=(TscnPropertyValue)value;var extRes=ctx.Scene.ExtResources.FirstOrDefault(r=>r.Id==pv.RefId);if(extRes==null)return;if(extRes.Type=="Script"){var st=ScriptTypeRegistry.Resolve(extRes.Path);if(st!=null&&typeof(Node).IsAssignableFrom(st))return;}if(extRes.Type=="PackedScene"&&ctx.InstanceLoader!=null){var sub=ctx.InstanceLoader(extRes.Path);if(sub!=null){AssignSceneOwners(sub,sub);var packed=new PackedScene();if(packed.Pack(sub)==Error.Ok)node.Set(key,packed);else GameLogger.Log("TSCN_BUILD",$"ExtResourcePropertyResolver: failed to pack '{extRes.Path}' for '{key}'",LogLevel.Warning);}return;}if(ctx.ExtResourceResolver!=null){var r=ctx.ExtResourceResolver(pv.RefId);if(r!=null)node.Set(key,Variant.From(r));}}/// <summary> <see cref="PackedScene.Pack"/> serializes only nodes whose <c>Owner</c> is the packed root, while the runtime builder produces owner-less trees (Godot assigns owners only when loading native scenes). Without this, PackedScene-typed exports (e.g. <c>DialogBox.answerBoxScene</c>) instantiate as a bare root with no children. Owners are assigned on the throwaway instance built for packing, not on the cached resolver tree. </summary>
private static void AssignSceneOwners(Node root,Node current){foreach(var child in current.GetChildren()){child.Owner=root;AssignSceneOwners(root,child);}}}}

using System;using Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnBuild.PropertyResolvers{/// <summary> Applies editor-written theme overrides (<c>theme_override_constants/separation</c>, <c>theme_override_font_sizes/font_size</c>, <c>theme_override_colors/...</c>, and the stylebox/font/icon variants) through Control's <c>AddTheme*Override</c> API. <para/> The runtime parser used to declare these nested keys unsupported, which is invisible for mod scenes authored with scripts but not for native scenes: <c>scenes/menu/main_menu.tscn</c> and <c>settings_menu.tscn</c> rely on them, and patched native scenes must build through the runtime pipeline, so dropping them would visibly change the menu. Handling them here closes that gap without changing how mod scenes are authored. <para/> Values that are <see cref="TscnPropertyValue"/> references (an override pointing at an ext/sub resource) are deliberately left to the existing resource resolvers. </summary>
public class ThemeOverridePropertyResolver:IPropertyResolver{private const string Prefix="theme_override_";/// <summary>Claims plain-valued <c>theme_override_*/</c> keys; reference-valued overrides are left to the resource resolvers.</summary>
public bool CanResolve(string key,object value){return!string.IsNullOrEmpty(key)&&key.StartsWith(Prefix,StringComparison.Ordinal)&&key.IndexOf('/')>0&&value is not TscnPropertyValue;}/// <summary>Routes the override to the matching AddTheme*Override by category (constants, font_sizes, colors, fonts, icons, styles).</summary>
public void Apply(Node node,string key,object value,PropertyContext ctx){if(node is not Control control){GameLogger.Log("TSCN_BUILD",$"ThemeOverridePropertyResolver: '{key}' on non-Control '{node.Name}' ignored",LogLevel.Warning);return;}var slash=key.IndexOf('/');var category=key.Substring(Prefix.Length,slash-Prefix.Length);var name=key.Substring(slash+1);var variant=SubResourceFactory.ToVariant(value);try{switch(category){case"constants":control.AddThemeConstantOverride(name,variant.AsInt32());break;case"font_sizes":control.AddThemeFontSizeOverride(name,variant.AsInt32());break;case"colors":control.AddThemeColorOverride(name,variant.AsColor());break;case"fonts":control.AddThemeFontOverride(name,variant.As<Font>());break;case"icons":control.AddThemeIconOverride(name,variant.As<Texture2D>());break;case"styles":control.AddThemeStyleboxOverride(name,variant.As<StyleBox>());break;default:GameLogger.Log("TSCN_BUILD",$"ThemeOverridePropertyResolver: unknown category '{category}' for '{key}'",LogLevel.Warning);break;}}catch(Exception ex){GameLogger.Log("TSCN_BUILD",$"ThemeOverridePropertyResolver: failed to apply '{key}': {ex.Message}",LogLevel.Warning);}}}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using System.Linq;using System.Reflection;using Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnBuild{/// <summary> Auto-discovering registry of <see cref="ISubResourceBuilder"/> implementations, indexed by ResourceType. <para/> Initial scan on first access picks up all already-loaded assemblies (including core). <see cref="RegisterAssembly"/> is called by <see cref="Mods.ModAssemblyLoader.RegisterAssembly"/> when a mod DLL is loaded, adding the mod's builders without re-scanning everything. First-registered-wins — core builders always take priority over mod-added ones. <para/> The registry instance lives in <see cref="AppServices.Current"/>; the static members below are a facade delegating to it, so existing callers keep working unchanged. </summary>
public class SubResourceBuilderRegistry:IGameRegistry{private Dictionary<string,ISubResourceBuilder>_builders;private bool built;/// <summary>Shared instance the static facade delegates to.</summary>
private static SubResourceBuilderRegistry Owned=>AppServices.Current.SubResourceBuilders;/// <summary> Creates an empty registry: cheap and side-effect free per the IGameRegistry contract. <see cref="Rebuild"/> fills the data. </summary>
internal SubResourceBuilderRegistry(){}/// <inheritdoc />
public string Id=>"tscn_sub_builders";/// <summary> Scans all loaded assemblies for <see cref="ISubResourceBuilder"/> implementations unless already built. Keeps the old Initialize idempotence: later calls are no-ops until the registry is cleared. </summary>
public void EnsureBuilt(){if(!built)Rebuild();}/// <summary> Forced full re-scan of all loaded assemblies (assembly order equals load order, so first-registered-wins keeps core builders ahead of mod-added ones), replacing the previous table. Safe to call repeatedly; picks up assemblies loaded after the previous build. </summary>
public void Rebuild(){var scanned=new Dictionary<string,ISubResourceBuilder>();foreach(var b in Reflections.FindAndCreate<ISubResourceBuilder>())if(!scanned.ContainsKey(b.ResourceType))scanned[b.ResourceType]=b;_builders=scanned;built=true;}/// <summary> Drops all registered builders; the next build re-scans the assemblies. Called on mod reload through AppServices.ClearRegistries. </summary>
public void Clear(){_builders=null;built=false;}// ---- Static facade (legacy API, unchanged for callers) ------------ <summary>Legacy entry point; delegates to the shared instance.</summary>
public static void Initialize()=>Owned.EnsureBuilt();/// <summary>Scans a newly-loaded mod assembly for <see cref="ISubResourceBuilder"/> implementations and registers them. Called from <see cref="Mods.ModAssemblyLoader.RegisterAssembly"/>.</summary>
public static void RegisterAssembly(Assembly assembly)=>Owned.AddFromAssembly(assembly);/// <summary>Looks up a builder by resource type name. Returns null if no builder is registered for the given type.</summary>
public static ISubResourceBuilder Get(string type)=>Owned.GetBuilder(type);/// <summary>Unload pass: drops builders contributed by the given assembly. Delegates to the shared instance.</summary>
public static void UnregisterAssembly(Assembly assembly)=>Owned.RemoveFromAssembly(assembly);// ---- Instance implementation --------------------------------------
private void AddFromAssembly(Assembly assembly){EnsureBuilt();foreach(var b in Reflections.FindAndCreate<ISubResourceBuilder>(assembly))if(!_builders.ContainsKey(b.ResourceType))_builders[b.ResourceType]=b;}/// <summary> Removes builders whose concrete type comes from the given assembly — the unload pass of the assembly consumer pipeline. Built-in builders survive; a slot left empty falls back to a full rebuild on next use. </summary>
public void RemoveFromAssembly(Assembly assembly){if(_builders==null)return;foreach(var key in _builders.Where(kvp=>kvp.Value.GetType().Assembly==assembly).Select(kvp=>kvp.Key).ToList())_builders.Remove(key);}private ISubResourceBuilder GetBuilder(string type){EnsureBuilt();_builders.TryGetValue(type,out var b);return b;}}}

public class GradientBuilder:ISubResourceBuilder{/// <summary>Handles <c>[sub_resource type="Gradient"]</c>.</summary>
public string ResourceType=>"Gradient";/// <summary>Builds the gradient, converting the <c>colors</c> ParsedGodotValue array and <c>offsets</c> float array explicitly.</summary>
public Resource Build(SubResourceDef def,SubResourceBuildContext ctx){var g=new Gradient();foreach(var kvp in def.OrderedProperties){if(kvp.Key=="colors"&&kvp.Value is ParsedGodotValue[]ca){var cc=new Color[ca.Length];for(var i=0;i<ca.Length;i++)cc[i]=new Color(AsF(ca[i].Arg(0)),AsF(ca[i].Arg(1)),AsF(ca[i].Arg(2)),AsF(ca[i].Arg(3),1f));g.SetColors(cc);}else if(kvp.Key=="offsets"&&kvp.Value is float[]oa)g.SetOffsets(oa);else SubResourceFactory.SetProperty(g,kvp.Key,kvp.Value);}return g;}private static float AsF(object v,float fb=0f)=>v is float f?f:v is int i?i:v is double d?(float)d:fb;}}

public class SubResourceFactory{private readonly Dictionary<string,Resource>_built=new();/// <summary>Register a pre-built resource under its sub_resource id. Used so that BuildAll can resolve cross-references between sub-resources.</summary>

using System.Collections.Generic;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing{/// <summary> Parses a single section type in a .tscn file (e.g. [node], [ext_resource]). Each implementation is responsible for exactly one section type. <para/> Lifecycle: Open (section header) → Property* (zero or more property lines) → Close (commit to ParsedScene). The orchestrator (<see cref="TscnParser"/>) calls these methods as it walks token stream, never branching on section type itself — lookup is deferred to <see cref="SectionParserRegistry"/>. <para/> Auto-discovered via <c>Reflections.FindAndCreate&lt;ISectionParser&gt;()</c>. To add a new section type, implement this interface in any loaded assembly — no registration code needed. </summary>
public interface ISectionParser{/// <summary>Section type name as it appears in .tscn (e.g. "node", "ext_resource").</summary>
string SectionType{get;}/// <summary>Called when a section header is encountered. <paramref name="headerAttrs"/> are the parsed key=value attributes from the brackets.</summary>
void Open(Dictionary<string,string>headerAttrs);/// <summary>Called for each key=value property line under the current section.</summary>
void Property(string key,string rawValue);/// <summary>Called when the next section header is encountered (or at end of file). Commits all accumulated state to <paramref name="scene"/>.</summary>
void Close(ParsedScene scene);}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing{/// <summary>Lightweight wrapper for Godot-specific property values (Vector2, Color, NodePath, etc.) — avoids creating actual Godot objects during parsing to remain testable outside the engine.</summary>
public class ParsedGodotValue{/// <summary>Constructor-style name of the Godot value, e.g. "Vector2", "Color", "NodePath".</summary>
public string TypeName{get;set;}/// <summary>Positional arguments inside the parentheses; numbers are stored as float/int, strings as string.</summary>
public System.Collections.Generic.List<object>Args{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>Convenience factory for parsers and tests.</summary>
public static ParsedGodotValue Create(string typeName,params object[]args)=>new(){TypeName=typeName,Args=new System.Collections.Generic.List<object>(args)};/// <summary>Returns the argument at <paramref name="index"/>, or null when out of range (Godot constructors allow omitted trailing args).</summary>
public object Arg(int index)=>index<Args.Count?Args[index]:null;}}

using System.Collections.Generic;namespace Cthangover.Core.Scenes.TscnParsing{/// <summary> Intermediate representation of a fully parsed .tscn scene file. Contains flat lists of resources, nodes, and connections — the node hierarchy is encoded via <see cref="ParsedNode.Parent"/> references, not a tree. </summary>
public class ParsedScene{/// <summary>Value of the <c>format=</c> attribute in [gd_scene]; information only (format 3 expected).</summary>
public string Format{get;set;}/// <summary>All [ext_resource] entries in file order.</summary>
public List<ExtResourceRef>ExtResources{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>All [sub_resource] entries in file order.</summary>
public List<SubResourceDef>SubResources{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>All [node] sections in file order — the order is the build order.</summary>
public List<ParsedNode>Nodes{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>Root-script [connection] sections kept by the parser.</summary>
public List<ParsedConnection>Connections{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>Fully-qualified entry-point class from the root node's <c>__entry_point</c> property; null when absent.</summary>
public string EntryPointClass{get;set;}}/// <summary>Parsed [ext_resource] entry. Stores type ("Script"/"PackedScene"), mod-relative path, and local id.</summary>
public class ExtResourceRef{/// <summary>Declared resource type ("Script", "PackedScene", "Texture2D", …).</summary>
public string Type{get;set;}/// <summary>Mod-relative (or normalized) path of the resource file.</summary>
public string Path{get;set;}/// <summary>Local id referenced by <c>ExtResource("id")</c> within this scene file.</summary>
public string Id{get;set;}}/// <summary>Parsed [sub_resource] section. Inline resources (StyleBoxFlat, Gradient, etc.), built later by <see cref="TscnBuild.ISubResourceBuilder"/>.</summary>
public class SubResourceDef{/// <summary>Resource type name from the section header ("StyleBoxFlat", "Gradient", …).</summary>
public string Type{get;set;}/// <summary>Local id referenced by <c>SubResource("id")</c>.</summary>
public string Id{get;set;}/// <summary>Parsed property values keyed by property name.</summary>
public Dictionary<string,object>Properties{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>Keys of <see cref="Properties"/> in source-file order. Godot applies properties in file order, which matters for layout/anchors and sub-resource cross-references.</summary>
public List<string>PropertyOrder{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>Properties in the order they appeared in the .tscn source.</summary>
public IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string,object>>OrderedProperties{get{foreach(var key in PropertyOrder)if(Properties.TryGetValue(key,out var value))yield return new KeyValuePair<string,object>(key,value);}}}/// <summary> Parsed [node] section. Nodes are stored flat — parent-child relationships via <see cref="Parent"/>: null = root, "." = direct child of root, "Name" or "Name/Child" = explicit path. <see cref="InstanceRef"/> and <see cref="ScriptRef"/> store raw ExtResource strings, resolved at build time. </summary>
public class ParsedNode{/// <summary>Node name from the section header.</summary>
public string Name{get;set;}/// <summary>Godot class name for new nodes; null on override/instance headings.</summary>
public string Type{get;set;}/// <summary>Parent path: null for the root, "." for a direct child of root, "Name/Child" for deeper placement.</summary>
