using System.Collections.Generic;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Skills{/// <summary> Sums skill effects across a set of owned skills into the totals shown by the skills panel's global "collection effect" plate. The result is what the player actually gains right now — a card collected from any mod changes it immediately, without touching the individual definitions. <para/> Aggregation is keyed by <see cref="SkillEffectInfo.Key"/> and preserves first-seen order, so the plate does not reshuffle between openings and a newly granted skill appends its unique effects at the end. Null skills, null effect lists and effects without a key are skipped: mod JSON is not trusted to be complete. </summary>
public static class SkillEffectAggregator{/// <summary> Builds the collection-wide totals from the given skills. Effects with the same key are summed; the <c>Percent</c> flag survives if any contributor set it, so a mixed authoring mistake degrades to the percent display instead of silently dropping the suffix. </summary> <param name="skills">Owned skills, usually resolved from <see cref="SkillData.Skills"/>.</param> <returns>One entry per unique effect key, in first-seen order. Empty when nothing contributes.</returns>
public static List<SkillEffectInfo>Aggregate(IEnumerable<SkillInfo>skills){var order=new List<string>();var totals=new Dictionary<string,SkillEffectInfo>();if(skills!=null){foreach(var skill in skills){if(skill?.Effects==null)continue;foreach(var effect in skill.Effects){if(effect==null||string.IsNullOrEmpty(effect.Key))continue;if(!totals.TryGetValue(effect.Key,out var total)){total=new SkillEffectInfo{Key=effect.Key,Percent=effect.Percent};totals[effect.Key]=total;order.Add(effect.Key);}total.Value+=effect.Value;total.Percent|=effect.Percent;}}}var result=new List<SkillEffectInfo>();foreach(var key in order)result.Add(totals[key]);return result;}}}

using System;using System.Globalization;using System.Text.Json.Serialization;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Skills{/// <summary> One numeric bonus granted by a skill card — the gameplay payload behind the collection. <see cref="Key"/> is the locale key naming the affected stat (e.g. <c>characters/skills/effects/recruit</c>), <see cref="Value"/> its magnitude and <see cref="Percent"/> the display unit. <para/> Effects sharing a key are summed by <see cref="SkillEffectAggregator"/> into the panel's global "collection effect" plate, so one key must keep the same unit across every skill: two effects of <c>+10%</c> and <c>+5%</c> become <c>+15%</c>, never <c>+15</c>. Mods author these values in the skill JSON next to the card's rarity and type. </summary>
[Serializable]public class SkillEffectInfo{/// <summary>Locale key of the affected stat, shared by all skills that touch it.</summary>
[JsonPropertyName("Key")]public string Key{get;set;}/// <summary>Magnitude in the unit encoded by <see cref="Percent"/>. Negative values are penalties.</summary>
[JsonPropertyName("Value")]public float Value{get;set;}/// <summary>When true the value is displayed with a <c>%</c> suffix; still summed as a plain number.</summary>
[JsonPropertyName("Percent")]public bool Percent{get;set;}/// <summary> Formats the magnitude for cards, chips and the collection plate. An explicit <c>+</c> marks positive values so a bonus never reads as a subtracted amount; trailing zeros are trimmed (<c>+50%</c>, not <c>+50.0%</c>); <c>%</c> is appended when <see cref="Percent"/> is set. </summary>
public string FormatValue(){var number=Value.ToString("0.##",CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);if(Value>0f)number="+"+number;return Percent?number+"%":number;}}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using System.Text.Json.Serialization;using Cthangover.Core.Factories;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Skills{/// <summary> Immutable data model for a single skill definition, populated by <see cref="SkillFactory"/> from JSON assets. Each instance carries the metadata required to render a skill card in the UI (<see cref="Sprite"/>, <see cref="Name"/>, <see cref="Description"/>) and to resolve its gameplay behaviour through <see cref="SkillType"/> and <see cref="RareType"/>. Instances are shared across the runtime and should not be mutated after construction. </summary>
[Serializable][EntityKind("skill")]public class SkillInfo:IIdentifiable{/// <summary> The unique string key of this skill, used as the primary lookup in <see cref="SkillFactory"/> and as the identity token in <see cref="SkillData.Skills"/>. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("Id")]public string ID{get;set;}/// <summary> The display name shown on the skill card. This value is passed through <see cref="TranslationServer.Translate"/> before rendering, allowing localisation via Godot's translation system. </summary>
public string Name{get;set;}/// <summary> A longer textual description explaining what the skill does in gameplay terms. Displayed in tooltip and detail views alongside the card artwork. </summary>
public string Description{get;set;}/// <summary> The relative path to the skill's artwork texture, resolved inside the mod-group "characters/skills" by <see cref="TextureUtils.LoadFromModGroup"/> when the <see cref="Sprite"/> property is first accessed. </summary>
public string Image{get;set;}/// <summary> Optional ID of the action card this skill gifts to the player when acquired (e.g. an active skill that hands over a battle card). Resolved against <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls.ActionCharacterFactory"/> when the skills panel renders the detail view, and pushed into <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Settings.ActionPoolData.ActionIds"/> by <see cref="SkillService"/> so the card becomes assignable to a character. Empty for skills that only act as passive gates and never produce a card. </summary>
public string GrantsAction{get;set;}/// <summary> Numeric bonuses this skill grants while owned. They are the card's actual payload: the skills panel shows the first effect on the grid card, lists all of them in the study plate, and sums every owned skill's effects into the global "collection effect" plate via <see cref="SkillEffectAggregator"/>. Empty for skills that only gate content (e.g. unlock an action) without touching stats. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("Effects")]public List<SkillEffectInfo>Effects{get;set;}/// <summary> The gameplay classification of this skill (<c>Active</c>, <c>Passive</c>, or <c>ForCharacter</c>), serialised as a string in JSON and converted via <see cref="JsonStringEnumConverter"/>. </summary>
[JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter))][JsonPropertyName("Type")]public SkillType SkillType{get;set;}/// <summary> The rarity tier of this skill, serialised as a string in JSON and converted via <see cref="JsonStringEnumConverter"/>. Drives the colour of the card frame, study plate and rarity badge through <see cref="SkillPalette"/>. </summary>
[JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter))][JsonPropertyName("Rare")]public RareType RareType{get;set;}private Texture2D cacheSprite;/// <summary> Lazily loads and caches the <see cref="Texture2D"/> for this skill's card artwork. On first access the texture is resolved from the mod-group "characters/skills" using the <see cref="Image"/> path; subsequent accesses return the cached reference. </summary>
public Texture2D Sprite{get{if(cacheSprite==null)cacheSprite=TextureUtils.LoadFromModGroup("characters/skills",Image);return cacheSprite;}}}}

===== FILE mods/skills_base/src/SkillService.cs =====
using Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls;using Cthangover.Core.Settings;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Skills{/// <summary> Single entry point for acquiring a skill at runtime. A skill is more than a checkbox in <see cref="SkillData"/>: an active skill can hand the player an action card through <see cref="SkillInfo.GrantsAction"/>, and that card is what the player later assigns to a character in the character panel. Granting the skill and its card together keeps the two collections from drifting apart — a skill without its card (or a card without its skill) would survive save/restore inconsistently and the skills panel could not explain where the card came from. <para/> Granting is idempotent: once <see cref="SkillData"/> owns the skill ID, repeated calls are no-ops, so replayed scenario events cannot duplicate action cards in the pool. </summary>
public static class SkillService{/// <summary> Resolves the skill definition through <see cref="SkillFactory"/> and grants it to the current runtime. This is the path used by scenario actions and mod initializers. Unknown IDs are logged and rejected instead of partially mutating the runtime state. </summary> <param name="id">Skill ID as authored in the skill's JSON file (e.g. "slave_master").</param> <returns><c>true</c> when the skill was newly granted; <c>false</c> when it was already owned or could not be resolved.</returns>
public static bool GrantSkill(string id){if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(id))return false;var skill=SkillFactory.Instance.Get(id);if(skill==null){GameLogger.Log("SKILL",$"GrantSkill: unknown skill '{id}'",LogLevel.Warning);return false;}return GrantSkill(GameData.Instance.Runtime,skill);}/// <summary> Core grant routine operating on an explicit runtime, so the skill/card pairing can be exercised without the Godot autoload. Adds the skill to <see cref="RuntimeData.SkillData"/> and, when the definition names one, appends its granted action to <see cref="RuntimeData.ActionPool"/> where the character panel can pick it up. </summary> <param name="runtime">Session state that owns both the skill set and the action pool.</param> <param name="skill">Resolved skill definition to grant.</param> <returns><c>true</c> when the skill was newly granted; <c>false</c> when it was already owned or the arguments are invalid.</returns>
public static bool GrantSkill(RuntimeData runtime,SkillInfo skill){if(runtime==null||skill==null||string.IsNullOrEmpty(skill.ID))return false;if(runtime.SkillData.HasSkill(skill.ID))return false;runtime.SkillData.AddSkill(skill.ID);if(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(skill.GrantsAction))runtime.ActionPool.ActionIds.Add(skill.GrantsAction);GameLogger.Log("SKILL",string.IsNullOrEmpty(skill.GrantsAction)?$"GrantSkill: granted '{skill.ID}'":$"GrantSkill: granted '{skill.ID}', action '{skill.GrantsAction}' added to pool");return true;}}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using System.Linq;using System.Text.Json;using Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap;using Cthangover.Core.Characters;using Cthangover.Core.Items;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;using Cthangover.Core.Mods.Resolvers;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Mods.TestDefaultsAndPatches{/// <summary> Entry point of the property patches itest: active only with <c>--itest=property_patches</c>. The fixture itself is loaded only by <c>--with-mods=test_defaults_and_patches</c> (manifest <c>fixture</c>). </summary>
public class PropertyPatchesTestInitializer:IModInitializer{private static bool queued;public void OnModLoaded(string modId){}public void OnModResourcesReady(){if(queued|| !OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs().Contains("--itest=property_patches"))return;queued=true;GameLogger.Log("TEST","PropertyPatchesTest: activating");(Godot.Engine.GetMainLoop()as SceneTree)?.Root?.CallDeferred("add_child",new PropertyPatchesTestDriverNode());}}/// <summary> Checks the merge of <c>patches/character.json</c> and <c>patches/item.json</c> into the real entities of other mods, as the game resolves them: a targeted patch wins over the wildcard, the wildcard reaches every entity of the kind, and untouched typed fields survive. Prints <c>[TEST_RESULT] name=property_patches</c> and quits. </summary>
public partial class PropertyPatchesTestDriverNode:Node{private const string ResultName="property_patches";private const double TimeoutSeconds=60;private int passed;private int failed;private double elapsed;private bool done;public override void _Process(double delta){if(done)return;elapsed+=delta;if(elapsed>TimeoutSeconds){Check("boot finished in time",false);Finish();return;}if(!Boot.IsReady)return;try{Run();}catch(Exception ex){Check($"no exception ({ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message})",false);}Finish();}private void Run(){var characterPatches=Patches.Collect("character");Check("character patches collected (Marao + *)",characterPatches!=null&&characterPatches.ContainsKey("Marao")&&characterPatches.ContainsKey("*"));var itemPatches=Patches.Collect("item");Check("item patches collected (food/ration + *)",itemPatches!=null&&itemPatches.ContainsKey("food/ration")&&itemPatches.ContainsKey("*"));var characters=Entities.Collect<CharacterInfo>();Check("Marao resolved",characters.ContainsKey("Marao"));if(characters.TryGetValue("Marao",out var marao)){Expect(marao.ExtraProperties,"TestPatched","42","Marao: targeted value");Expect(marao.ExtraProperties,"TestDefault","100","Marao: targeted beats wildcard");Expect(marao.ExtraProperties,"TestGlobalPatch","1","Marao: wildcard-only key");}var other=characters.Values.FirstOrDefault(c=>c.ID!="Marao");Check("another character exists",other!=null);if(other!=null){Expect(other.ExtraProperties,"TestDefault","-20",$"{other.ID}: wildcard value");Check($"{other.ID}: no targeted key",other.ExtraProperties==null|| !other.ExtraProperties.ContainsKey("TestPatched"));}var items=Entities.Collect<ItemInfo>();if(items.TryGetValue("food/ration",out var ration)){Expect(ration.ExtraProperties,"Durability","99","ration: targeted beats wildcard");Expect(ration.ExtraProperties,"SpecialProp","true","ration: targeted-only key");Expect(ration.ExtraProperties,"GlobalItemProp","patched","ration: wildcard-only key");Check("ration: typed field survives the merge",!string.IsNullOrEmpty(ration.Name));}else Check("food/ration resolved",false);if(items.TryGetValue("food/wolf_meat",out var meat))Expect(meat.ExtraProperties,"Durability","50","wolf_meat: wildcard value");else Check("food/wolf_meat resolved",false);}private void Expect(Dictionary<string,object>properties,string key,string expected,string what){var actual=properties!=null&&properties.TryGetValue(key,out var value)?Text(value):null;Check($"{what}: {key}={expected}"+(actual==expected?string.Empty:$" (got {actual ?? "nothing"})"),actual==expected);}private static string Text(object value)=>value switch{JsonElement{ValueKind:JsonValueKind.String}s=>s.GetString(),JsonElement e=>e.GetRawText(),bool b=>b?"true":"false",null=>null,_=>Convert.ToString(value,System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture),};private void Check(string what,bool ok){if(ok)passed++;else failed++;GameLogger.Log("TEST",$"  [{(ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL")}] {what}");}private void Finish(){done=true;GameLogger.Log("TEST",$"[TEST_RESULT] name={ResultName} passed={passed} failed={failed}");GetTree().Quit(failed==0?0:1);}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Actions;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Time{/// <summary> Resets the lighting depth and albedo maps to null via the lighting service. This effectively disables scene-specific lighting masks, reverting to default flat lighting. Used when transitioning between scenes that have different lighting setups or when entering a scene that doesn't use depth-based lighting. </summary>
public class LightingClearMapAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary> Registered as "lighting.clear_map" — resets the depth and albedo lighting maps to null via UiLightController. Both maps are cleared simultaneously because the lighting shader requires either both present or neither — partial clearing produces visual artifacts. Use when transitioning between scenes that have different lighting setups, or when entering a scene that doesn't use depth-based lighting. </summary>
public string Name=>"lighting.clear_map";/// <summary> Delegates to ctx.Lighting.ClearDepthMap which nulls out both depth and albedo textures on the UiLightController singleton. Safe to call when the controller hasn't been initialized (null-conditional access in the implementation). </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){ctx.Lighting.ClearDepthMap();ctx.Log("SHADER","LightingClearMapAction: cleared depth and albedo maps");}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Actions;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Time{/// <summary> Thin wrapper around UiLightController.Instance. ClearDepthMap sets both depth and albedo to null simultaneously — partial clearing would leave the shader in an inconsistent state. SetUseTime delegates to the controller's IsUseLight property. </summary>
public class LightingServiceImpl:ILightingService{/// <summary> Sets both depth and albedo maps to null on UiLightController. Both are cleared together because the lighting shader requires either both textures present or neither — partial clearing produces visual artifacts. Safe to call when the controller hasn't been initialized yet (null-conditional access). </summary>
public void ClearDepthMap(){var controller=UiLightController.Instance;controller?.SetupDepthMap(null);controller?.SetupAlbedoMap(null);}/// <summary> Toggles the IsUseLight property on UiLightController. When true, the controller applies time-of-day lighting adjustments; when false, lighting remains static. public void SetUseTime(bool useTime){var controller=UiLightController.Instance;if(controller!=null)controller.IsUseLight=useTime;}}}

using System.Text.Json.Serialization;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Time{/// <summary> Serializable light definition for JSON scene lighting. Coordinates are viewport-relative (0.0–1.0) so scenes adapt to different resolutions. ToPixelPos/FromPixelPos convert between normalized space and pixel space using a reference viewport size. Color is stored as a hex string for human-readable JSON editing. </summary>
public class LightDef{/// <summary> Normalized horizontal position (0.0–1.0) relative to viewport width. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("x")]public float X{get;set;}/// <summary> Normalized vertical position (0.0–1.0) relative to viewport height. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("y")]public float Y{get;set;}/// <summary> Light radius in pixel units. Determines the falloff distance in the lighting shader. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("radius")]public float Radius{get;set;}/// <summary> Light intensity (0.0–1.0). At <c>1.0</c>, the light fully brightens pixels within its radius. Lower values create subtler effects. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("influence")]public float Influence{get;set;}=1f;/// <summary> Light color as a hex string (e.g. "#ff8800"). Parsed by <see cref="ToColor"/> for shader upload. </summary>
[JsonPropertyName("color")]public string ColorHex{get;set;}="#ffff00";/// <summary> Converts <see cref="ColorHex"/> to a Godot <c>Color</c> struct. </summary>
public Color ToColor(){return new Color(ColorHex);}/// <summary> Converts normalized coordinates (<see cref="X"/>, <see cref="Y"/>) to pixel coordinates based on <paramref name="viewportSize"/>. </summary> <param name="viewportSize">Current viewport dimensions in pixels.</param>
public Vector2 ToPixelPos(Vector2 viewportSize){return new Vector2(X*viewportSize.X,Y*viewportSize.Y);}/// <summary> Computes normalized coordinates from pixel coordinates by dividing by <paramref name="referenceSize"/>. Enables saving light positions across different resolutions. </summary> <param name="pixelPos">Light position in pixel space.</param> <param name="referenceSize">Viewport dimensions used as reference.</param>
public void FromPixelPos(Vector2 pixelPos,Vector2 referenceSize){X=pixelPos.X/referenceSize.X;Y=pixelPos.Y/referenceSize.Y;}}}

On <c>OnModResourcesReady</c> it installs the lighting adapters into <see cref="LightingBridge"/> (first registration wins) and registers the <see cref="TimeTickController"/> with the scene event system, so in-game time advances each timer pulse. The controller lives in a static field: <c>EnsureRegistered</c> is idempotent per instance, and a process-wide singleton guarantees a mod reload cannot stack a second timer-tick subscription onto <c>EventController</c>. </summary>

using Cthangover.Core.Bootstrap;using Cthangover.Core.Settings;using Cthangover.Core.Events;using Cthangover.Core.Mods;using Cthangover.Core.UI.Event;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Time{/// <summary> Bridges the scene-event timer system to the in-game clock. Implements <see cref="Cthangover.Core.UI.Event.IOnTimeEvent"/> with priority 0 so that the tick is processed before most other listeners. The controller must be explicitly registered via <see cref="EnsureRegistered"/>, which finds the <see cref="Cthangover.Core.UI.Event.SceneEventController"/> in the scene tree and subscribes <see cref="OnTimerTick"/> to it. Registration is idempotent — subsequent calls are no-ops. </summary>
public class TimeTickController:IOnTimeEvent{/// <summary>Executes before default-priority listeners so time updates are visible to all other tick handlers.</summary>
public int Priority=>0;private bool _registered;/// <summary> Locates the <see cref="Cthangover.Core.UI.Event.SceneEventController"/> in the scene tree and registers this controller as a timer-tick listener. Safe to call multiple times — only the first call does work. </summary>
public void EnsureRegistered(Node node){if(_registered)return;var eventController=node.GetTree()?.Root?.FindChild("EventController",true,false)as SceneEventController;if(eventController==null)return;eventController.AddTimerTickEventListener(this);_registered=true;}/// <summary> Called by the event system on each timer pulse. Advances the in-game clock by one minute via <see cref="TimeData.AddTick"/>. </summary>
public void OnTimerTick(){// The SceneEventController keeps ticking (1s interval, ProcessMode Always) while the launcher boot compiles mods in the background — registration in GameData._Ready succeeds because the engine puts every autoload into the tree before any _Ready fires. Touching Runtime here would create it before the starter inventory can be seeded through loaded mod factories: the seed then runs against an empty registry, logs "Initialize refused" spam and permanently skips the starter items. Skip boot-window ticks instead — the same readiness contract GameData.Runtime enforces.
if(!Boot.ModsReady)return;GameData.Instance.Runtime.Time.AddTick();ModEventBus.Publish(new TimeTickEvent{TimeTick=GameData.Instance.Runtime.Time.Tick,NormalizedTime=GameData.Instance.Runtime.Time.Normalized,});}}}

The stock of <see cref="Sells"/> is unlimited and the shop has no state of its own: what the player sells disappears into the merchant's pocket, so nothing needs saving except the player's inventory. Money is an ordinary inventory item (<see cref="Currency"/>), which keeps it in the items save slot and lets scenarios pay with <c>item.add</c>. </summary>
[EntityKind("shop")]public class ShopInfo:IIdentifiable{/// <summary>Currency item used when a shop does not name one.</summary>
public const string DefaultCurrency="money/coin";/// <summary>Shop id, the <c>shop=</c> argument of <c>trade.open</c>.</summary>
[JsonPropertyName("Id")]public string ID{get;set;}/// <summary>Locale key of the window title (the merchant's name).</summary>
public string Name{get;set;}/// <summary>Item id of the money this shop takes and pays.</summary>
public string Currency{get;set;}=DefaultCurrency;/// <summary>What the merchant sells to the player, in display order.</summary>
public List<ShopOffer>Sells{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>What the merchant buys from the player; anything else is refused.</summary>
public List<ShopOffer>Buys{get;set;}=new();/// <summary>The offer for buying <paramref name="itemId"/> from the merchant, or <c>null</c>.</summary>
public ShopOffer FindSell(string itemId)=>Find(Sells,itemId);/// <summary>The offer for selling <paramref name="itemId"/> to the merchant, or <c>null</c>.</summary>
public ShopOffer FindBuy(string itemId)=>Find(Buys,itemId);private static ShopOffer Find(List<ShopOffer>offers,string itemId){if(offers==null||string.IsNullOrEmpty(itemId))return null;foreach(var offer in offers){if(offer!=null&&offer.Price>0&&string.Equals(offer.Item,itemId,StringComparison.Ordinal))return offer;}return null;}}}

namespace Cthangover.Mods.Trading{/// <summary> One line of a shop's price list: an item id and its unit price in the shop's currency. The same type serves both directions — in <see cref="ShopInfo.Sells"/> it is what the player pays, in <see cref="ShopInfo.Buys"/> what the merchant pays. An offer with a price below 1 is ignored by <see cref="TradeLedger"/>: a free deal is a gift and belongs in a scenario. </summary>
public class ShopOffer{/// <summary>Item id (<c>"Kind": "item"</c>).</summary>
public string Item{get;set;}/// <summary>Unit price in the shop's currency.</summary>
public int Price{get;set;}}}

===== FILE mods/trading/src/TradeLedger.cs =====
using Cthangover.Core.Items;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Trading{/// <summary> The arithmetic of a deal, apart from the window so it can be tested and reused by a scenario action later. A deal is all or nothing: it is checked first (offer exists, positive quantity, enough money or goods) and only then both stacks change, so a refused deal leaves the inventory untouched. </summary>
public static class TradeLedger{/// <summary>The player's money in the shop's currency.</summary>
public static int Money(IInventory inventory,ShopInfo shop){return inventory==null||shop==null?0:inventory.CheckCount(shop.Currency);}/// <summary>How many units of <paramref name="itemId"/> the player can afford; 0 when the shop does not sell it.</summary>
public static int MaxBuy(IInventory inventory,ShopInfo shop,string itemId){var offer=shop?.FindSell(itemId);return offer==null?0:Money(inventory,shop)/offer.Price;}/// <summary>How many units of <paramref name="itemId"/> the player can sell; 0 when the merchant does not buy it.</summary>
public static int MaxSell(IInventory inventory,ShopInfo shop,string itemId){if(inventory==null||shop?.FindBuy(itemId)==null||itemId==shop.Currency)return 0;return inventory.CheckCount(itemId);}/// <summary> Buys <paramref name="count"/> units: takes their price in money and adds the items. Returns <c>false</c> and changes nothing when the shop does not sell the item, the count is not positive or the money is short. </summary>
public static bool Buy(IInventory inventory,ShopInfo shop,string itemId,int count){if(count<=0||count>MaxBuy(inventory,shop,itemId))return false;if(!inventory.Remove(shop.Currency,shop.FindSell(itemId).Price*count))return false;inventory.Add(itemId,count);return true;}/// <summary> Sells <paramref name="count"/> units: removes the items and pays their price. Returns <c>false</c> and changes nothing when the merchant does not buy the item, the count is not positive or the player has fewer units. </summary>
public static bool Sell(IInventory inventory,ShopInfo shop,string itemId,int count){if(count<=0||count>MaxSell(inventory,shop,itemId))return false;if(!inventory.Remove(itemId,count))return false;inventory.Add(shop.Currency,shop.FindBuy(itemId).Price*count);return true;}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Actions;using Cthangover.Core.UI;namespace Cthangover.Mods.Trading{/// <summary> <c>action trade.open shop=village_merchant</c> — opens the trade window with that merchant. Usually the last line of a merchant's dialog. The window is a hosted overlay of the UI registry (it lives above every scene and is built once), so the action hands it the shop and then shows it through the registry, which keeps the host's record of open entries right. </summary>
public class TradeOpenAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary>DSL name.</summary>
public string Name=>"trade.open";/// <summary>Resolves the shop and shows the window for it.</summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var id=ctx.GetParam("shop");var shop=string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(id)?null:ShopFactory.Instance.Get(id.Trim());if(shop==null){ctx.LogWarning("TRADE",$"trade.open: unknown shop '{id}'");return;}var entry=UiRegistry.Get(TradePanel.EntryId);if(entry==null||UiHost.Instance?.EnsureInstance(entry)is not TradePanel panel){ctx.LogWarning("TRADE","trade.open: the trade window is not available");return;}panel.SetShop(shop);if(!panel.Visible)UiRegistry.Toggle(TradePanel.EntryId);}}}

private void CheckMushroomHeals(){var hero=GameData.Instance.Runtime.CharacterData.Characters["rpg_hero"];var item=ItemFactory.Instance.Get(Mushroom);var heal=item?.ItemAction as ITargetedItemAction;Check(heal!=null,"the mushroom has a targeted heal action");if(heal==null)return;var max=hero.Attributes.Health.BaseValue;hero.Attributes.Health.Value=max-8;Check(heal.UseOn(item,hero)&&hero.Attributes.Health.Value==max-3,$"eating heals 5, health {hero.Attributes.Health.Value}/{max}");hero.Attributes.Health.Value=max;Check(!heal.UseOn(item,hero),"no eating at full health");}/// <summary> Holds S until the hero leaves row 2 (the world reads the held key each frame, a tap within one tick would be missed), then waits for the touch event's dialog to end; true while busy. </summary>

using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Characters;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle.Actions{/// <summary> Central action-execution dispatcher. Resolves an action ID to an IActionExecutor in two tiers: first the active provider (set by the current IBattleCore, allowing per-battle-engine overrides), then a global fallback registry. This two-level lookup lets mods supply custom executors for specific battle cores without replacing the global ones. Execute returns ChangedAttributes to allow the caller to inspect the result (success/failure, stat deltas). </summary>
public class ActionExecutorHub{/// <summary> Singleton hub instance. There is one global dispatcher shared across all battle cores; cores swap providers via <see cref="SetActiveProvider"/> when they activate. </summary>
public static readonly ActionExecutorHub Instance=new();private IActionExecutorProvider _activeProvider;private readonly Dictionary<string,IActionExecutor>_globalExecutors=new();/// <summary> Installs a per-core executor provider. The active provider is consulted before the global registry, allowing the current battle core to override specific action handlers. </summary>
public void SetActiveProvider(IActionExecutorProvider provider){_activeProvider=provider;}/// <summary> Registers a fallback executor in the global pool, keyed by <see cref="IActionExecutor.ActionId"/>. Global executors are used when no active provider supplies a match. </summary>
public void RegisterGlobal(IActionExecutor executor){if(executor!=null&& !string.IsNullOrEmpty(executor.ActionId))_globalExecutors[executor.ActionId]=executor;}/// <summary> Dispatches an action to the appropriate executor. Resolution order: active provider first, then global registry. Returns <c>Result = false</c> if no executor is found or if <paramref name="action"/> is null. </summary>
public ChangedAttributes Execute(ActionCharacter action,Character user,Character target){if(action==null)return new ChangedAttributes{Result=false};var executor=Resolve(action.ID);if(executor==null)return new ChangedAttributes{Result=false};return executor.Execute(action,user,target);}private IActionExecutor Resolve(string actionId){if(_activeProvider!=null){var executor=_activeProvider.GetExecutor(actionId);if(executor!=null)return executor;}_globalExecutors.TryGetValue(actionId,out var fallback);return fallback;}}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.UI;using Godot;using Cthangover.Mods.Interface.Base;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle.Actions{/// <summary> Sequential action queue that processes one IBattleAction per frame until it signals completion (DoAction returns true), then moves to the next. Fires OnStopMachine when the queue drains naturally or is explicitly stopped — used by battle cores to detect when a turn's animation sequence is finished. Actions can be added before or during processing; the machine starts automatically once at least one action is queued and no current action is running. <para/> Derives from <see cref="ModNode"/> so the engine lifecycle callbacks reach this runtime-compiled script through the core base class (mod assemblies have no Godot source generation of their own). </summary>
public partial class BattleActionMachine:ModNode{/// <summary> Pending action queue. Actions are dequeued one-by-one in the process hook, starting the next as soon as the current signals completion. Can be extended while the machine is running — new actions will be processed after the current queue drains. </summary>
public List<IBattleAction>Actions{get;set;}=new();private IBattleAction CurrentAction{get;set;}private bool _hadActions;/// <summary> Fired when the machine drains naturally or is explicitly stopped. Battle cores subscribe to advance the turn phase without polling. </summary>
public event StopMachineDelegate OnStopMachine;/// <summary>Stops the machine and fires <see cref="OnStopMachine"/> when the node leaves the tree, so subscribers never wait on a dead node.</summary>
protected override void OnExitTree(){base.OnExitTree();StopMachine();}/// <summary>Drives the queued actions once per frame; fires <see cref="OnStopMachine"/> when the queue drains.</summary>
protected override void OnProcess(double delta){if(Actions.Count==0&&CurrentAction==null){if(_hadActions){_hadActions=false;StopMachine();}return;}var action=CurrentAction;if(action==null){CurrentAction=Actions[0];Actions.RemoveAt(0);action=CurrentAction;_hadActions=true;action?.DoStart();}if(action==null){_hadActions=false;StopMachine();return;}if(action.DoAction()){action.DoEnd();CurrentAction=null;}}/// <summary> Enqueues a single action. If the machine is idle (no current action), processing starts on the next _Process tick. </summary>
public void AddAction(IBattleAction action){if(action==null)return;Actions.Add(action);}/// <summary> Batch-enqueues multiple actions. All are appended to the existing queue and processed in FIFO order on subsequent frames. </summary>
public void AddActions(List<IBattleAction>actions){if(actions==null||actions.Count==0)return;Actions.AddRange(actions);}/// <summary> Immediately clears the queue, aborts the current action, and fires <see cref="OnStopMachine"/>. Called on tree exit and when the queue drains naturally. </summary>
public void StopMachine(){CurrentAction=null;Actions.Clear();_hadActions=false;OnStopMachine?.Invoke();}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Characters;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle.Actions{/// <summary> Adapter that lets a GDScript mod act as a battle action executor. The script is detected by <see cref="TurnBattleGDScriptHook"/> when it exposes <c>get_action_id()</c> and <c>execute(action, user, target)</c>; this adapter flattens the C# arguments into Godot dictionaries via <see cref="BattleGDScriptBridge"/> and maps the returned dictionary back to <see cref="ChangedAttributes"/>. Dictionaries are used instead of custom RefCounted DTOs because runtime-compiled mod classes get no Godot source generation, so their members would not be visible to GDScript. </summary>
public class GDBattleActionExecutor:IActionExecutor{private readonly GodotObject _instance;/// <summary>Creates an adapter around a live GDScript object. The object is retained by reference.</summary>
public GDBattleActionExecutor(string actionId,GodotObject instance){ActionId=actionId;_instance=instance;}/// <summary>Action id reported by the script through <c>get_action_id()</c>.</summary>
public string ActionId{get;}/// <summary> Calls the script and converts its result. A script that returns anything other than a dictionary (or throws) yields a failed result so one broken mod cannot abort the action pipeline. </summary>
public ChangedAttributes Execute(ActionCharacter action,Character user,Character target){var gdAction=BattleGDScriptBridge.ActionToDictionary(action);var gdUser=BattleGDScriptBridge.CharacterToDictionary(user);var gdTarget=BattleGDScriptBridge.CharacterToDictionary(target);var variant=_instance.Call("execute",gdAction,gdUser,gdTarget);if(variant.VariantType!=Variant.Type.Dictionary)return new ChangedAttributes{Result=false};return BattleGDScriptBridge.ResultFromDictionary(variant.AsGodotDictionary());}}}

The executor is keyed by ActionId (matching the action's ID) so the hub can look it up without knowing the concrete type. namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle.Actions{/// <summary> A single step in the battle action queue (animation, damage, effect). DoStart is called once when the action begins, DoAction is polled every frame — it returns true when the action is done — and DoEnd is the cleanup callback. This polling model lets actions drive their own duration (e.g. a tween runs until finished) without the machine needing timers. </summary>
public interface IBattleAction{/// <summary> Called once when the action is dequeued and begins execution. Use for setup: spawning nodes, caching references, starting tweens or coroutines. </summary>
void DoStart();/// <summary> Polled every frame. Returns <c>true</c> when the action has finished its work; returns <c>false</c> to remain active. This model eliminates the need for the machine to manage timers. </summary>
bool DoAction();/// <summary> Cleanup callback fired after <see cref="DoAction"/> returns <c>true</c>. Use for teardown: freeing nodes, resetting state, applying final stat deltas. </summary>
void DoEnd();}}

using Cthangover.Core.Characters;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> Default IBattleContext wired to the current BattleSceneContext. ApplyDamage clamps at 0 (no negative health from defence overflow), EndBattle delegates to ShowWinground/ShowDeadground on the scene context. ScheduleAnimation and EndTurn are stubs — specific battle cores are expected to override or supplement this behaviour. </summary>
public class BattleContextImpl:IBattleContext{private readonly BattleSceneContext _sceneContext;/// <summary> Root Godot <see cref="Node"/> of the battle scene, used by animation actions to parent spawned visual effects. </summary>
public Node RootNode=>_sceneContext;/// <summary> The owning <see cref="BattleSceneContext"/> that manages the battle lifecycle. </summary>
public BattleSceneContext SceneContext=>_sceneContext;/// <summary> Creates a context adapter around the given scene context. </summary>
public BattleContextImpl(BattleSceneContext sceneContext){_sceneContext=sceneContext;}/// <summary> Subtracts <paramref name="defence"/> from <paramref name="rawDamage"/>, clamping at 0 to prevent negative health from defence overflow, and applies the result to <paramref name="target"/>'s health. </summary>
public void ApplyDamage(Character source,Character target,int rawDamage,int defence){var finalDamage=Mathf.Max(0,rawDamage-defence);target.Attributes.Health.Value-=finalDamage;}/// <summary> Stub — specific battle cores override this to enqueue animation actions into the <see cref="BattleActionMachine"/>. </summary>
public void ScheduleAnimation(IBattleAnimation animation){}/// <summary> Stub — cores implement this to advance the turn sequence when a side finishes its action phase. </summary>
public void EndTurn(BattleSide side){}/// <summary> Resolves the battle outcome by delegating to <see cref="BattleSceneContext.ShowWinground"/> for player victory or <see cref="BattleSceneContext.ShowDeadground"/> for enemy victory. </summary>
public void EndBattle(BattleSide winner){if(winner==BattleSide.Player)_sceneContext.ShowWinground();else _sceneContext.ShowDeadground();}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Battle.Actions;using Cthangover.Core.Characters;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> Pluggable battle engine contract. Each implementation is a self-contained battle rule set (turn order, AI, phases). Init receives the two character arrays and a context adapter; Start begins the loop. The ActionProvider property lets the core inject its own executor overrides via the hub. Cores are instantiated fresh per battle — they carry no persistent state between encounters. </summary>
public interface IBattleCore{/// <summary> Unique identifier for this battle engine (e.g. "card_battle", "ff_battle"). Used by <see cref="BattleCoreRegistry"/> and <see cref="BattleData.ActiveBattleCore"/> for lookup. </summary>
string Id{get;}/// <summary> Provider that returns core-specific <see cref="IActionExecutor"/> overrides. Set on the <see cref="ActionExecutorHub"/> when this core activates, so actions route through custom logic before falling back to the global registry. </summary>
IActionExecutorProvider ActionProvider{get;}/// <summary> Initialises the core with the two character arrays and a <see cref="IBattleContext"/> for callbacks. Called once per battle before <see cref="Start"/>. </summary>
void Init(Character[]playerChars,Character[]enemyChars,IBattleContext ctx);/// <summary> Begins the turn loop. Cores may use coroutines, polling, or event-driven state machines — the core owns its own lifecycle after this call. </summary>
void Start();}}

using Cthangover.Core.Battle.Actions;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Characters{/// <summary> Convenience base for IActionExecutor implementations. Provides CheckRequiredAndUsePoint which validates that the user has enough "Point" attribute (a generic action-point / mana pool) before deducting it — returning false lets the action fail gracefully. ID is abstract so each action declares its own identity. </summary>
public abstract class ActionBase:IActionExecutor{/// <summary> Maps to the abstract <see cref="ID"/> so the hub can resolve this executor by action name. </summary>
public string ActionId=>ID;/// <summary> Unique action identifier that matches <see cref="ActionCharacter.ID"/> in data. </summary>
public abstract string ID{get;}/// <summary> Applies the action's effects to <paramref name="target"/> using <paramref name="user"/>'s stats and the <paramref name="action"/> definition. Returns stat deltas and a success/failure flag. </summary>
public abstract ChangedAttributes Execute(ActionCharacter action,Character user,Character target);/// <summary> Validates that <paramref name="user"/> has at least <c>"RequiredPoint"</c> remaining, deducts it, and returns <c>true</c>. Returns <c>false</c> with a warning log if the user lacks sufficient points, allowing the action to fail gracefully. </summary>
protected bool CheckRequiredAndUsePoint(ActionCharacter action,Character user){var requiredPoint=action.GetInt("RequiredPoint");if(user.Attributes.Point.Value<requiredPoint){GameLogger.Log("BATTLE",user.ID+" not checked point required ["+user.Attributes.Point.Value+"] for action "+action.ID+" ["+requiredPoint+"]",LogLevel.Warning);return false;}GameLogger.Log("BATTLE",user.ID+" use ["+requiredPoint+"] points for action "+action.ID,LogLevel.Debug);user.Attributes.Point.Value-=requiredPoint;return true;}}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using System.Linq;using Cthangover.Core.Games;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> Pluggable battle-core registry. The kernel hands every mod's IBattleCore implementations to <see cref="BattleCoreConsumer"/>, which registers them by ID (each core self-identifies) and removes them again when their mod unloads; one core is activated by ID. GetActive constructs a fresh instance every call — battle cores are stateless between battles. Falls back to the first registered core if no active ID was set, enabling mods to ship drop-in battle engines. </summary>
public class BattleCoreRegistry{/// <summary>Game collection setting naming the battle core of that game.</summary>
public const string GameSettingKey="battle.core";/// <summary>Singleton registry instance.</summary>
public static readonly BattleCoreRegistry Instance=new();private readonly Dictionary<string,Type>_cores=new();private string _activeCoreId;/// <summary> Registers a core by its self-reported <see cref="IBattleCore.Id"/>; a later core with the same id replaces the earlier one. Fed by <see cref="BattleCoreConsumer"/> for every mod assembly. </summary>
public void Register(IBattleCore core){if(core==null)return;_cores[core.Id]=core.GetType();GameLogger.Log("BATTLE",$"BattleCoreRegistry: registered core '{core.Id}'");}/// <summary> Removes a core whose mod is being unloaded (only when the id still maps to that core's type); an active selection of it is dropped. </summary>
public void Unregister(IBattleCore core){if(core==null|| !_cores.TryGetValue(core.Id,out var type)||type!=core.GetType())return;_cores.Remove(core.Id);if(_activeCoreId==core.Id)_activeCoreId=null;}/// <summary> Selects the active core by ID. Throws if the core is not registered. The selected core will be instantiated fresh on the next call to <see cref="GetActive"/>. </summary>
public void SetActive(string id){if(!_cores.ContainsKey(id))throw new Exception($"Battle core '{id}' not found");_activeCoreId=id;}/// <summary> Constructs a fresh instance of the active core type. Without an explicit <c>battle.set_core</c> the active game's <c>settings["battle.core"]</c> decides, then the first registered core. Throws if no cores are registered at all. </summary>
public IBattleCore GetActive(){if(_activeCoreId!=null&&_cores.ContainsKey(_activeCoreId))return(IBattleCore)Activator.CreateInstance(_cores[_activeCoreId]);var gameCore=ActiveGame.GetSetting(GameSettingKey);if(gameCore!=null&&_cores.ContainsKey(gameCore)){_activeCoreId=gameCore;return(IBattleCore)Activator.CreateInstance(_cores[gameCore]);}var firstId=GetFirstCoreId();if(firstId!=null){_activeCoreId=firstId;return(IBattleCore)Activator.CreateInstance(_cores[firstId]);}throw new Exception("No active battle core set. Use battle.set_core first.");}/// <summary> Returns the ID of the first registered core, or null if the registry is empty. Used as a fallback when no active core has been explicitly set. </summary>
public string GetFirstCoreId(){return _cores.Keys.FirstOrDefault();}/// <summary> Checks whether a core with the given <paramref name="id"/> has been registered. </summary>
public bool HasCore(string id){return _cores.ContainsKey(id);}/// <summary> Registered core IDs, sorted for stable output. Used by the battle coverage tool as the single source of truth for how many battle cores ship with the current mod set. </summary>
public IReadOnlyList<string>CoreIds{get{var ids=new List<string>(_cores.Keys);ids.Sort(System.StringComparer.Ordinal);return ids;}}/// <summary> Returns the registered <see cref="Type"/> for a core, or <c>null</c>. Lets tooling inspect a core's implemented interfaces (e.g. <see cref="IBattleAutoPlayable"/>) without instantiating it. </summary>
public Type GetCoreType(string id){return _cores.TryGetValue(id,out var type)?type:null;}}}

The private constructor forces creation through the factories so that all required data is supplied upfront. </summary>
public class BattleData{/// <summary>The quest that triggered this battle; may be <c>null</c> for non-quest skirmishes.</summary>
public QuestBase Quest{get;set;}/// <summary>Auxiliary tag set on new characters acquired via recruitment after this battle.</summary>
public string NewTag{get;set;}/// <summary>List of enemy <see cref="Character"/> instances spawned from the provided IDs or default templates.</summary>
public List<Character>EnemiesCards{get;private set;}/// <summary>Battle background texture (full-resolution).</summary>
public Texture2D Background{get;private set;}/// <summary>Depth map texture for the parallax post-process effect.</summary>
public Texture2D DepthMap{get;set;}/// <summary>Albedo/colour map texture for the parallax post-process effect.</summary>
public Texture2D AlbedoMap{get;set;}/// <summary>Which side of the screen the player's cards are drawn on.</summary>
public BattleSide BattleSide{get;private set;}=BattleSide.Player;/// <summary>Identifier for the active battle core logic module.</summary>
public string ActiveBattleCore{get;set;}/// <summary>Scene name to transition to when the battle finishes or is fled. Stored as a string to avoid type coupling.</summary>
public string ReturnScene{get;private set;}private BattleData(){}/// <summary> Convenience overload that defaults <see cref="BattleSide"/> to <c>BattleSide.Player</c>. Constructs enemies from their string IDs via <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls.CharacterFactory"/>, falling back to a level-1 template when the ID is unknown. </summary>
public static BattleData InitBattle(Texture2D background,string returnScene,params string[]enemies){return InitBattle(background,returnScene,BattleSide.Player,enemies);}/// <summary> Creates a battle with a specified <see cref="BattleSide"/> and enemy IDs. Each ID is resolved through <see cref="Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls.CharacterFactory.Get"/>. Unknown IDs produce a fallback <see cref="Character"/> with 20 HP and 3 action points. </summary>
public static BattleData InitBattle(Texture2D background,string returnScene,BattleSide cardOrder=BattleSide.Player,params string[]enemies){var list=enemies.Select(o=>CharacterFactory.Instance.Get(o)??new Character{ID=o,Attributes=new CharacterAttributes{Health=new Attribute{Value=20,BaseValue=20},Point=new Attribute{Value=3,BaseValue=3},},Level=1,Exp=10,}).ToList();return InitBattle(background,returnScene,list,cardOrder);}/// <summary> Core factory that directly accepts a pre-built <see cref="List{Character}"/> for the enemy roster. This is the overload that all other <c>InitBattle</c> variants delegate to. </summary>
public static BattleData InitBattle(Texture2D background,string returnScene,List<Character>enemiesCards,BattleSide cardOrder=BattleSide.Player){return new BattleData{Background=background,ReturnScene=returnScene,EnemiesCards=enemiesCards,BattleSide=cardOrder,};}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Characters;using Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls;using Cthangover.Core.Items;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> Converts battle data to and from plain Godot collections so GDScript mods can work with it. The previous bridge exposed <c>[GlobalClass]</c> DTOs (GDCharacter, GDBattleResult, GDWingroundContext), but classes compiled at runtime inside mods never go through Godot's C# source generator, so their properties and methods are invisible to GDScript. Dictionaries and arrays are native variants and work regardless of which assembly produced them. <para/> Keys are snake_case to match GDScript conventions. The same helpers are used by <see cref="GDBattleActionExecutor"/> (action/character snapshots in, result deltas out) and <see cref="GDWingroundListener"/> (victory context in, exp/loot mutations out). </summary>
public static class BattleGDScriptBridge{/// <summary>Flattens a character into a dictionary of primitive stats and identity fields.</summary>
public static Godot.Collections.Dictionary CharacterToDictionary(Character character){var data=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary();if(character==null)return data;data["id"]=character.ID;data["name"]=character.Name;data["level"]=character.Level;data["exp"]=character.Exp;data["recruitment_chance"]=character.RecruitmentChance;var attrs=character.Attributes;if(attrs!=null){data["health_value"]=attrs.Health?.Value??0;data["health_max"]=attrs.Health?.BaseValue??0;data["defence_value"]=attrs.Defence?.Value??0;data["defence_max"]=attrs.Defence?.BaseValue??0;data["attack_value"]=attrs.Attack?.Value??0;data["attack_max"]=attrs.Attack?.BaseValue??0;data["point_value"]=attrs.Point?.Value??0;data["point_max"]=attrs.Point?.BaseValue??0;var properties=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary<string,string>();if(attrs.Properties?.Values!=null){foreach(var kvp in attrs.Properties.Values)properties[kvp.Key]=kvp.Value;}data["properties"]=properties;}return data;}/// <summary>Flattens an action card into a dictionary of identity fields and raw properties.</summary>
public static Godot.Collections.Dictionary ActionToDictionary(ActionCharacter action){var data=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary();if(action==null)return data;data["id"]=action.ID;data["name"]=action.Name;data["description"]=action.Description;data["type"]=(int)action.Type;var properties=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary<string,string>();if(action.Properties?.Values!=null){foreach(var kvp in action.Properties.Values)properties[kvp.Key]=kvp.Value;}data["properties"]=properties;return data;}/// <summary> Builds <see cref="ChangedAttributes"/> from the dictionary a GDScript executor returns. Missing keys default to zero/false; <c>result</c> defaults to <c>true</c> so a script that only reports deltas still counts as a successful action. </summary>
public static ChangedAttributes ResultFromDictionary(Godot.Collections.Dictionary data){if(data==null)return new ChangedAttributes{Result=false};var result=new ChangedAttributes();if(data.TryGetValue("source_damage",out var sourceDamage))result.Source.Damage=sourceDamage.AsInt32();if(data.TryGetValue("source_defence",out var sourceDefence))result.Source.Defence=sourceDefence.AsInt32();if(data.TryGetValue("target_damage",out var targetDamage))result.Target.Damage=targetDamage.AsInt32();if(data.TryGetValue("target_defence",out var targetDefence))result.Target.Defence=targetDefence.AsInt32();result.Result= !data.TryGetValue("result",out var success)||success.AsBool();return result;}/// <summary>Builds the mutable victory context dictionary passed to GDScript winground hooks.</summary>
public static Godot.Collections.Dictionary WingroundToDictionary(WingroundContext ctx){var data=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary();if(ctx==null)return data;var expGained=new Godot.Collections.Dictionary<string,int>();if(ctx.PlayerExpGained!=null){foreach(var kvp in ctx.PlayerExpGained)expGained[kvp.Key]=kvp.Value;}data["exp_gained"]=expGained;var defeated=new Godot.Collections.Array<Godot.Collections.Dictionary>();if(ctx.DefeatedEnemies!=null){foreach(var enemy in ctx.DefeatedEnemies)defeated.Add(CharacterToDictionary(enemy));}data["defeated_enemies"]=defeated;var loot=new Godot.Collections.Array<Godot.Collections.Dictionary>();if(ctx.GeneratedLoot!=null){foreach(var item in ctx.GeneratedLoot){loot.Add(new Godot.Collections.Dictionary{["item_id"]=item.Item?.ID??string.Empty,["count"]=item.Count,});}}data["generated_loot"]=loot;data["return_scene"]=ctx.BattleData?.ReturnScene??string.Empty;return data;}/// <summary> Writes GDScript mutations from a winground context dictionary back to the C# pipeline. Only <c>exp_gained</c> and <c>generated_loot</c> are synced — defeated enemies are read-only snapshots, matching the documented contract of <see cref="IWingroundListener"/>. </summary>
public static void SyncWingroundBack(Godot.Collections.Dictionary data,WingroundContext ctx){if(data==null||ctx==null)return;if(data.TryGetValue("exp_gained",out var expVariant)&&expVariant.AsGodotDictionary()is Godot.Collections.Dictionary expDict&&ctx.PlayerExpGained!=null){ctx.PlayerExpGained.Clear();foreach(var key in expDict.Keys)ctx.PlayerExpGained[key.AsString()]=expDict[key].AsInt32();}if(data.TryGetValue("generated_loot",out var lootVariant)&&lootVariant.AsGodotArray()is Godot.Collections.Array lootArray&&ctx.GeneratedLoot!=null){ctx.GeneratedLoot.Clear();foreach(var entry in lootArray){if(entry.AsGodotDictionary()is not Godot.Collections.Dictionary itemDict)continue;var itemId=itemDict.TryGetValue("item_id",out var idVariant)?idVariant.AsString():null;var count=itemDict.TryGetValue("count",out var countVariant)?countVariant.AsInt32():0;ctx.GeneratedLoot.Add(new ItemContainer{Item=string.IsNullOrEmpty(itemId)?null:ItemFactory.Instance.Get(itemId),Count=count,});}}}}}

using Cthangover.Core.Actions;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> Dispatched by the scenario DSL to initiate battle. Reads "scene", "enemies", "quest_id" and "new_tag" from dialog variables and calls <see cref="BattleService.Init"/>. The enemies string is a comma-separated list embedded in the scenario script. Battle initialization must happen *after* the background has been set by a prior background action, otherwise the encounter gets a null backdrop. <para/> Registered by the battle mod's assembly scan, so the core scenario action registry stays free of battle commands. </summary>
public class BattleInitAction:IScenarioAction{/// <summary>Registered as "battle.init" — the scenario DSL's primary battle initiation command.</summary>
public string Name=>"battle.init";/// <summary> Reads battle parameters from dialog variables and initiates battle construction. Requires both "scene" and "enemies" to be non-empty — returns early with a log if either is missing. </summary>
public void Run(IActionContext ctx){var sceneRaw=ctx.GetParam("scene");var enemies=ctx.GetParam("enemies");var questId=ctx.GetParam("quest_id");var newTag=ctx.GetParam("new_tag");if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(sceneRaw)||string.IsNullOrEmpty(enemies)){ctx.Log("EVENT","BattleInitAction: missing 'scene' or 'enemies' variable");return;}BattleService.Init(sceneRaw,enemies,questId,newTag);ctx.Log("EVENT",$"BattleInitAction: battle started at '{sceneRaw}' with enemies '{enemies}'");}}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Battle;using Cthangover.Core.Settings;using Cthangover.Core.UI.Theming;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.TurnBattle{/// <summary> In-battle speed toggle bar (x1/x4/x8). Anchors are used instead of a viewport-size lookup because the viewport is unavailable before the node enters the tree. </summary>
public BattleSpeedControl(){CthangoverTheme.Apply(this);var speeds=new[]{1,4,8};var hbox=new HBoxContainer{Name="SpeedButtons"};hbox.Alignment=BoxContainer.AlignmentMode.Begin;foreach(var speed in speeds){var btn=new Button{Text=$"x{speed}",CustomMinimumSize=new Vector2(48,32)};btn.Pressed+=()=>OnSpeedSelected(speed);hbox.AddChild(btn);_buttons[speed]=btn;}AddChild(hbox);AnchorLeft=1f;AnchorRight=1f;AnchorTop=0f;AnchorBottom=0f;OffsetLeft= -200f;OffsetRight= -20f;OffsetTop=20f;OffsetBottom=52f;ApplySavedSpeed();}/// <summary> Restores the speed from <see cref="GameData.Settings.BattleSpeed"/>. Called on <c>_Ready</c> to reapply the saved preference. </summary>
public void ApplySavedSpeed(){var speed=GameData.Instance.Settings.BattleSpeed;if(speed<1||speed>8)speed=1;_activeSpeed=speed;Godot.Engine.TimeScale=speed;UpdateHighlight();}/// <summary> Resets <see cref="Godot.Engine.TimeScale"/> to 1.0x without persisting to settings. using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> GDScript bridge for <see cref="IWingroundListener"/>. Holds a reference to a GDScript object and delegates each hook through <see cref="GodotObject.HasMethod"/> / <see cref="GodotObject.Call"/>. <para/> All three hooks are optional — the GDScript mod implements only the methods it needs. The context is marshalled into a plain Godot dictionary (<c>exp_gained</c>, <c>defeated_enemies</c>, <c>generated_loot</c>, <c>return_scene</c>) before each call and synced back afterward, so GDScript mutations to exp and loot propagate to the C# victory pipeline. Dictionaries replace the old GDWingroundContext RefCounted DTO because mod classes compiled at runtime are not visible to GDScript. </summary>
public class GDWingroundListener:IWingroundListener{private readonly GodotObject _instance;/// <summary>Registry key reported by the script's <c>get_winground_listener_id()</c>; deduplicates on rescan.</summary>
public string Id{get;}/// <summary> Creates a bridge around a live GDScript object. The caller must ensure the object outlives the registry. </summary>
public GDWingroundListener(string id,GodotObject instance){Id=id;_instance=instance;}/// <summary>Calls the script's <c>on_winground_before_exp(ctx)</c> if implemented; no-op otherwise.</summary>
public void OnBeforeExpAward(WingroundContext ctx){if(!_instance.HasMethod("on_winground_before_exp"))return;var gdCtx=BattleGDScriptBridge.WingroundToDictionary(ctx);_instance.Call("on_winground_before_exp",gdCtx);BattleGDScriptBridge.SyncWingroundBack(gdCtx,ctx);}/// <summary>Calls the script's <c>on_winground_after_loot(ctx)</c> if implemented; no-op otherwise.</summary>
public void OnAfterLootGenerated(WingroundContext ctx){if(!_instance.HasMethod("on_winground_after_loot"))return;var gdCtx=BattleGDScriptBridge.WingroundToDictionary(ctx);_instance.Call("on_winground_after_loot",gdCtx);BattleGDScriptBridge.SyncWingroundBack(gdCtx,ctx);}/// <summary>Calls the script's <c>on_winground_before_show(ctx)</c> if implemented; no-op otherwise.</summary>
public void OnBeforeShow(WingroundContext ctx){if(!_instance.HasMethod("on_winground_before_show"))return;var gdCtx=BattleGDScriptBridge.WingroundToDictionary(ctx);_instance.Call("on_winground_before_show",gdCtx);BattleGDScriptBridge.SyncWingroundBack(gdCtx,ctx);}}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> Optional automation contract for battle cores. The base <see cref="IBattleCore"/> contract describes how a battle starts but not how it advances: every core owns its own UI and waits for player input in its own way. Integration tests and AI tooling therefore ask the core itself when it waits for the player and how to advance the turn, instead of hunting for core-specific buttons by node path. Cores that don't implement this interface are still runnable but are reported as not universally testable by the battle coverage tool. </summary>
public interface IBattleAutoPlayable{/// <summary> <c>true</c> while the core accepts a player turn advance. Must become <c>false</c> immediately when the turn ends, so a polling driver cannot trigger two turns in a row. </summary>
bool IsWaitingForPlayerInput{get;}/// <summary> Ends the current player turn through the same path the core's UI uses (skipping the player's actions is a valid strategy for smoke tests). Must be a no-op when <see cref="IsWaitingForPlayerInput"/> is <c>false</c>. </summary>
void AdvancePlayerTurn();}}

namespace Cthangover.Core.Battle{/// <summary> Extension point for mods to inspect and mutate victory-screen data. Implementations are auto-discovered via <see cref="WingroundListenerRegistry.RegisterAssembly"/> (C#) or detected by method signature in <see cref="Mods.ModGDScriptLoader"/> (GDScript). The three hooks fire in order during <see cref="WingroundBehaviour.Show"/>: <list type="number"> <item><see cref="OnBeforeExpAward"/> — EXP data is available but has not yet been applied to characters.</item> <item><see cref="OnAfterLootGenerated"/> — loot has been rolled from enemies but has not yet been added to inventory.</item> <item><see cref="OnBeforeShow"/> — all processing is done; final chance to mutate data before the UI appears.</item> </list> The same <see cref="WingroundContext"/> instance is passed to all listeners across all three phases, so mutations from earlier hooks are visible to later hooks and to subsequent listeners. </summary>
public interface IWingroundListener{/// <summary> Unique identifier for this listener. Used in logs and for cross-mod dependency ordering. Convention: <c>"mod_id.listener_name"</c>. </summary>
string Id{get;}/// <summary> Called before EXP is awarded to surviving characters. <see cref="WingroundContext.PlayerExpGained"/> and <see cref="WingroundContext.DefeatedEnemies"/> are populated; <see cref="WingroundContext.GeneratedLoot"/> is empty at this stage. </summary>
void OnBeforeExpAward(WingroundContext ctx);/// <summary> Called after loot has been generated from <see cref="WingroundContext.DefeatedEnemies"/> but before the items are added to the player's inventory. <see cref="WingroundContext.GeneratedLoot"/> is populated and mutable — adding, removing, or modifying entries here directly affects the inventory outcome. </summary>
void OnAfterLootGenerated(WingroundContext ctx);/// <summary> Called after EXP, loot, inventory, and recruitment have all been processed, immediately before the victory UI is shown (<c>base.Show()</c>). Use for post-processing or cleanup that must happen before the player sees the screen. </summary>
void OnBeforeShow(WingroundContext ctx);}}

using Cthangover.Core.Characters;namespace Cthangover.Core.Cards.StatusEffect{/// <summary> Behaviour hooks for a status effect type. Each hook receives the owning character so a single IStatusActions instance can be shared across multiple characters. OnDealDamage / OnTakeDamage use ref int to let effects amplify or reduce damage before it is applied. ModifyAttributes is a passive stat modifier called independently of turn phases. OnFinalAction fires once when the effect expires. All hooks have empty default semantics — effects override only the hooks they care about. </summary>
public interface IStatusActions{/// <summary>Factory key matching the <c>Actions</c> field in <see cref="StatusEffectInfo"/>, e.g. <c>"basic/stun"</c>.</summary>
string ID{get;}/// <summary>Fires when the owning character's turn begins. Use for start-of-turn damage-over-time or regeneration effects.</summary>
void OnTurnStart(Character target);/// <summary>Fires when the owning character's turn ends. Mirrors <see cref="OnTurnStart"/> for symmetry; useful for effects that activate after the character acts.</summary>
void OnTurnEnd(Character target);/// <summary>Called before the owning character deals damage to <paramref name="target"/>. Modify <paramref name="damage"/> via <see langword="ref"/> to amplify or reduce outgoing damage — all active effects stack multiplicatively through the queue's iteration.</summary>
void OnDealDamage(Character source,Character target,ref int damage);/// <summary>Called before the owning character receives damage from <paramref name="source"/>. Modify <paramref name="damage"/> via <see langword="ref"/> to add damage reduction or vulnerability. Fires after <see cref="OnDealDamage"/> in the damage pipeline.</summary>
void OnTakeDamage(Character target,Character source,ref int damage);/// <summary>Fires immediately when the effect is first placed on a character. Use for one-shot stat boosts, visual feedback, or initialisation logic.</summary>
void OnApply(Character target);/// <summary>Fires when the effect is manually removed (e.g. via a cleanse card). Not called on natural expiration — use <see cref="OnFinalAction"/> for that path.</summary>
void OnRemove(Character target);/// <summary>Fires once when the effect expires naturally (timer reaches zero). Use for end-of-effect triggers like explosion damage or stat restoration. Not called on manual removal.</summary>
void OnFinalAction(Character target);/// <summary>Passive stat modifier invoked independently of turn phases. Receives a reference to the character's attribute container; implementors can add flat or percentage bonuses that other effects may also contribute to.</summary>
void ModifyAttributes(CharacterAttributes attributes);}}

using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Cards.StatusEffect{/// <summary> Status effect data contract. Separates identity (ID, Name, Icon) from mutable state (Duration, RemainingTurns) and behaviour (Actions — an IStatusActions hook set). Copy() is required so the StatusEffectQueue can clone effects when characters are duplicated. </summary>
public interface IStatusEffect{/// <summary>Unique mod identifier, e.g. <c>"basic/stun"</c>. Used by factories and the queue to look up and remove effects by key.</summary>
string ID{get;}/// <summary>Display name shown in the battle UI.</summary>
string Name{get;}/// <summary>Flavour text explaining the effect to the player.</summary>
string Description{get;}/// <summary>High-level category (<c>Buff</c>, <c>Debuff</c>, <c>Stun</c>) used for UI tinting and quick type checks like <see cref="StatusEffectQueue.HasStun"/>.</summary>
StatusEffectType EffectType{get;}/// <summary>Base duration in turns. Set during effect creation; may be overridden by the caller via <see cref="StatusEffectQueue.Add"/>. A value of 0 or negative means the effect never expires naturally.</summary>
int Duration{get;set;}/// <summary>Turns remaining before the effect expires. Decremented each turn boundary by the queue. Independent of <c>Duration</c> so that the original value is preserved for display or re-apply logic.</summary>
int RemainingTurns{get;set;}/// <summary>Icon texture loaded from the <c>"characters"</c> mod group, displayed beside the effect name in the HUD.</summary>
Texture2D Icon{get;}/// <summary>Behaviour hooks that fire during turn phases and on damage events. Resolved by <c>StatusEffectActionFactory</c> from the <see cref="StatusEffectInfo.Actions"/> string ID.</summary>
IStatusActions Actions{get;}/// <summary>Creates a shallow clone. <c>Actions</c> is a shared reference (stateless singleton) so it is not deep-copied. Used by <see cref="StatusEffectQueue.Copy"/> when duplicating a character.</summary>
IStatusEffect Copy();}}

using System.Collections.Generic;using System.Linq;using Cthangover.Core.Characters;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;using Godot;namespace Cthangover.Core.Cards.StatusEffect{/// <summary> Per-character status-effect pipeline. Manages a list of active effects, advancing their timers on turn boundaries and removing expired ones after firing OnFinalAction. Add resolves the effect info via the factory and calls OnApply immediately. OnTurnStart iterates backwards to safely remove expired effects during traversal. OnDealDamage / OnTakeDamage pipe through every active effect via ref parameters, enabling multiplicative stacking. ActiveStatusEffects returns a defensive copy so external code cannot mutate the internal list. Copy creates a deep clone for character duplication, re-firing OnApply on the new owner. </summary>
public class StatusEffectQueue{private readonly List<IStatusEffect>activeStatusEffectData;private readonly Character owner;/// <summary>Defensive copy of the internal effect list. Returns a new <c>List</c> each access so external code cannot mutate the queue's backing store. Safe for enumeration.</summary>
public List<IStatusEffect>ActiveStatusEffects=>activeStatusEffectData.ToList();/// <summary>Initialises an empty queue bound to <paramref name="owner"/>. The owner reference is used by all action-hook calls to pass the affected character.</summary> <param name="owner">The character who carries these effects.</param>
public StatusEffectQueue(Character owner){this.activeStatusEffectData=new List<IStatusEffect>();this.owner=owner;}/// <summary>Checks whether any active effect has <see cref="StatusEffectType.Stun"/>. Called by the battle engine to determine if the owner should skip their turn.</summary> <returns><see langword="true"/> if at least one Stun-type effect is active.</returns>
public bool HasStun(){foreach(var statusEffect in activeStatusEffectData)if(statusEffect.EffectType==StatusEffectType.Stun)return true;return false;}/// <summary>Looks up <paramref name="statusEffectId"/> in the factory, constructs a <see cref="StatusEffectItem"/>, optionally overrides its duration, fires <c>OnApply</c>, and appends it to the active list.</summary> <param name="statusEffectId">Factory key matching a <see cref="StatusEffectInfo"/> entry.</param> <param name="duration">If positive, overwrites the default duration from the effect definition.</param> <returns><see langword="false"/> if the factory lookup fails (key not found); otherwise <see langword="true"/>.</returns>
public bool Add(string statusEffectId,int duration= -1){var statusEffectInfo=Factories.Impls.StatusEffectInfoFactory.Instance.Get(statusEffectId);if(statusEffectInfo==null){GameLogger.Log("STATUS",$"statusEffect with ID '{statusEffectId}' not found!",LogLevel.Error);return false;}var statusEffect=new StatusEffectItem(statusEffectInfo);if(duration>0){statusEffect.Duration=duration;statusEffect.RemainingTurns=duration;}statusEffect.Actions?.OnApply(owner);activeStatusEffectData.Add(statusEffect);return true;}/// <summary>Removes the first effect matching <paramref name="statusEffectId"/> from the active list. Fires <c>OnRemove</c> so the effect can clean up before disappearing (e.g. revert stat modifications).</summary> <param name="statusEffectId">Factory key of the effect to remove.</param> <returns><see langword="false"/> if no matching effect was found; otherwise <see langword="true"/>.</returns>
public bool Remove(string statusEffectId){var statusEffect=activeStatusEffectData.FirstOrDefault(b=>b.ID==statusEffectId);if(statusEffect==null)return false;statusEffect.Actions?.OnRemove(owner);activeStatusEffectData.Remove(statusEffect);return true;}/// <summary>Advances all active effects at the start of the owner's turn. Fires <c>OnTurnStart</c> on each effect, decrements <see cref="IStatusEffect.RemainingTurns"/> for timed effects, and removes expired ones after firing <c>OnFinalAction</c>. Iterates backwards so removals do not corrupt the index.</summary>
public void OnTurnStart(){for(int i=activeStatusEffectData.Count-1;i>=0;i--){var statusEffect=activeStatusEffectData[i];statusEffect.Actions?.OnTurnStart(owner);if(statusEffect.RemainingTurns>0&&statusEffect.Duration>0){statusEffect.RemainingTurns--;if(statusEffect.RemainingTurns<=0){statusEffect.Actions?.OnFinalAction(owner);activeStatusEffectData.RemoveAt(i);}}}}/// <summary>Fires end-of-turn hooks on all active effects. Operates on a defensive copy so that <c>OnTurnEnd</c> callbacks that add or remove effects do not invalidate the enumerator. Durations count down in <see cref="OnTurnStart"/> only.</summary>
public void OnTurnEnd(){// Only the hook: the countdown belongs to OnTurnStart, a second one here halved every duration and expired effects without one.
foreach(var statusEffect in ActiveStatusEffects)statusEffect.Actions?.OnTurnEnd(owner);}/// <summary>Pipes outgoing damage through every active effect's <c>OnDealDamage</c> hook, allowing each to modify <paramref name="damage"/> via <see langword="ref"/>. Effects iterate in insertion order; multiplicative stacking means order-agnostic results for flat modifiers but order-sensitive for percentage modifiers.</summary> <param name="target">The character receiving the damage.</param> <param name="damage">The damage value, modifiable by effects through the <see langword="ref"/> parameter.</param>
public void OnDealDamage(Character target,ref int damage){foreach(var statusEffect in activeStatusEffectData){statusEffect.Actions?.OnDealDamage(owner,target,ref damage);}}/// <summary>Pipes incoming damage through every active effect's <c>OnTakeDamage</c> hook. Called after <see cref="OnDealDamage"/> in the damage pipeline, so defensive modifiers stack on top of the attacker's amplified value.</summary> <param name="source">The character dealing the damage.</param> <param name="damage">The damage value, modifiable by effects through the <see langword="ref"/> parameter.</param>
public void OnTakeDamage(Character source,ref int damage){foreach(var statusEffect in activeStatusEffectData){statusEffect.Actions?.OnTakeDamage(owner,source,ref damage);}}/// <summary>Removes all active effects, firing <c>OnRemove</c> on each before clearing the list. Used when a character dies or an encounter ends so effects do not leak between battles.</summary>
public void ClearAll(){foreach(var statusEffect in activeStatusEffectData){statusEffect.Actions?.OnRemove(owner);}activeStatusEffectData.Clear();}/// <summary>Deep-clones the entire queue for a new character owner. Each effect is copied via <see cref="IStatusEffect.Copy"/>, and <c>OnApply</c> is re-fired on <paramref name="newOwner"/> so initialisation hooks run in the target's context. Used when a character is duplicated mid-encounter (e.g. a summon or mirror effect).</summary> <param name="newOwner">The character who will own the clone.</param> <returns>A new <see cref="StatusEffectQueue"/> bound to <paramref name="newOwner"/> with copies of all active effects.</returns>
public StatusEffectQueue Copy(Character newOwner){var newSystem=new StatusEffectQueue(newOwner);foreach(var statusEffect in activeStatusEffectData){var copiedstatusEffect=statusEffect.Copy();copiedstatusEffect.Actions?.OnApply(newOwner);newSystem.activeStatusEffectData.Add(copiedstatusEffect);}return newSystem;}}}

using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;using Cthangover.Core.Characters;namespace Cthangover.Core.Cards.StatusEffect{/// <summary> Side-table that owns the <see cref="StatusEffectQueue"/> of every character participating in battle. The queue used to live on <see cref="Character"/> itself, but the core character model must stay free of battle subsystems — so the battle mod keeps queues keyed by character instance instead. <para/> Uses <see cref="ConditionalWeakTable{TKey, TValue}"/>: queues die together with their character, which matters because each battle constructs fresh copies via <see cref="Character.Copy"/> and discards them afterwards. All access happens on the main thread during battle, so no extra locking is needed beyond what the weak table provides. </summary>
public static class StatusEffectService{private static readonly ConditionalWeakTable<Character,StatusEffectQueue>queues=new();/// <summary> Returns the queue of <paramref name="character"/>, creating an empty one on first access. Returns <c>null</c> for a null character so call sites can keep their existing null-conditional patterns. </summary>
public static StatusEffectQueue Of(Character character){if(character==null)return null;return queues.GetValue(character,CreateQueue);}private static StatusEffectQueue CreateQueue(Character owner){return new StatusEffectQueue(owner);}}}

using System;using System.Collections.Generic;using Cthangover.Core.Cards.StatusEffect;using Cthangover.Core.Utils;namespace Cthangover.Core.Factories.Impls{/// <summary> Reflection-based plugin registry for status effect behaviour classes, mirroring the pattern used by <c>ItemActionFactory</c>. Each <c>IStatusActions</c> implementation corresponds to a status effect ID referenced in battle data JSON. The kernel hands every mod's implementations to <see cref="StatusActionsConsumer"/>, so mod authors add new status effects (e.g. poison, burn, freeze) by implementing the interface in their assembly; they leave again when their mod unloads. </summary>
public class StatusEffectActionFactory{private readonly Dictionary<string,IStatusActions>actions;
#region Singleton
private static readonly Lazy<StatusEffectActionFactory>instance=new(()=>new StatusEffectActionFactory());/// <summary>Lazy singleton, filled by <see cref="StatusActionsConsumer"/>.</summary>
public static StatusEffectActionFactory Instance=>instance.Value;public StatusEffectActionFactory(){actions=new Dictionary<string,IStatusActions>();}
#endregion
/// <summary>Registers a behaviour set under its <c>ID</c>; the first registration of an id wins.</summary>
public void Register(IStatusActions action){if(action!=null&& !string.IsNullOrEmpty(action.ID)&& !actions.ContainsKey(action.ID))actions[action.ID]=action;}/// <summary>Removes exactly <paramref name="action"/> (its mod is being unloaded).</summary>
public void Unregister(IStatusActions action){if(action!=null&& !string.IsNullOrEmpty(action.ID)&&actions.TryGetValue(action.ID,out var current)&&ReferenceEquals(current,action))actions.Remove(action.ID);}/// <summary>Resolves the behaviour set registered under the effect's <c>Actions</c> id; unknown ids are logged and return <c>null</c>.</summary>
public IStatusActions Get(string id){if(actions.TryGetValue(id,out var result))return result;GameLogger.Log("STATUS","actions '"+id+"' not found!",LogLevel.Error);return null;}}}
